Anna was very happy. It was her birthday and she had many presents. She opened them one by one. She got a doll, a book, a hat and a ball. She thanked her mom and dad and her friends.

But there was one present left. It was from her cousin Ben. She opened it and saw a wooden horse. It was ugly. It had no mane, no tail, no eyes, no mouth. It was just a block of wood with four sticks. Anna did not like it. She said, "This is a bad present. I don't want it. It is ugly."

Ben was sad. He had made the wooden horse himself. He had no money to buy a present. He had worked hard to carve the wood and paint it. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I tried to make you a nice present. It is not ugly. It is special. It can balance on its legs. Look." He showed her how the horse could stand on two legs or even one leg without falling. He said, "It is a magic horse. You can make it do tricks. You can pretend it is a circus horse or a racing horse or a flying horse. It is fun."

Anna looked at the horse again. She saw that it was not ugly. It was different. It was special. It could balance on its legs. It was a magic horse. She felt sorry for being mean to Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. It is a good present. It is special. It can balance on its legs. It is a magic horse. Thank you, Ben. You are a good cousin. Can you show me how to make it do tricks?"

Ben smiled. He was happy. He said, "Sure, Anna. I can show you. Come, let's play with the magic horse." He took her hand and they went to play with the horse. They had fun. They pretended it was a circus horse or a racing horse or a flying horse. They laughed and hugged.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge a present by its looks. It may have a hidden value. Be grateful for what you have. Be kind to others.

But then Emily heard a voice. "Don't be scared," the voice said. Emily stopped and looked around but she couldn't see anyone. 

The voice spoke again. "I'm a spirit. I used to live in this forest, but I died a long time ago". Emily felt scared, and she slowly began to move away. 

The spirit voice said again, "It's ok, don't be afraid. You can go now". 

That night, Emily told her mom about her experience in the forest. As she was telling her story, she slowly came to understand that the forest was a special place, full of life and beauty, even if it looked dead and black on the outside.

"Don't worry," said Billy. "I'll help you find your doll." And so, Billy went deep into the woods with the little girl. They looked and looked, but they couldn't find the doll.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. "What's that?" asked the little girl. "I don't know," said Billy. "Let's go see." As they got closer, they saw that a group of birds were disturbing a nest. "We have to help them," said Billy. And so, they scared away the birds and saved the nest. The little girl was so happy that she gave Billy a big hug. "Thank you, Billy," she said. "You're my hero."

The day of the race arrived, and the rabbit was very nervous. He knew he couldn't win with his leaky bottle. Suddenly, the fox and the bear appeared with a new water bottle for the rabbit. "We saw you struggling and we wanted to help," they said. The rabbit was so grateful and happy that he cried.

In the end, the rabbit won the race. But he knew he couldn't have done it without the help of his friends. The moral of the story is that it's always better to ask for help when you need it. And sometimes, helping others can make you a winner too.

Later that day, Timmy and his dad played with the car outside. Timmy wanted to make the car go backwards, so his dad showed him how to reverse it. Timmy thought it was so cool and had so much fun playing with his reliable car.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy wanted to get a haircut, so his mom took him to the barber. The barber was a nice man with scissors and combs. Timmy didn't know the barber, but he wasn't scared. 

The barber asked Timmy how he wanted his hair to look. Timmy didn't know what to say, so he just said "short". The barber started cutting Timmy's hair and soon it was all done. Timmy looked in the mirror and smiled. He liked his new haircut! 

From that day on, Timmy knew that the barber was a good person who could make him look nice. And whenever Timmy needed a haircut, he would go back to the small barber shop and see his friend again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park to play with her friends. One day, her mommy and daddy told her that they were going to a big festival in the city. Lily was so excited! She loved festivals because there were lots of fun things to do and yummy food to eat.

But then, Lily's mommy and daddy got upset because they couldn't find their car keys. They looked everywhere, but they were nowhere to be found. Lily was sad because she didn't want to miss the festival. But her mommy and daddy told her not to worry, they trusted that they would find the keys soon.

Finally, after searching for a long time, they found the keys under the couch. They all got into the car and drove to the festival. Lily had so much fun playing games and eating cotton candy. She was happy that she could trust her mommy and daddy to find the keys and take her to the festival. The end.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Lily has a doll and Ben has a laser. Ben likes to make the laser shine on the wall and make noises. Lily likes to dress up her doll and talk to her.

"Look, Lily, look!" Ben says. "My laser is so cool! It can make red and green and blue lights!"

Lily looks at Ben and his laser. She thinks it is noisy and boring. She likes her doll better. She says, "My doll is so pretty! She has a pink dress and a bow in her hair. She is my best friend!"

Ben does not care about Lily's doll. He thinks it is silly and quiet. He likes his laser better. He says, "My laser is my best friend! It can do anything! It can make shapes and sounds and even cut things!"

Lily and Ben do not agree. They start to argue. They say, "My toy is better than your toy!" They do not share or play nicely.

Mom hears them and comes to the living room. She sees them fighting and their toys on the floor. She is not happy. She says, "Lily and Ben, stop it! You are not being good. You are not being kind. You should not fight over your toys. You should share and play together."

Lily and Ben look at Mom and feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We were not good. We were not kind."

Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "It's okay. I love you both. You have different toys and that's fine. You can like different things and still be friends. You can also try new things and have fun. Why don't you swap your toys for a while and see what you can do?"

Lily and Ben think that is a good idea. They say, "Okay, Mom. We will swap our toys and play together."

They give each other their toys and say, "Thank you." They start to play with their new toys and discover new ways to have fun. Lily makes her doll dance with the laser lights and Ben makes his laser cut out shapes from paper. They laugh and talk and enjoy their toys. They also mention how cool and pretty their toys are. They are being good and kind. They are happy.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys. Anna had a new doll. She loved her doll very much. She did not want to share her doll with anyone.

One day, Ben came to Anna's house. He saw the doll and wanted to play with it. He asked Anna, "Can you lend me your doll for a little while? I will be careful."

Anna did not want to lend her doll, but she did not want to be rude. She said, "Okay, you can play with her for a little while. But you have to give her back soon."

Ben took the doll and ran to the garden. He played with the doll and had fun. He forgot about Anna and the time.

Anna waited and waited. She was upset. She wanted her doll back. She went to the garden and looked for Ben. She saw him sitting on a swing. He was holding the doll. But the doll was not the same. The doll had dirt on her dress, a tear on her eye, and a missing shoe. Anna was very angry. She shouted, "Ben, what did you do to my doll? You ruined her! Give her back to me!"

Ben was scared. He did not mean to hurt the doll. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was just playing. I did not know she was so fragile. Please don't be mad at me."

But Anna was mad. She snatched the doll from Ben's hands. She said, "You are a bad friend. You did not take care of my doll. You did not keep your promise. You can never play with her again. Go away!"

Ben felt sad. He wanted to say sorry again, but Anna did not listen. She ran to her house and slammed the door. Ben was left alone in the garden. He heard the silence. He knew he had lost his friend. He cried.

"That's very good, Lily and Ben," Mom says, happy. "You are being good friends and creative builders. I'm proud of you too."

But then, Sam saw a big spider on the hose. He was very scared of spiders. He dropped the hose and ran away, screaming. "Help! Help! Spider! Spider!" he shouted.

Mia heard Sam and looked at the hose. She saw the spider too. It was black and hairy and had eight legs. She was not scared of spiders. She thought they were interesting. She picked up the hose and moved it closer to the spider. She wanted to see it better.

"Sam, come back! It's just a spider. It won't hurt you. Look, it's small and cute," she said.

But Sam did not listen. He was hiding behind a tree, weeping. He did not think the spider was small or cute. He thought it was big and ugly and scary. He did not want to see it or touch it. He wanted Mia to leave it alone.

"Mia, no! Don't touch it! It will bite you! It will make you sick! Throw it away! Throw it away!" he cried.

But the ship does not wave back. It comes closer and closer. It has a big mouth and sharp teeth. It is not a ship. It is a monster!

The monster wants to eat the ships. It opens its mouth and bites the big ships and the small ships. It makes loud noises and splashes water.

Tim and Sam are scared. They run away from the shore. They hide behind a rock and hug each other. They hope the monster will go away soon. They do not want to play with ships anymore.

One day, an old man was walking with his cane in the park. He liked to see the birds and the flowers and the children playing. He felt happy and calm.

But then, he saw a big dog running towards him. The dog was barking and jumping and wagging its tail. The old man was scared. He did not like big dogs. He thought the dog might bite him or knock him down.

He tried to walk faster, but his legs were tired and sore. He held his cane tightly and looked for help. He saw a little girl sitting on a bench. She had a red hat and a blue dress. She was holding a book.

"Help me, please!" the old man shouted. "There is a big dog coming!"

The little girl looked up and saw the old man and the dog. She was not scared. She liked dogs. She knew the dog was friendly and just wanted to play.

She put down her book and stood up. She stretched her arms and waved at the dog.

"Hello, doggy!" she said. "Do you want to play with me?"

The dog heard the little girl and changed its direction. It ran towards her and licked her face. The little girl laughed and hugged the dog.

The old man was relieved. He smiled and thanked the little girl.

"You are very brave and kind," he said. "What is your name?"

"My name is Anna," the little girl said. "And this is Max. He is my friend. He likes to run and play."

The old man nodded and sat down on the bench. He invited Anna and Max to join him. He opened his bag and took out some cookies and water. He shared them with the little girl and the dog.

They ate and drank and talked and played. They became friends, too. The old man felt happy and calm again. He liked the birds and the flowers and the children and the dog. He thought it was a good day.

Lila was sad. She had a bad dream and woke up crying. She wanted her mommy and daddy, but they were not in their room. She looked for them in the living room, but they were not there either. She felt scared and alone.

She saw a bowl of oats on the table. She remembered that mommy made oats for breakfast. She liked oats. They were warm and sweet and made her feel good. She climbed on a chair and reached for the bowl. But the chair was wobbly and she lost her balance. The bowl fell on the floor and broke. The oats spilled everywhere. Lila fell too and hurt her knee. She cried louder.

She heard a noise from the couch. It was her puppy, Spot. He was adorable. He had black and white fur and a wet nose. He heard Lila crying and came to see what was wrong. He saw the mess on the floor and the blood on Lila's knee. He licked her face and wagged his tail. He wanted to comfort her.

"Spot, you are a good boy," Lila said, hugging him. "You make me feel better. I love you."

"I love you too, Lila," Spot barked. "Don't be sad. Mommy and daddy will come soon. They went to the store to buy you a surprise. They told me to watch over you. You are my best friend."

Lila smiled. She felt safe and happy with Spot. He was her best friend too. She forgot about her bad dream and her hurt knee. She cuddled with him on the couch and waited for mommy and daddy. She hoped they would bring her a toy or a book or a candy. She loved surprises. And she loved her family. And she loved her oats. And she loved her adorable puppy, Spot.

Tom and Lily liked to play near the old train tracks. They would imagine they were riding on fast trains to faraway places. Sometimes they would put coins on the rails and wait for the trains to flatten them.

One day, they saw a shiny red train coming. They wanted to get a closer look, so they ran towards the tracks. Lily was careful and stopped before the rail, but Tom was careless and ran too far. He tripped and fell on the rail.

"Tom, get up! The train is coming!" Lily shouted. She tried to pull him up, but he was too heavy. Tom was scared and cried. He could hear the train horn and see the smoke.

The train driver saw the children on the tracks and tried to stop, but it was too late. The train hit Tom and Lily with a loud crash. They were gone.

The end.

Rex wags his tail and licks their faces. He is happy to see them. He thinks they are his friends.

"Ow, Rex! You are hurting me!" Ben cries.

"Rex, get off them! You are a dangerous dog!" she shouts.

She pulls Rex away from Ben and Mia. She hugs them and checks if they are okay.

"I'm sorry, Ben and Mia. Rex didn't mean to hurt you. He just wanted to play. But he doesn't know his own strength. He is a dangerous dog for little kids. You have to be careful around him. Do you understand?" she says.

Ben and Mia nod. They are scared of Rex, but they are also sorry for him. They know he is not a bad dog. They just wish he was smaller and gentler.

"Can we still be friends with Rex?" Ben asks.

"Of course you can. But you have to stay away from him when he is excited. And you have to tell me when you want to pet him. I will hold him and make sure he doesn't jump on you. Okay?" aunt Lucy says.

Ben and Mia agree. They still love Rex, but they also respect him. They learn to play with him safely and happily.

One day, they find a big icy hill. They want to slide down the hill on their sleds. Lily has a red sled and Ben has a blue sled. They take turns to go down the hill. They have fun and laugh.

But then, Ben has an idea. He says to Lily, "Let's make a race. The first one to reach the bottom of the hill wins. Are you ready?"

Lily nods. She likes to race. She says, "OK, let's go. On your mark, get set, go!"

They push their sleds and start to slide down the hill. They go fast and faster. They feel the icy wind on their faces. They see the snowflakes in the air.

But then, something goes wrong. Ben's sled hits a bump and swerves to the side. It bumps into Lily's sled and makes it spin. Lily loses her balance and falls off her sled. She lands on the snow and feels a pain in her arm. She cries.

Ben sees what happens and stops his sled. He runs to Lily and says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to make you fall. Are you OK?"

Lily looks at Ben and says, "No, I'm not OK. You made me lose the race and hurt my arm. You are a bad brother. Go away!"

Ben feels sad and sorry. He says, "Please, Lily, don't be mad at me. I love you. You are my sister. Can I help you?"

Lily shakes her head and says, "No, you can't help me. You can only make things worse. Leave me alone!"

He takes off his blue vest and puts it on Lily. He says, "Here, take my vest. It will keep you warm and cozy. It will make you feel better. I don't need it. I have you."

Lily feels the warm vest on her body. She feels the soft fabric and the blue color. She looks at Ben and sees his smile. She feels a warm feeling in her heart. She says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. I love you too. I'm sorry I was mad at you."

Ben hugs Lily and says, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you are OK. I'm sorry I made you fall. Can we be friends again?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, we can be friends again. Can we share the sled and slide down the hill together?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, we can share the sled and slide down the hill together. That will be fun. Come on, let's go!"

They get on the sled and slide down the hill. They laugh and cheer. They forget about the pain and the race. They only feel the joy and the love. They wear their vests and their smiles. They are happy.

"Maybe it is a treasure," Ben said.

"Maybe it is a moon," Mia said.

"Ben, Mia, it is time to go home. The tide is coming in. We have to leave the beach," she said.

Ben and Mia did not want to go. They wanted to play with the shiny ball.

"Can we take it with us?" Ben asked.

"No, we cannot. It is too big and heavy. And it belongs to the sea. It is a buoy. It helps boats find their way," mom said.

"What is a buoy?" Mia asked.

"A buoy is a thing that floats on the water and has a light or a sound. It is like a sign for the boats. It tells them where to go and where not to go," mom said.

"Oh, I see. It is a helpful ball," Mia said.

"Yes, it is. But we have to go now. The water is getting higher. Come on, let's go," mom said.

Ben and Mia said goodbye to the buoy. They hoped to see it again. They followed mom to the car. They looked back at the beach. The tide was covering their sand castles and shells. But the buoy remained. It shone in the sun. It was different and special.

Lily nodded. She loved butterflies. They were so pretty and graceful.

Her mom said, "Then you have to let the caterpillar go. It will make a cocoon and become a butterfly. Maybe you can see it again when it comes out of the cocoon. But you have to be patient and wait. It takes some time for the caterpillar to change."

Bob said to Tim, "I want to eat that big prune up there." Tim looked up and saw the big prune. "Be careful, Bob," Tim said. "That branch looks weak."

Bob did not listen to Tim. He flew up to the big prune. The branch was weak and it broke. Bob fell down with the branch and the big prune.

Bob was hurt and sad. He could not play with Tim for many days. They both learned it is important to be careful and listen to friends.

One day, Ben finds a new novel in his room. It is big and blue and shiny. It has a picture of a snowman on the cover. Ben thinks it looks fun. He opens the novel and starts to read.

The novel is about a snowman who can talk and move. He lives in a land of ice and snow. He has many friends, like a penguin and a polar bear. He likes to play and sing and dance. Ben likes the snowman. He wishes he could meet him.

But then, something bad happens. A mean man comes to the land of ice and snow. He has a big machine that makes hot air. He wants to melt the snowman and his friends. He says he hates ice and snow. He says he wants to make the land warm and dry.

The snowman and his friends are scared. They try to hide and run away. But the mean man finds them. He points his machine at them. He says he will make them go away forever. He laughs a crazy laugh.

Ben feels sad and angry. He wants to help the snowman and his friends. He does not like the mean man. He thinks he is bad and mean. He wishes he could stop him.

Suddenly, Ben has an idea. He remembers a word he learned from his mom. It is a word that can make things stop moving. It is a word that can make things cold and hard. It is a word that can save the snowman and his friends.

Ben shouts the word as loud as he can. He shouts: "Freeze!"

And then, something amazing happens. The novel starts to glow. The air starts to blow. The room starts to snow. The mean man and his machine freeze. They become cold and hard. They cannot move or talk or laugh. They are stuck.

The snowman and his friends are happy. They are safe and free. They thank Ben for saving them. They say he is brave and smart and kind. They say he is their friend.

Ben smiles. He feels happy and proud. He closes the novel and hugs it. He says he likes the snowman and his friends. He says he is glad he read the novel. He says he will read it again. He says it is his favorite novel.

"Your movie is ugly," Ben says. "The car is boring and the robot is dumb."

The movie store man sees them. He is not happy. He questions them.

"Why are you fighting?" he asks. "Movies are for fun, not for fighting. You can watch both movies. You can take turns. You can learn from each other. You can be friends."

Anna and Ben think. They feel sorry. They say sorry.

"Sorry, Anna," Ben says. "Your movie is not ugly. The dragon is cool and the princess is brave."

"Sorry, Ben," Anna says. "Your movie is not ugly. The car is fast and the robot is smart."

They hug. They smile. They share their movies. They thank the movie store man. They go home. They watch both movies. They have fun. They are friends.

Lily felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I thought it was a jewelry box. I like jewelry. Can I have a cookie?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily. You cannot have a cookie. They are for your dad. You have to wait until his birthday. Now, put the box back where you found it and go wash your hands. It is time for lunch."

Lily did as she was told. She put the box back in her mom's room and went to the bathroom. She washed her hands and dried them with a towel. She was hungry, but she was also sad. She wanted a cookie. She wanted to see the jewelry.

She went to the kitchen, where her mom had made some sandwiches and soup. She sat on her chair and looked at her plate. She did not want to eat. She was grumpy.

Her mom said, "Lily, what is wrong? Why are you not eating? You like sandwiches and soup."

Lily said, "I don't want to eat. I want a cookie. I want to see the jewelry."

Her mom said, "Lily, stop being grumpy. There is no jewelry. There are only cookies. And you cannot have a cookie until your dad's birthday. You have to eat your lunch first. It is good for you. It will make you happy and strong."

Lily said, "No, it won't. It will make me sad and weak. I don't like lunch. I like cookies. I like jewelry."

Her mom said, "Lily, that is enough. You are being very rude and selfish. You have to eat your lunch or you will go to your room. Do you understand?"

Lily said, "No, I don't. I don't want to eat. I don't want to go to my room. I want a cookie. I want to see the jewelry."

Her mom said, "Lily, that is it. You are going to your room. You can stay there until you are ready to apologize and eat your lunch. And you can forget about the cookies and the jewelry. You will not get any of them. Now, go."

Lily started to cry. She said, "No, mom. Please, mom. I'm sorry, mom. I'll eat my lunch. I'll be good. Please, mom."

But her mom did not listen. She took her by the hand and led her to her room. She closed the door and left her alone. Lily sat on her bed and sobbed. She felt very unhappy. She wished she had not played with the box. She wished she had not been grumpy. She wished she had a cookie. She wished she had some jewelry.

The boy took the necklace and looked at it. He sighed. "It's okay, I guess. I dropped it by accident. It was a gift from my grandma. She said it was very special. It's called a sapphire."

Lily nodded. She did not know what a sapphire was, but it sounded nice. She smiled at the boy. "It's very beautiful. I'm glad you found it."

The boy smiled back. He was not angry anymore. He was curious too. He asked Lily, "What's your name?"

Lily told him her name. They introduced themselves. They decided to be friends. They swam together in the lake and looked for more shiny things. They had fun. They learned new words. They were happy.

"What is this?" Lila asked.

"Sure, why not? Let's pick one," Ben said.

They looked at the map and pointed at different countries. Lila liked the ones that were pink and purple. Ben liked the ones that were green and blue.

"I want this one. It is big and pretty," Lila said, pointing at a pink country.

"No, I want that one. It is bigger and prettier," Ben said, pointing at the same country.

They started to argue and pull the map. They did not want to share the country.

"Stop it! You are tearing the map!" Lila cried.

"I don't care. You are being greedy!" Ben shouted.

They pulled harder and harder, until the map ripped in half. They both fell to the ground, holding their pieces.

They looked at each other and felt sad. They had ruined the map and their friendship.

They saw an old man walking by. He had a long beard and a kind smile. He saw the torn map and the unhappy children.

"What happened here?" he asked.

"We wanted to own a country, but we could not agree on which one. So we ripped the map," Lila said.

"That is a shame. You know, owning a country is not as fun as you think. It comes with many problems and troubles. You have to deal with other countries, and wars, and money, and people. It is not easy to make everyone happy," the old man said.

"Really?" Ben asked.

"Really. I know, because I used to own a country," the old man said.

"You did?" Lila and Ben asked.

"Yes, I did. But I gave it up, because it made me unhappy. It was an ugly country, with no flowers, no trees, no animals, no sun. It was always dark and cold and dirty. I hated it," the old man said.

"Which country was it?" Lila and Ben asked.

The old man pointed at the map. He pointed at a gray country that was very small and had no neighbors.

"It was this one. It was called Noland. It was the worst country in the world," he said.

Lila and Ben looked at the map. They saw the gray country. It looked very sad and lonely.

They looked at each other and smiled. They hugged and said sorry.

"Can we still be friends?" Lila asked.

"Of course we can. Friends are better than countries," Ben said.

They gave their pieces of the map to the old man. They thanked him for his story. They asked him to join them in the park.

The old man smiled. He was happy to have new friends. He followed them to the park.

They played and shared and laughed. They forgot about the map and the countries. They were happy.

The moral of the story is to always be careful when you ride in a jeep. It's important to drive safely and make sure the doors are closed.

Suddenly, she heard a strange noise. Sophie was scared at first, but when she looked closer, she saw something that surprised her. It was a small rabbit hopping around in the garden! Sophie giggled and reached out to touch it. The rabbit was very friendly and squeaked in delight. 

Sophie and the rabbit played together in the garden until Sophie had to go home. She waved goodbye and continued to be surprised by the world around her!

She was so excited that she started jumping up and down and couldn't stop smiling. She couldn't wait to go visit her Grandparents and have a wonderful time.

Once upon a time, there was a leopard who liked to play games. One day, it saw a sour apple. It tried to eat the apple, but it was too sour. So it decided to reverse its game and throw the apple.

As the leopard threw the apple, it flew over the trees. Then it landed back in the leopard's paws. The leopard thought this was fun, so it decided to throw the apple again.

This time, the apple flew higher than before. But it did not land in the leopard's paws. Instead, it landed in the tree! 

The leopard laughed and ran to the tree. It tried to reach the apple with its paw but it was too high up. So the leopard thought and thought until it came up with a plan.

It reversed its game once again. This time, the leopard curled up its tail and threw it straight up. As the tail rose, it hooked the sour apple and brought it back down to the ground.

The leopard was happy and proud of itself. It ate the sour apple and enjoyed its sweet taste. After this, it continued to play the same game until the sun set.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a dog named Spot who was very friendly and liked to chase balls.

One day, their mom told them to get ready for school. She said they had to wear their jackets because it was cold outside. Anna and Ben ran to their room and put on their jackets. But Anna had a problem. Her zipper was stuck and she could not close her jacket. She tried to pull it hard, but it did not move.

"Ben, help me!" she cried. "My zipper is stuck!"

Ben came over and looked at her zipper. He saw that it was twisted and jammed. He tried to fix it, but it was too hard.

"Maybe we can ask mom to help us," he said.

But Anna did not want to ask mom. She was afraid that mom would be angry with her for breaking her zipper. She was also afraid that they would be late for school and miss the bus.

"No, we can't ask mom," she said. "She will be mad and we will be in trouble. Let's just go outside and pretend nothing is wrong."

Ben was not sure about this. He knew that mom would not be mad, but he wanted to make Anna happy. So he agreed to go outside with her. They put on their backpacks and ran to the door.

But Spot was waiting for them. He was a nosy dog who liked to sniff everything. He saw Anna's zipper and thought it was a toy. He jumped on her and tried to bite it.

"Spot, no!" Anna shouted. "Leave my zipper alone!"

But Spot did not listen. He pulled harder and harder on the zipper, until it broke off. Anna's jacket flew open and she felt the cold air on her chest. She started to shiver and cry.

Ben saw what happened and felt sorry for Anna. He took off his jacket and wrapped it around her. He hugged her and said, "It's okay, Anna. Don't cry. We can tell mom what happened and she will fix it. She will not be mad at you. She will be proud of you for telling the truth."

Anna looked at Ben and nodded. She realized that he was right. She wiped her tears and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I lied to you. Let's go tell mom what happened."

They walked back to the house and found mom in the kitchen. They told her everything that happened and showed her the broken zipper. Mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you told me the truth. I'm not mad at you, Anna. I know you were scared. But lying is not a good thing to do. It can make things worse and hurt the people you love. Next time, if you have a problem, you can always come to me and I will help you. Okay?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We're sorry we lied to you. We love you."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too. Now, let's go find another jacket for Anna and catch the bus. We still have time. But next time, don't delay getting ready for school. It's important to be on time and prepared."

Anna and Ben learned their lesson. They never lied to mom again. They always got ready for school on time and checked their zippers. And they always played with Spot, but not with their clothes.

Ben likes to count his money. He has a wallet with many coins and some bills. He keeps his wallet in his drawer under his bed. He counts his money every night before he sleeps.

One day, Ben comes home from school and wants to count his money. He goes to his drawer and opens it. But his wallet is not there. He looks around and sees his brother Sam. Sam has a big smile and a new toy. It is a furry bear that can talk.

Ben is angry. He runs to Sam and says, "Give me back my wallet! You took my money and bought that bear!" Sam says, "No, I did not. I found this bear in the trash. It is mine now. Go away!" Ben tries to grab the bear, but Sam pushes him away. They start to fight.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees Ben and Sam on the floor, pulling the bear. She is mad. She says, "Stop it, both of you! What is going on here?" Ben says, "Sam stole my wallet and bought that bear! He is a thief!" Sam says, "No, I did not. I found this bear in the trash. Ben is a liar!"

Mom looks at the bear and sees a tag. It says, "Price: $20. Store: Toy Land." She knows that Sam is lying. She says, "Sam, tell me the truth. Did you take Ben's wallet and buy this bear?" Sam looks down and says, "Yes, I did. I'm sorry."

Mom is very disappointed. She says, "Sam, you did a very bad thing. You took Ben's money without his permission. You lied to me and to him. You hurt his feelings. You have to give back his wallet and his money. And you have to return this bear to the store. And you have to say sorry to Ben and to me."

Sam feels ashamed. He gives back Ben's wallet and his money. He says sorry to Ben and to Mom. He takes the bear and goes to the store. He tells the cashier what he did and asks for a refund. The cashier is surprised and says, "You are very brave to admit your mistake. But I'm sorry, we don't accept returns for toys that are used or damaged. You have to keep the bear."

Sam comes back home with the bear. He does not want it anymore. He thinks it is ugly and annoying. He tries to give it to Ben, but Ben does not want it either. He says, "That bear is not a good toy. It reminds me of how you stole my money. I don't like it. You can keep it."

Sam is sad. He has no money, no new toy, and no friends. He puts the bear in his closet and closes the door. He hears the bear say, "I love you. Do you love me?" He does not answer. He wishes he never took Ben's wallet. He wishes he never bought the bear. He wishes he could start over. But he can't. He has to live with his mistake. He has to live with the furry bear. The end.

Then, they heard a loud beep from the computer. They looked up and saw their dad on the screen. He was talking to someone. He said, "Hello, this is Tom from the network. I need your help with a problem."

Lily and Ben were curious. They wanted to see what their dad was doing. They got up and walked to the computer. They saw a lot of numbers and words on the screen. They did not understand them.

They saw a button that said "shrink". They wondered what it did. Lily reached out and pressed it. Suddenly, the screen got smaller and smaller. Their dad and the other person disappeared. The computer made a strange noise.

Lily and Ben were scared. They did not know what they had done. They tried to press the button again, but it did not work. They heard their dad's voice from inside the computer. He sounded angry. He said, "Lily, Ben, what did you do? You shrunk the network! You need to fix it now!"

Lily and Ben did not know how to fix it. They started to cry. They wished they had not touched the button. They wished their dad was not mad at them.

Then, they heard a knock on the door. They opened it and saw their grandma. She was elderly and kind. She had gray hair and glasses. She smiled and said, "Hello, my darlings. I came to visit you. What's wrong?"

If you want to keep it, you have to get a bigger tank, a heater, a filter and more fish. That will cost a lot of money. Do you have that money?"

Timmy said, "No, I don't. I only have a little money. I used it to buy the fish."

The veterinarian said, "Then I'm afraid you have to quit keeping this fish. It is not fair to the fish. It will die soon if you don't change its home. You have to give it back to the pet store or find someone who can take care of it. Do you understand?"

Timmy felt sad and angry. He liked his fish. He didn't want to give it up. He said, "No, I don't understand. It is my fish. I bought it. I love it. You can't take it away from me. You are a bad veterinarian. You don't care about animals. You are mean."

He grabbed his fish tank and ran out of the room. He tripped on his toy animals and fell down. The tank broke and the water spilled. The fish flopped on the floor. Timmy cried and screamed. His mom and the veterinarian tried to help him and the fish. But it was too late. The fish was dead.

The moral of the story is: You should not buy animals without knowing how to take care of them. You should listen to the experts and respect their advice. You should not be selfish and stubborn. You should think about the animals' needs and feelings. You should be a responsible and kind pet owner.

Sarah said, "Buddy, let's play together!" Buddy wagged his tail and barked happily. They played for a whole year, kicking the ball and laughing. Buddy and Sarah became best friends and had lots of fun together.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a sweet, little cat. The cat had a hurt thumb. Tim frowned because he felt sad for the cat.

"Meow," said the cat. Tim wanted to help the cat. He tried to make the cat feel better by giving it a hug. But the cat was scared and ran away.

Tim looked for the cat but could not find it. He felt very sad and cried. His friend came and tried to make him feel better, but Tim still felt sad. The cat did not come back, and Tim went home with a frown on his face.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. He wore his favorite hat. It was a big, red hat. Tim loved to play in the park with his friends.

Tim saw a grumpy old man sitting on a bench. The old man was sad because he lost his hat. Tim wanted to help the old man. He had an idea. He asked his friends to gather and look for the old man's hat.

They looked all around the park. They found the old man's hat under a tree. It was a blue hat. Tim gave the hat to the grumpy old man. The old man was very happy. He said thank you to Tim and his friends. They all played together in the park and had a great day.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a strong girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to help her mom with chores. One day, Lucy's mom asked her to complete a task. "Lucy, can you please fold the cloth for me?" said her mom.

Lucy was happy to help. She picked up the big, soft cloth and started to fold it. She made sure it was nice and neat. "Look, Mom! I did it!" said Lucy, showing her mom the folded cloth.

"Great job, Lucy!" her mom said with a big smile. "You are such a strong and helpful girl. Thank you for completing the task." Lucy felt proud and happy that she could help her mom. They both hugged and continued to do more chores together, making their little house clean and tidy.

Once there was a lonely fan. It lived in a small room. The fan was sad because it had no friends to play with. One day, a little girl named Jane came to the room. She saw the sad fan and said, "Hi, fan! Why are you sad?"

The fan replied, "I am lonely. I have no friends to play with." Jane thought for a moment and then said, "I will be your friend! But first, we need to wash you. You are very dirty."

So Jane got a cloth and some water. She washed the fan until it was clean and shiny. The fan felt very happy and said, "Thank you, Jane! Now I am clean and have a friend to play with."

From that day on, Jane and the fan played together every day. They had a lot of fun and the fan was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a funny bunny named Bob. Bob loved to play games with his friends. One sunny day, Bob and his friends decided to have a race in the park.

As they lined up, Bob's friend, the squirrel, said, "If you win, you get a big chocolate!" Bob's eyes grew wide, and he got very excited. He loved chocolate more than anything.

The race began, and Bob hopped as fast as he could. His friends ran and jumped, trying to win too. Bob hopped and hopped, and finally, he crossed the finish line first. His friends clapped and cheered.

Bob's friend, the squirrel, gave him the big chocolate. "You won, Bob! Here's your prize!" he said with a smile. Bob thanked his friend and shared the chocolate with everyone. They all laughed and had a great time eating the sweet treat together. And that's how Bob, the funny bunny, had the best day ever with his friends.

Once upon a time, in a big tree, there lived a loud owl. The owl liked to make noise at night when everyone was sleeping. The other animals in the forest did not like this.

One night, the animals had a meeting. They talked about the loud owl. "We must do something," said the squirrel. "I can't sleep because of the noise." The other animals agreed. They decided to punish the loud owl.

The next day, the animals went to the loud owl's tree. "You must stop making noise at night," said the rabbit. "Or we will punish you." The owl listened and felt sad. He promised to be quiet at night from then on.

That night, the loud owl was quiet. The animals in the forest could finally sleep. They were happy that the owl learned his lesson. From then on, they all lived happily and quietly in the forest.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. He saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. Tim felt happy when he was climbing the tree. But when he got to the top, he saw something disgusting on the branch. It was a big, gooey mess.

Tim didn't want to touch the disgusting mess, but he wanted to keep climbing. He tried to go around it, but he couldn't. Tim felt sad and didn't know what to do. He called for his mom to help him.

His mom came and saw the disgusting mess too. She told Tim that they should clean it up, so other kids don't feel sad too. They got some paper and wiped the mess away. Tim felt happy again and could keep climbing. He learned the value of helping others and keeping the park clean.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play together. One day, they decide to play shop. Tom has a big bag of rice. He says he will sell the rice to Anna. Anna has some coins. She says she will buy the rice from Tom.

They go to the garden and find a table. They put the bag of rice on the table. Tom makes a sign that says "Rice for sale". Anna comes to the table and looks at the rice. She says, "How much is the rice, Tom?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He says, "The rice is five coins, Anna. It is very good rice. It is big and white and tasty."

Anna counts her coins. She has four coins. She says, "I only have four coins, Tom. Can I have some rice for four coins?"

Tom shakes his head. He says, "No, Anna. The rice is five coins. You need one more coin."

Anna is sad. She wants the rice. She says, "Please, Tom. Can you give me some rice for four coins? I am your friend."

Tom looks at Anna. He sees that she is sad. He is her friend. He says, "Okay, Anna. You can have some rice for four coins. But only a little bit. Not the whole bag."

Anna is happy. She says, "Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. Here are four coins for you."

Tom takes the coins and gives Anna some rice. He says, "You are welcome, Anna. Enjoy the rice."

They smile at each other. They are happy. They have played shop. They have sold and bought rice. They have shared and helped each other. They are good friends.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the snow. They made a snowman and a snow fort. They threw snowballs at each other. They had fun.

But one day, Sam forgot his mittens at home. His hands were very cold. He wanted to go inside. He tried to tell Lily, but Lily did not hear him. She was busy making a snow angel. She did not see Sam's sign.

Sam was sad and angry. He thought Lily did not care about him. He picked up a big snowball and threw it at Lily. It hit her in the face. It hurt.

Lily was shocked and hurt. She did not know why Sam did that. She started to cry. She looked at Sam. She saw his sign. He was pointing at his hands. He was shivering.

Lily understood. She felt sorry for Sam. She was compassionate. She took off one of her mittens and gave it to Sam. She said, "Here, Sam. You can have my mitten. I don't want you to be cold."

Sam was surprised and happy. He took Lily's mitten and put it on his hand. He felt warmer. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. I'm sorry I threw a snowball at you. I was mad and cold."

Lily smiled and hugged Sam. She said, "It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. You are my best friend. Let's go inside and have some hot chocolate."

They held hands and walked to Lily's house. They were friends again. They were happy.

Lily liked to write in her journal every day. She wrote about her toys, her friends, her family, and her dreams. She kept her journal in a secret place under her bed, where no one could find it.

One day, Lily's big brother Jake was bored. He wanted to play with Lily, but she was busy writing in her journal. He tried to peek under her bed, but Lily saw him and shouted, "No, Jake! That's mine! Go away!"

Jake was angry. He waited until Lily went to the bathroom, and then he grabbed her journal. He ran to the living room, where Mom and Dad were talking on the phone. He wanted to show them what Lily wrote, and make fun of her.

But as he ran, he tripped over the rug and fell. The journal flew out of his hand and landed on the coffee table. The phone also fell and hit the floor. It made a loud ring sound that scared Jake.

Mom and Dad turned around and saw what happened. They were very upset. They saw Lily's journal and the broken phone. They scolded Jake for being naughty and careless. They told him to apologize to Lily and pay for the phone.

Lily came back and saw her journal on the table. She was very sad and angry. She cried and hugged her journal. She did not want to talk to Jake. She did not trust him anymore.

Jake felt sorry and ashamed. He said he was sorry, but Lily did not listen. He wished he had not taken her journal. He wished he had been a good and dependable brother. He learned his lesson, but it was too late.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big dog with a ball in his mouth. The dog was friendly and wagged his tail. Tom and Lily wanted to play with the dog and his ball.

"Can we play with you, dog?" Tom asked. The dog barked and dropped the ball. Tom and Lily picked up the ball and threw it. The dog ran after it and brought it back. They played for a long time and had fun.

But then a mean boy came. He was bigger than Tom and Lily and had a bad face. He saw the dog and his ball and wanted to take them. He grabbed the ball from the dog's mouth and kicked the dog. The dog yelped and ran away. Tom and Lily were scared and angry.

"Hey, that's not nice! Give the ball back to the dog!" Lily shouted. The mean boy laughed and threw the ball far away. He said, "You are stupid and the dog is stupid. I have the ball now and you can't have it. I have more muscle than you and the dog."

Tom and Lily felt sad and wanted to help the dog. They looked around and saw a big stick. They had an idea. They ran to the stick and picked it up. They ran back to the mean boy and hit him with the stick. The mean boy dropped the ball and cried. He ran away and said, "Ow, ow, ow! You are mean and the stick is mean. I don't want the ball anymore. You are stronger than me and the stick."

Tom and Lily smiled and picked up the ball. They looked for the dog and found him hiding behind a tree. He was shaking and had a hurt leg. Tom and Lily hugged him and said, "We are sorry, dog. We are your friends and we want to play with you. We will rescue you from the mean boy and take you to the vet. You are not stupid and you have more muscle than the mean boy."

The dog licked their faces and wagged his tail. He was happy and grateful. Tom and Lily took the dog and his ball and walked to the vet. They helped the dog and played with him. They became best friends and never saw the mean boy again.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a big box of toys in the park. They were very happy and opened the box. There were many toys inside, like cars, dolls, balls and books.

"Wow, look at all these toys!" Tom said. "Let's play with them!"

"Yes, let's!" Lily agreed. "But we have to share them, okay?"

"Okay, okay," Tom said. But he did not really want to share. He wanted to have all the toys for himself.

They started to play with the toys, but soon Tom began to take more and more toys from Lily. He took her car, her doll, her ball and her book. He put them all in a big pile and tied them with a rope.

"Hey, stop that!" Lily said. "Those are my toys too! You have to share!"

"No, they are mine!" Tom said. "I found them first! Go away!"

Lily was very sad and angry. She tried to get her toys back, but Tom was stronger and pushed her away. He laughed and said, "I succeed! I have all the toys! You have none!"

Lily ran away, crying. She did not want to be friends with Tom anymore. She thought he was very mean and selfish. She wished he was more generous and kind.

Tom was left alone with his pile of toys. He felt proud and happy for a while, but soon he got bored. He had no one to play with, no one to talk to, no one to have fun with. He looked around and saw that the park was empty. He felt lonely and sad. He wished he had not taken all the toys from Lily. He wished he had shared them with her. He wished he had not lost his friend. But it was too late. He had made a big mistake. He had a bad ending.

Anna and Ben were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very happy and excited. They put on their hats and shoes and waited for the taxi.

"Mom, when will the taxi come?" Anna asked.

"Soon, honey. Don't worry. We have plenty of time," Mom said.

The taxi came and they got in. The driver was nice and asked them where they wanted to go.

"To the zoo, please. We want to see the lions and the monkeys and the penguins," Ben said.

The driver smiled and drove away. He turned on the radio and they heard some music.

"Mom, can we sing along?" Anna asked.

"Sure, sweetie. As long as you don't sing too loud and bother the driver," Mom said.

They sang some songs they knew and had fun. The taxi stopped at a red light and they saw a man selling lemonade.

"Mom, can we have some lemonade? We are thirsty," Ben said.

Mom looked at the man and saw that he had a sign that said "One dollar for a cup".

"I'm sorry, kids. We don't have enough money for lemonade. We need to save it for the zoo tickets," Mom said.

"But Mom, it's so hot and we are so thirsty," Anna said.

"I know, honey. But we have some water in the bag. We can drink that when we get to the zoo. It's not far now," Mom said.

"OK, Mom. We promise we won't ask for lemonade again," Ben said.

"Good. Thank you for being good kids. I love you both," Mom said.

They hugged Mom and said they loved her too. The taxi started moving again and soon they arrived at the zoo. They paid the driver and thanked him. They got out of the taxi and ran to the gate. They were ready to see the animals and have a great day.

"Hey, those are my gears!" Ben said. He was angry that Lily took his gears without asking. He wanted to make a gear spaceship. He tried to take back his gears from Lily's dragon.

"No, they are mine now!" Lily said. She did not want to share her gears with Ben. She wanted to finish her dragon. She held on to her gears tightly.

Ben and Lily started to pull and tug on the gears. They both wanted the same gears for their toys. They did not listen to each other. They did not say sorry or please. They did not have fun.

Suddenly, Lily felt a sharp pain in her hand. She looked and saw that Ben had bitten her. He had bitten her hard because he was very mad. Lily screamed and dropped the gears. She started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! Ben, you bit me! That hurts!" Lily said. She ran to their mom and showed her the bite mark.

Mom was shocked and upset. She saw the bite mark on Lily's hand and the gears on the floor. She knew that Ben and Lily had been fighting over the gears. She was not happy with them.

"Ben, why did you bite your sister? That is not nice. That is not how we play. You need to say sorry to Lily and share your gears with her. Biting is not okay." Mom said. She scolded Ben and made him apologize to Lily. She also gave Lily a band-aid and a hug.

Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He knew that biting was wrong. He did not want to hurt Lily. He wanted to play with her. He said sorry to Lily and gave her a hug. He also gave her some of his gears to make her dragon.

Lily felt better and forgave Ben. She knew that Ben was sorry. She wanted to play with him. She said thank you to Ben and gave him a hug. She also gave him some of her gears to make his spaceship.

Ben and Lily learned their lesson. They decided to share their gears and play nicely. They made a gear dragon and a gear spaceship together. They had fun. They were happy.

Sara and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a big tent with many people inside. Mom said it was a bake sale for the school. Sara and Ben liked cake very much, so they asked mom if they could go inside.

Mom said yes, but they had to stay close to her. She gave them some money and told them to pick one cake each. Sara and Ben walked around the tent, looking at all the different cakes. There were chocolate cakes, vanilla cakes, carrot cakes, and more. They smelled very good.

He gave the man some money and took the cake.

"Let's travel in the tube!" Lila says. "Maybe we can see something new."

"OK!" Tom says. "But we have to be careful. The tube might be dirty or dark."

They crawl into the tube. It is not dirty or dark. It is bright and colorful. They see flowers and butterflies and birds. They hear music and laughter. They smell honey and cake. They feel happy and curious.

"Wow!" Lila says. "This is a magic tube! It takes us to a wonderful place."

"Yes!" Tom says. "But we should not forget where we came from. We have to go back soon. Our moms and dads will miss us."

They nod. They are humble. They know they are lucky to see the magic place, but they also love their home and family. They say thank you to the tube and crawl out. They hug each other and run back to the park. They have a big smile on their faces. They have a story to tell.

Mia liked to play with her toys in her room. She had many toys, but her favorite was a doll named Lily. Mia was very organized. She always put her toys in the right boxes when she was done playing.

One day, Mia found a shiny ring on the floor. She did not know where it came from, but she thought it was pretty. She put it on her finger and said, "I wish I was as big as Lily!"

Suddenly, Mia felt a strange feeling. She looked around and saw that everything was bigger. Her bed, her dresser, her toys, even Lily! She had shrunk!

Mia was scared. She wanted to be normal again. She tried to take off the ring, but it was stuck. She cried, "Help! Help!"

A raven heard Mia's cry. It flew to the window and saw Mia on the floor. It was curious. It liked shiny things. It flew into the room and landed next to Mia. It said, "Hello, little girl. What are you doing here?"

Mia was surprised. She did not know that ravens could talk. She said, "Please, help me. I shrunk because of this ring. Can you take it off?"

The raven looked at the ring. It sparkled in the light. It said, "This ring is very nice. I want it. If you give it to me, I will help you."

Mia did not want to give the ring to the raven. She liked it too. But she wanted to be normal more. She said, "Okay, you can have it. But please, make me big again."

The raven nodded. It used its beak to pull the ring off Mia's finger. It said, "Thank you, little girl. Now, say your wish again."

Mia said, "I wish I was as big as Lily!"

Suddenly, Mia felt a strange feeling. She looked around and saw that everything was normal. Her bed, her dresser, her toys, even Lily! She had grown!

Mia was happy. She hugged Lily and said, "Thank you, raven. You are very kind."

The raven smiled. It said, "You are welcome, little girl. You are very brave. Goodbye." It flew away with the ring.

Mia waved goodbye to the raven. She learned a lesson. She decided to be careful with what she wished for. She also decided to be more organized. She put the ring in a box and labeled it, "Do not touch."

Tom and Lily liked to play on the carpet in the living room. They had many toys and books and games. But sometimes they got bored and wanted to do something new.

One day, they had an idea. They decided to move the carpet and see what was under it. They pushed and pulled and lifted the carpet. It was hard work, but they were strong and brave.

When they moved the carpet, they saw a big hole in the floor. It was dark and deep and scary. They heard a strange noise coming from the hole. It sounded like a growl or a roar.

Tom and Lily were scared. They dropped the carpet and ran to their mom. They told her what they saw and heard. Mom was surprised and worried. She went to the living room and looked at the hole.

She saw a furry face and two big eyes. It was their cat, Fluffy. He had crawled under the carpet and got stuck in the hole. He was not happy. He was hungry and angry.

Mom got a flashlight and a rope. She shone the light on Fluffy and threw the rope to him. She told him to grab the rope and she would pull him out. Fluffy did as he was told. He was glad to see mom and the light.

Lila and Ben were playing in the forest. They liked to climb trees and look for animals. They saw a big log on the ground. It was brown and long and had many holes.

"Let's see what is inside the log," Lila said. She ran to the log and put her hand in one of the holes. She felt something soft and furry. She pulled it out and saw a baby squirrel. It was gray and cute and had a bushy tail.

"Wow, look what I found!" Lila said, holding the squirrel. "It is so charming!"

Ben came closer and looked at the squirrel. He smiled and reached out his hand. "Can I hold it too?" he asked.

Lila nodded and gave him the squirrel. Ben held it gently and stroked its fur. The squirrel made a small noise and curled up in his hand.

"It must be lost," Ben said. "Maybe its mommy is looking for it."

"Maybe we can help it find its mommy," Lila said. "We can support it and keep it safe."

They decided to look around the log for any signs of the squirrel's family. They saw some nuts and acorns near the log. They also saw some scratch marks on the bark. They followed the marks and found a hole in the log that was bigger than the others.

"Maybe this is where the squirrel lives," Lila said. She put her ear to the hole and listened. She heard some squeaks and rustles. She smiled and said, "I think I hear its mommy and siblings!"

She and Ben carefully put the squirrel back in the hole. They saw its head pop out and look at them. It seemed to say thank you with its eyes. Then it disappeared into the log.

Lila and Ben waved goodbye to the squirrel and walked back to their parents. They felt happy and proud that they had helped a charming animal. They hoped the squirrel would have a good life in the log.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a stream in the woods. They saw fish and frogs and stones in the water. They wanted to catch some fish and frogs, but they did not have a net or a jar.

"I have an idea," said Ben. "We can use our hands to pinch the fish and frogs. Then we can put them in our pockets and take them home."

"That sounds clever," said Lily. "But how do we pinch them? They are very fast and slippery."

Ben said, "We have to be very quiet and sneaky. We have to wait until they come close to us. Then we have to grab them quickly and squeeze them hard."

They agreed to try Ben's idea. They took off their shoes and socks and rolled up their pants. They stepped into the stream and looked for fish and frogs. They saw a big fish swimming near a rock. Ben whispered, "Look, there is a fish. I will pinch it first. You watch and learn."

Ben crept closer to the rock. He reached out his hand and waited for the fish to come. The fish swam closer and closer. Ben was ready to pinch it. But just as he was about to grab it, the fish saw him and darted away. Ben missed the fish and pinched the rock instead. He hurt his finger and yelled, "Ow!"

Lily laughed and said, "That was not clever. That was silly. You pinched a rock, not a fish. You need to be more careful."

Ben felt embarrassed and angry. He said, "It was not my fault. The fish was too fast. You try and see if you can do better."

Lily said, "Okay, I will try. But I will not pinch a rock. I will pinch a frog. Frogs are easier to catch. They sit on the leaves and do not move much."

She looked for a frog and saw one on a leaf near the bank. She tiptoed to the leaf and reached out her hand. She was about to pinch the frog when the frog saw her and jumped. The frog landed on Lily's face and made a loud croak. Lily screamed and dropped the frog. She rubbed her eyes and nose and said, "Ew!"

Ben laughed and said, "That was not clever. That was funny. You pinched a frog, not a leaf. You need to be more brave."

Lily felt annoyed and scared. She said, "It was not my fault. The frog was too jumpy. You try and see if you can do better."

They argued for a while and then decided to try again. They looked for more fish and frogs in the stream. But they did not have any luck. They pinched rocks and leaves and sticks and mud, but not fish and frogs. They got wet and dirty and tired and bored. They gave up and said, "This is not fun. This is hard. Let's go home."

They put on their shoes and socks and walked back to their house. They saw their mom waiting for them. She saw their wet and dirty clothes and their sad faces. She said, "What happened to you? Did you have a good time in the woods?"

They said, "No, we did not. We tried to pinch fish and frogs, but we could not. We only pinched rocks and leaves and sticks and mud. We hurt our fingers and our faces and our feelings. We are not clever. We are silly."

Their mom hugged them and said, "You are not silly. You are curious and adventurous. You tried something new and learned something new. You learned that fish and frogs are not easy to catch. You learned that pinching is not a good way to catch them. You learned that pinching can hurt you and others. You learned that pinching is not fun. You learned a lot today. You are very clever."

They smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are very clever too. And very kind. And very sweet. Can we have a cookie?"

Their mom laughed and said, "Yes, you can have a cookie. But first, you have to wash your hands and your faces and your clothes. And then, you have to promise me that you will not pinch anything or anyone ever again."

They said, "Okay, mom. We promise. We will not pinch anything or anyone ever again. We will only pinch cookies. And we will share them with you."

They washed their hands and their faces and their clothes. They ate their cookies and shared them with their mom. They felt happy and loved. They forgot about the stream and the fish and the frogs. They did not pinch anything or anyone ever again. Except cookies.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pile of twigs near a tree. They ran to the pile and started to pick up the twigs.

"Look, I found a long twig!" Tim said. "I can use it as a sword!"

"Me too!" Sam said. "Let's have a sword fight!"

They swung their twigs at each other, pretending to be knights. They had fun, but they also got filthy. Their clothes, hands and faces were covered with dirt and leaves.

She grabbed their twigs and threw them away. Then she dragged them to the car, scolding them all the way. Tim and Sam felt sad and ashamed. They wished they had not played with the twigs.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not meant to be toys. They can be dangerous or dirty. Listen to your mom and respect the park.

Once upon a time there was a gray bird with a big knot on her tail. Even though the other birds made fun of her knot, the gray bird flapped her wings and flew with happiness.

One day, a storm struck the sky. All the birds were scared and flew away for safety, but the gray bird with the knot stayed. She looked up at the angry clouds and said, "I can handle this storm."

The storm raged for hours, but the gray bird remained perched on her branch, keeping her knot safe. Eventually, the storm stopped and the sky became clear. The other birds returned, amazed at how brave the gray bird had been. They thanked her for staying and admiringly cooed at her knot.

The moral of the story is that courage doesn't come from the absence of fear, but from the motivation to do what is right, even when it takes bravery. This means that no matter what difficulties or challenges come our way, we should always be brave and face them with courage.

Max didn't notice that his collar was gone, and he kept running after the squirrel. But when he got too far away from Sarah, he realized he was lost. Max felt scared without his collar, and he didn't know how to find his way back home.

"Hi, dad!" Tom says. "Can we play hockey now?"

"Sure, Tom," dad says. "But first, we have to complete a small job. We have to rake the leaves and put them in the bag. Then we can play hockey as long as we want."

Tom is not happy. He does not like raking leaves. He thinks it is boring and hard. He wants to play hockey right away. But he knows dad is right. He has to help dad with the job. He takes a rake and starts to rake the leaves.

Dad rakes the leaves too. He smiles at Tom and says, "You are doing a great job, Tom. We are almost done. Then we can have fun with your new hockey stick and puck."

Tom tries to smile back. He rakes faster and faster. He wants to complete the job quickly. He does not see the big rock under the leaves. He hits the rock with his rake. The rake breaks in half. Tom falls down and hurts his knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cries. He drops the rake and holds his knee. He feels a big bump and a lot of pain.

Dad runs to Tom and picks him up. He hugs him and says, "Oh, Tom, I'm so sorry. Are you okay? Let me see your knee."

Dad looks at Tom's knee. He sees a small cut and some blood. He says, "It's not too bad, Tom. Just a little scratch. We can clean it and put a band-aid on it. Then you will feel better."

Tom sniffles and nods. He is glad dad is here. He says, "Thank you, dad. I'm sorry I broke the rake."

Dad says, "Don't worry, Tom. The rake is not important. You are important. And you know what? We have completed the job. We have raked all the leaves. We can play hockey now. Do you still want to play?"

Tom smiles and says, "Yes, dad. I still want to play. I love hockey. And I love you."

Dad smiles and says, "I love you too, Tom. Come on, let's play hockey. You can use your new hockey stick and puck. And I will use the old one. Maybe you can score a goal on me."

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. One day, they saw a big jar of salt on the counter. They wondered what it was and how it tasted. They climbed on a chair and opened the jar.

"Look, it's like snow!" Sara said, scooping some salt with her hand.

"Let me try!" Ben said, grabbing some salt and putting it in his mouth. He made a face and spat it out. "Yuck! It's not sweet, it's bitter!"

Sara laughed and tried some salt too. She also spat it out and said, "You're right, it's not good!"

They heard their mom coming and quickly closed the jar and got down from the chair. They ran to the living room and pretended to read a book.

Mom came in and smiled at them. She said, "What are you two doing? Are you having fun?"

Sara and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom, we are reading a book."

Mom said, "That's good, reading is good for you. But do you know what else is good for you? Drinking water. Especially after you eat something salty."

Sara and Ben looked at each other and felt guilty. They knew they had done something wrong. They said, "Sorry, mom, we were playing with the salt. We were wondering what it was and how it tasted. We didn't like it."

Mom said, "It's okay, I'm not angry. But you should always ask me before you touch something in the kitchen. Some things are not safe or healthy for you. Salt is good for cooking, but not for eating by itself. It can make you thirsty and sick. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We won't do it again. Can we have some water, please?"

Mom said, "Of course, here you go. Drink some clear water and wash away the salt. And next time, if you wonder about something, just ask me. I'll be happy to tell you."

Sara and Ben said, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, my little wonders."

The moral of the story is: Don't give up hope. Your friends will always miss you and look for you. Your trunk is tough and can help you in many ways.

One day, Tim and Sam play chess at Tim's house. Tim is black and Sam is white. Tim moves his pieces fast and smart. He catches many of Sam's pieces. Sam moves his pieces slow and careful. He tries to save his king.

"Ha ha, I am winning!" Tim says. He smiles big. He is proud of his chess. He wants to show his chess to everyone. He puts his chess on the window. He points at his chess. He says, "Look, look, I am the best at chess!"

But Tim does not see a bird. The bird sees the chess. The bird likes shiny things. The bird flies to the window. The bird grabs a piece with its beak. The bird flies away with the piece.

"Oh no, my chess!" Tim says. He runs to the window. He sees the bird. He sees his piece. He is sad and angry. He cries loud. He says, "Give me back my chess!"

Sam sees Tim. He feels sorry for Tim. He says, "Don't cry, Tim. It is just a game. It is not nice to display your chess like that. You should be humble and kind. You should share your chess with others. Maybe the bird will bring back your piece. Maybe we can play chess again."

Tim hears Sam. He thinks about what Sam says. He knows Sam is right. He wipes his tears. He says, "I am sorry, Sam. You are a good friend. You are good at chess too. I was mean and selfish. I will not display my chess like that again. I will be humble and kind. I will share my chess with others. Thank you, Sam."

Sam smiles. He says, "You are welcome, Tim. I am glad you are sorry. You are a good friend too. I hope the bird will bring back your piece. I hope we can play chess again."

The bird hears Tim and Sam. The bird sees their chess. The bird likes their chess. The bird brings back the piece. The bird puts the piece on the board. The bird makes a sound. The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet!"

Tim and Sam see the bird. They see their piece. They are happy and surprised. They say, "Wow, thank you, bird! You are a nice bird. You are good at chess too. Do you want to play chess with us?"

The bird nods. The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet!"

Tim and Sam laugh. They say, "Okay, let's play chess together. We can take turns. We can have fun. We can learn from each other. Chess is a game for everyone."

The end.

"Come on, Liz," he said. "It's so good. You can have some too."

Liz shook her head. She did not want to be bad. She ran to Mom and told her what Tim did.

Mom was angry. She went to the kitchen and saw the pastry. She saw Tim with cream and fruit on his face. She scolded him and sent him to his room.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Tim said. "I was hungry. I didn't mean to ruin the pastry."

Mom sighed. She hugged Liz and thanked her for being honest. She said, "Tim, you have to learn to plan ahead. If you are hungry, you can ask me for a snack. You don't have to take what is not yours. And you have to respect other people's things. How would you feel if someone ate your cake?"

Mom smiled. She said, "It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. But you have to make it up to Dad. You have to help me make a new pastry for him. And you have to share it with everyone."

Moral value: The story teaches the value of planning ahead, respecting other people's things, being honest, and sharing.

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy!" But then she looked at the real cactus again and started to weep. "Why are you crying, Lily?" her mom asked. "I don't want the cactus to be lonely," Lily said. "I want to draw it some friends." So Lily drew some more cacti and they all became friends. From that day on, Lily loved to draw and make new friends for her cactus.

Lily was happy because she saw many new things on her tour and she knew that her mommy and daddy would always keep her safe.

The storm kept growing and everything stayed still. But then something amazing happened. A little girl walked outside with something special in her hand. It was a tiny snow globe. 

The little girl spun it around, and with a wave of her hand, the storm stopped. The birds started flying again and the people moved about. Everything was back to normal. 

The little girl smiled and kept her snow globe safe inside her pocket. She would never forget the day the storm was gone and everything was free to move again.

Papa said, "Come, we should find a warm place to stay." He pointed to an old broken stove at the side of the road. 

Mama asked, "Will it keep us warm?" 

Papa said, "It might be broken, but we can try to make it work." 

So they both went to the stove, opened it, and put some logs inside to make a fire. 

Then, standing close to the stove, they closed their eyes, shivered, and waited for the warmt to come. Soon, the stove was giving off a nice, warm heat. 

Mama and Papa stayed near the broken stove and stayed warm until the snow stopped. Then Papa took Mama home.

Lily was a little dog who loved to sing. She sang when she was happy, she sang when she was sad, she sang when she was bored. She sang to the birds, the flowers, the sun and the moon. She sang all day long.

One day, she found a big bone in the park. She was very happy and ran to it. She picked it up with her mouth and started to sing. She sang a song about the bone, how tasty it was, how lucky she was, how much she liked it.

But then, she heard a loud growl behind her. She turned around and saw a big dog, bigger than her, with sharp teeth and angry eyes. The big dog wanted the bone. He barked at Lily and said, "Give me the bone, or I will bite you!"

Lily was frightened. She did not want to give up the bone, but she did not want to be bitten either. She did not know what to do. She looked at the big dog and said, "Please, can we share the bone? I found it first, but you can have some too. I don't want to fight with you."

The big dog was surprised. He had never heard a dog sing before. He had never heard a dog ask to share before. He was used to taking what he wanted by force. He looked at Lily and said, "You sing? Why do you sing?"

Lily said, "I sing because I love to sing. Singing makes me happy. Singing makes everything better. Do you want to sing with me?"

The big dog was curious. He had never tried to sing before. He said, "How do you sing?"

Lily said, "It's easy. You just open your mouth and make a sound. Like this: woof, woof, woof!"

The big dog said, "Woof, woof, woof?"

Lily said, "Yes, that's it! Now, let's sing a song about the bone. Like this: woof, woof, woof, we have a bone, woof, woof, woof, we are not alone, woof, woof, woof, we can be friends, woof, woof, woof, until the end!"

The big dog said, "Woof, woof, woof, we have a bone, woof, woof, woof, we are not alone, woof, woof, woof, we can be friends, woof, woof, woof, until the end!"

Lily and the big dog sang together. They sang louder and louder, until everyone in the park heard them. They sang until they were tired and hungry. Then, they ate the bone together, and shared it equally. They became friends, and decided to sing every day. They were happy.

Grandma listened to their stories and smiled. She said, "You have very good imaginations, my dears. But I think I know the real story of the boot. It belongs to Mr. Jones, the gardener. Ben and Lila nod. They understand. They thank the man and the bell. They go back to the park. They play with other things. They do not poke the bell anymore. They are good twins.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and water the plants. Lily had a red plant that she loved very much. She gave it a name: Ruby.

One day, Ben saw Ruby and wanted to have it. He said to Lily, "Give me your plant. It is pretty and red. I want it."

Lily was angry. She said, "No, Ben. This is my plant. I found it and I take care of it. You have your own plants. Go away."

Ben did not listen. He tried to grab Ruby from Lily. Lily held on tight. They pulled and tugged. Ruby was hurt. Some of her leaves fell off.

Lily and Ben both started to cry. They heard their mom coming. She saw what happened. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? You are hurting the plant and each other. You need to share and be kind. Say sorry and hug."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said sorry and hugged. They surrendered Ruby to their mom. She said, "I will put Ruby in a pot and give her some water. She will be okay. You can both look at her and talk to her, but you cannot fight over her. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We love Ruby and we love each other." They smiled and went back to play.

One day, Anna said to Sara, "Let's go to the park and play. But we have to be quiet. Mom is sleeping and we don't want to wake her up." Sara nodded and put on her shoes. She followed Anna out of the house and down the street.

The park was big and green. There were swings and slides and a sandbox. Anna ran to the swings and pushed one hard. She jumped on it and swung high in the air. Sara followed her and tried to do the same. But she was too small and scared. She fell off the swing and hurt her knee. She cried out loud.

But on the way back, they saw a big dog. The dog was black and hairy and had sharp teeth. It barked and growled and ran towards them. Anna and Sara were very afraid.
