Tom and Anna liked to play hide and seek in the house. They took turns to count and look for each other. One day, Tom decided to hide in the cabinet in the kitchen. He opened the door and crawled inside. He closed the door and waited for Anna to find him.

Anna counted to ten and shouted, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looked in the living room, the bedroom, and the bathroom, but she could not find Tom. She wondered where he was hiding. She went to the kitchen and saw the cabinet. She thought, maybe Tom is in there.

She opened the cabinet door and saw Tom. He smiled and said, "You found me!" Anna said, "Yes, I did. But why did you hide in there? It is dark and scary." Tom said, "No, it is not. It is safe and cozy. There are pots and pans and plates and cups. They keep me company." Anna said, "But they are not alive. They cannot talk to you or play with you. And what if Mom or Dad need something from the cabinet? They will be surprised to see you in there."

Tom said, "I don't care. I like it here. It is my secret place. You can join me if you want." Anna said, "No, thank you. I don't like it here. It is too small and stuffy. I prefer to play outside or in the toy room. There are more things to do and see. And I don't want to leave Mom and Dad alone. They might worry about us." Tom said, "Fine. Then you can leave. I will stay here." Anna said, "OK. But don't stay too long. It is not good for you. And don't forget to come out when Mom or Dad call us for lunch." She closed the cabinet door and left.

Tom stayed in the cabinet for a while. He pretended that the pots and pans and plates and cups were his friends. He made up stories and songs with them. He had fun. But after some time, he started to feel bored and lonely. He missed Anna and Mom and Dad. He wondered what they were doing. He wanted to play with them. He realized that the cabinet was not so safe and cozy after all. It was just a cabinet. He opened the door and came out. He looked for Anna and Mom and Dad. He found them in the living room. They were happy to see him. They hugged him and asked him where he was. He told them about his hiding place. They laughed and said, "That was a clever idea. But we are glad you came out. We love you and we want you to be with us." Tom said, "I love you too. And I want to be with you too. The cabinet is not my secret place anymore. It is just a cabinet." They smiled and said, "That's right. It is just a cabinet. And you are our precious son." They played and talked and had lunch together. Tom felt happy and warm. He knew he was safe and cozy with his family.

Anna and Ben were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and find shells and stones. They saw a large crab walking on the rocks. They wanted to catch it and look at it.

"Let's go get the crab!" Ben said. He ran towards the rocks with a bucket in his hand.

"Wait for me!" Anna said. She followed him with a net in her hand. She was afraid of the crab. It had big claws and eyes on stalks.

The crab saw the children coming. It did not like them. It wanted to be left alone. It hid under a rock and waited.

Ben reached the rock first. He put his bucket down and lifted the rock. He saw the crab and smiled. He reached for it with his hand.

"Stop!" Anna shouted. She saw something shiny under the sand. She thought it was a shell. She bent down and picked it up.

It was not a shell. It was a whistle. It made a loud noise when she blew it.

The noise scared the crab. It snapped its claws at Ben's hand. Ben screamed and dropped the rock. He ran away from the crab.

The noise also scared a seagull. It was flying over the beach. It saw the crab and thought it was food. It swooped down and grabbed the crab in its beak.

Anna and Ben watched the seagull fly away with the crab. They were sad and surprised. They had lost the crab and the whistle.

They went back to their parents. They told them what happened. Their parents hugged them and gave them ice cream. They said they were brave and lucky.

Anna and Ben felt better. They decided to play with their sandcastle instead. They did not want to catch any more crabs.

But he forgot to turn down the heat. The water boiled and boiled and spilled over the pot. It made a big mess and a lot of smoke. The smoke alarm went off and made a loud noise. Tom got scared and ran to his mom.

"Thank you, chef Lily. This looks delicious," the teddy bear says.

"Here is your rice with cheese and ham, madam," Max says, giving a plate to his doll. "This is the best dish in the town!"

"Thank you, chef Max. This smells wonderful," the doll says.

Lily and Max look at each other's dishes and start to argue. They think their own dish is better and more tasty. They try to convince their customers to switch plates.

"Hey, teddy bear, do you want to try my rice with cheese and ham? It is much more yummy than Lily's rice with chicken and broccoli," Max says.

"No, thank you, chef Max. I like Lily's dish. It has more vegetables and protein," the teddy bear says.

"Hey, doll, do you want to try my rice with chicken and broccoli? It is much more healthy and colorful than Max's rice with cheese and ham," Lily says.

"No, thank you, chef Lily. I like Max's dish. It has more cheese and flavor," the doll says.

Lily and Max get angry and start to throw rice at each other. They make a big mess in their room. Their mom hears the noise and comes to see what is going on.

"What are you doing, Lily and Max? Why are you wasting the rice and making a mess?" their mom asks.

Lily and Max stop throwing rice and look at their mom. They feel sorry and ashamed.

"We are sorry, mom. We were playing pretend and we got competitive. We wanted to make the best dishes with rice, but we forgot to have fun and share," Lily says.

"We are sorry, mom. We were playing pretend and we got competitive. We wanted to impress our customers, but we forgot to be nice and respectful," Max says.

Their mom smiles and hugs them.

"It's okay, Lily and Max. I'm glad you like to play pretend and be creative. But you also have to remember to be kind and cooperative. You can make different dishes with rice, but you can also try each other's dishes and learn from each other. And you have to clean up after yourselves," their mom says.

Lily and Max nod and agree.

"Okay, mom. We will clean up the mess and we will try each other's dishes. And we will say sorry to our customers," Lily says.

"Okay, mom. We will clean up the mess and we will try each other's dishes. And we will say thank you to our customers," Max says.

Lily and Max start to clean up the rice and the toys. They also apologize and thank their teddy bear and their doll. They taste each other's dishes and find out they are both good. They smile and hug each other.

"Your rice with cheese and ham is good, Max. I like the cheese and the ham," Lily says.

"Your rice with chicken and broccoli is good, Lily. I like the chicken and the broccoli," Max says.

They finish their pretend meal and put away their aprons and hats. They decide to play something else. They are still friends who like to play pretend. But they are also friends who like to share and learn.

"Mommy, help me!" she cried. "The zipper is broken!"

Mommy came and looked at the coat. She saw that the zipper was not broken, but it was caught on some fabric. She gently freed the zipper and zipped it up for Lily.

"There you go, sweetie. The zipper is fine. You just have to be careful not to catch it on anything."

Lily smiled and hugged Mommy. Then she looked at the coat again. She wanted to zip it by herself. She reached for the zipper and pulled it down.

"Lily, what are you doing?" Mommy asked. "It's cold outside. You need to keep your coat zipped up."

Lily shook her head. She wanted to play with the zipper. She liked how it made a sound. She insisted on zipping it up and down.

"No, Mommy, I want to zip it!" she said.

Mommy sighed. She knew that Lily was curious and liked to learn new things. But she also knew that the zipper was weak and could break if Lily pulled it too much. She did not want Lily to ruin her new coat.

"Lily, listen to me. The zipper is not a toy. It is a part of your coat. If you zip it too much, it will get tired and stop working. Then you will not be able to wear your coat anymore. Do you want that?"

Lily thought for a moment. She did not want to lose her coat. She liked her coat. It was warm and soft and had a big zipper. She decided to listen to Mommy. She zipped up her coat and left it alone.

"Okay, Mommy, I will not zip it too much. I will be gentle with the zipper. Thank you for helping me."

Mommy smiled and kissed Lily. She was proud of Lily for being smart and polite. She took Lily's hand and they went outside to play. Lily enjoyed the snow and the sun and the sound of the zipper. But she did not zip it too much. She knew that the zipper was weak and needed to rest. She wanted to keep her coat for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a normal car. It liked to drive around the town. One day, the car saw a bag on the road. The car stopped and looked at the bag. It was a big, blue bag. The car wanted to know what was inside.

The car asked a nearby dog, "Dog, what is in the bag?" The dog wagged its tail and said, "I don't know, let's open it!" So, the car and the dog opened the bag together. Inside the bag, they found many toys. There were balls, dolls, and toy cars. They were very happy.

The car and the dog decided to share the toys with their friends. They drove around the town, giving toys to all the animals they met. The animals were very happy to get the toys. At the end of the day, the car and the dog were tired but happy. They had made many new friends because of the big, blue bag.

Once upon a time, there was a furry dog named Max. Max liked to dance to the rhythm of music. One day, Max was dancing in the park when a big cat named Tom came along. Tom did not like Max's dancing. Tom said, "Stop dancing, Max!"

Max felt sad but he didn't want to stop dancing. So, Max came up with an idea. He asked Tom, "Do you want to dance with me?" Tom thought about it and said, "Okay, let's try."

Max and Tom danced together in the park. They found a new rhythm that they both liked. They became good friends and danced together every day.

One day, a little girl named Mia had a quiz at school. She was a bit scared because she did not have a pencil. Her friend Tom saw her looking sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Mia?"

Mia said, "I don't have a pencil for the quiz." Tom wanted to help Mia. He had an extra pencil and said, "I can lend you my pencil, Mia." Mia was very grateful and thanked Tom for his help.

They both took the quiz and did well. After the quiz, Mia gave the pencil back to Tom. They were both happy and went to play together. From that day on, they were best friends because they helped each other.

Once upon a time, in a small world, there lived a persistent little girl named Emma. Emma loved to supply her friends with toys and treats. She would always share her things with others.

One day, a big boy named Tom came to the world. Tom did not like to share. He took all the toys and treats from the other kids. The kids were sad and did not know what to do.

Emma, being persistent, wanted to help her friends. She went to Tom and asked him to share the toys and treats. Tom said no. But Emma did not give up. She asked Tom again and again. Finally, Tom agreed to share the toys and treats with the other kids. The world was happy again, and Emma learned that being persistent can make a big change.

Once upon a time, in a big, big pond, there was a lively hippo. This hippo loved to play all day. He splashed in the water, and he played with his friends, the fish and the frogs.

One day, the lively hippo saw a new friend. It was a small, brown bird. The bird was so pretty! The hippo wanted to play with the bird, but the bird was shy. The bird would fly up high, and then it would vanish!

The hippo was sad. He wanted to play with the bird. So, he thought of a plan. The next time the bird vanished, the hippo hid behind a big rock. When the bird came back, it looked for the hippo, but it could not find him. The bird was sad too.

Then, the lively hippo jumped out from behind the rock. "Boo!" he said. The bird was so surprised! But then, the bird laughed. The hippo and the bird became best friends. They played together all day, every day, and they were very, very happy.

Tim listened to his mother and did not quit. They made the cake together. It was a big, yummy cake. Tim was proud of himself for not quitting. His mother was proud of him too. They had a great birthday party and everyone loved the cake.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a blue vest that he loved to wear. Every day, he would put on his vest and go play outside with his friends.

While playing, Tim saw a small dog. The dog was cold and it started to tremble. Tim wanted to help, so he took off his blue vest and put it on the dog. The dog stopped trembling and wagged its tail. Once upon a time, there was a pirate named Tom. He had a big hat and a ship. Tom was an important pirate. He liked to sail on the sea and find treasure.

One day, Tom found a big box on his ship. The box had a lock. Tom wanted to know what was inside. He found a key and opened the box. Inside the box, there was a little bird.

Tom knew he had to release the bird. He opened the box and let the bird fly away. The bird was happy to be free. It flew high in the sky and sang a pretty song.

From that day on, Tom and the bird were friends. The bird would fly around Tom's ship and help him find treasure. Tom learned that it was important to be kind and help others. And they lived happily ever after.

Lucy and her mom went to the store to buy a battery. When they got home, they put the battery in the car. The car went very fast. Lucy was happy.

Lucy played with the car outside. She called her friend, Tom, to come and play. Tom came and they played with the car together. They had a lot of fun with the high toy car.

One day, a dog named Max was playing in the park. He had a red collar around his neck. Max liked to run and play with his friends because it made him feel healthy.

Max looked for Lily under a big tree, but she was not there. He looked behind a bush, but she was not there either. Then, Max saw a red ribbon on the ground. It looked like Lily's collar. Max followed the ribbon and found Lily hiding behind a rock. "I found you!" said Max. Lily laughed and they both played hide and seek all day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a kind judge. The judge had a big chair and a big table. He helped people when they had problems.

One day, a small cat came to the town. The cat was lost and needed help. The cat went to the judge's big chair and asked for help. The judge wanted to help the small cat.

The judge told the cat to turn left and then turn right to find its home. The small cat did as the judge said. The cat turned left and then turned right. The small cat found its home and was very happy. The judge was happy too, because he helped the small cat.

One day, Bunny went to play outside. She loved to hop in the grass. She saw her friend, Frog, near a bathtub. "Hi, Bunny!" said Frog. Bunny hopped over to Frog and said, "Hi, Frog! What are you doing?"

Frog said, "I found this big bathtub, and I want to fill it with yummy treats!" Bunny liked yummy treats too. They both went to find some. They found apples, bananas, and cookies. They put all the yummy treats in the bathtub.

Later, Bunny and Frog invited their friends to come and see the bathtub full of treats. All their friends were so happy. They all shared the yummy treats and had a great time. Bunny and Frog smiled, knowing they made their friends happy with the bathtub surprise.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were hunters in the jungle. They had a big stick that was their spear. They used it to poke the bushes and the flowers.

"Look, Lily, I see a lion!" Tom said, pointing to a big orange cat that was sleeping under a tree. "Let's catch it with our spear!"

Lily was excited. She wanted to play with the cat. She followed Tom as he crept closer to the cat. He lifted the stick and threw it at the cat.

But the stick missed the cat and hit the tree. The cat woke up and saw the stick. It was angry. It hissed and ran towards Tom and Lily.

"Run, Lily, run!" Tom shouted. He was scared. He grabbed Lily's hand and they ran back to the house.

The cat stopped at the fence and watched them go. It was not a lion. It was just a cat. It did not want to hurt them. It just wanted to sleep. It picked up the stick with its mouth and pulled it back to the tree. It liked the stick. It was its new toy.

Ben and Lily liked to play soldiers. They had toy guns and hats and flags. They ran around the yard and pretended to fight. Sometimes they hid behind trees or bushes. Sometimes they shouted "bang bang" or "you're hit".

One day, they saw a big parade on TV. They saw soldiers in uniforms and cars and trucks and planes. They saw flags and music and people clapping. They wanted to have their own parade. They decided to stop fighting and be friends.

They got their flags and hats and guns and lined up. They marched around the yard and sang a song. They waved to their mom and dad, who watched from the window. They felt happy and proud.

But then, a big gray cloud came over the sky. It started to rain. The rain was cold and wet. It made their flags and hats and guns soggy. It made their clothes and shoes muddy. It made them shiver and frown.

"Let's go inside," Ben said. "This is no fun."

"OK," Lily said. "But first, we have to surrender."

"Surrender? What's that?" Ben asked.

"It means we give up and say sorry," Lily said. "We have to do that when we stop fighting."

"OK," Ben said. "But who do we surrender to?"

They looked around and saw their dog, Spot. He was barking and wagging his tail. He liked the rain. He wanted to play.

They ran to Spot and hugged him. They said, "We surrender, Spot. We're sorry we fought. You're our friend."

Spot licked their faces and wagged his tail more. He was happy. He led them to the door. They went inside and dried off. They had hot chocolate and cookies. They watched the parade on TV again. They smiled and said, "That was a good parade. Maybe we can do it again when it's sunny."

Sara and Ben went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Sara found a big shell that was shiny and pink. She was very happy and showed it to Ben.

"Look, Ben, I found a pretty shell!" Sara said.

Ben looked at the shell and smiled. He liked it too. He wanted to find a shell like that. He looked around and saw a small shell that was gray and smooth. He picked it up and showed it to Sara.

"Look, Sara, I found a modest shell!" Ben said.

Sara looked at the shell and frowned. She did not like it. She thought it was boring and plain. She wanted Ben to find a better shell.

"That is not a good shell, Ben. It is too small and dull. You should choose another shell," Sara said.

Ben felt sad. He liked his shell. He thought it was nice and simple. He did not want to choose another shell.

"But I like this shell, Sara. It is modest and smooth. I do not need a big and shiny shell," Ben said.

Sara and Ben did not agree. They argued about their shells. Mom and Dad heard them and came over.

"What is wrong, Sara and Ben?" Mom asked.

"Sara does not like my shell. She says it is not good. She wants me to choose another shell," Ben said.

"Ben does not like my shell. He says it is too modest. He wants me to choose a small and dull shell," Sara said.

Mom and Dad looked at their shells. They saw that they were different, but both beautiful.

"Sara and Ben, you both have lovely shells. They are different, but that is okay. You can choose the shell that you like best. There is no right or wrong shell. You can be happy with your own shell and respect the other's choice," Mom said.

Sara and Ben thought about what Mom said. They realized that Mom was right. They did not have to argue about their shells. They could like different shells and still be friends.

They hugged each other and said sorry.

"Sorry, Ben. I was mean to you. Your shell is modest and nice. You can keep it if you like it," Sara said.

"Sorry, Sara. I was rude to you. Your shell is shiny and pretty. You can keep it if you like it," Ben said.

They smiled and thanked Mom and Dad. They decided to share their shells and look for more. They had fun at the beach and learned to be kind and respectful.

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and hide. They saw a big hole in the ground. It was a well. They wanted to look inside.

"Be careful," Sara said. "The well is deep and dark. You might fall in."

"I'm not scared," Tom said. "I want to see what is in there. Maybe there is water or a frog or a treasure."

He went closer to the well and leaned over. He saw something shiny at the bottom. He reached out his hand to grab it.

"Tom, no!" Sara shouted. "That is too far. You will slip and hurt yourself."

But Tom did not listen. He wanted the shiny thing. He stretched his arm more and more. He lost his balance and fell into the well.

Sara screamed. She ran to the well and looked down. She saw Tom lying on the ground. He was not moving. She was very scared and sad.

"Tom, Tom, can you hear me?" she cried. "Are you okay? Please wake up."

She heard a groan. Tom opened his eyes. He was hurt and dirty, but he was alive. He saw the shiny thing next to him. It was a metal lid. He had tried to remove it from the well.

"Sara, I'm sorry," he said. "I was silly and greedy. I wanted the shiny thing, but it was nothing. It was just a lid. I should have listened to you. You are a good friend."

Sara was happy to hear his voice. She was still worried about him. She ran to the house and called for help. She told her mom and dad what happened. They came with a rope and a bucket. They lowered the bucket into the well and told Tom to get in. They pulled him up and hugged him. They were glad he was safe.

They took him to the doctor. The doctor checked him and gave him a bandage and a lollipop. He said Tom was lucky. He had only a few bruises and scratches. He said Tom should be more careful and not play near the well.

Tom learned his lesson. He said sorry to Sara and his mom and dad. He said he would never go near the well again. He said he did not want the shiny thing anymore. He said he wanted something different. He wanted a book. He wanted to learn new words and stories. He wanted to be smart and kind. Sara smiled and gave him a hug. She said she would read with him. They were still friends. They were happy.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to ride on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. One day, they saw a new thing in the park. It was a big yellow bike with a basket and a bell. They wanted to ride on it.

"Can we ride on the bike?" Ben asked Mia.

"I don't know. Maybe it belongs to someone," Mia said.

They looked around, but they did not see anyone. They decided to try the bike. Ben got on the seat and Mia got in the basket. They rang the bell and pedaled away.

They had fun riding on the bike. They went around the park and saw the trees, the flowers and the birds. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and sang.

But then, they heard a loud voice behind them.

"Hey, you! Stop! That's my bike!" the voice said.

They turned around and saw a woman running after them. She had a long black dress, a pointy hat and a broom. She looked angry and scary.

"It's a witch!" Ben shouted.

"Let's go faster!" Mia said.

They pedaled as fast as they could, but the witch was catching up. She waved her broom and shouted some words. Suddenly, the bike stopped moving. Ben and Mia felt a jolt and fell off the bike.

The witch reached them and grabbed the bike. She glared at them and said, "You naughty children! How dare you take my bike! It's a magic bike, you know. It can fly and turn invisible and do other things. You could have broken it or lost it or worse!"

Ben and Mia were scared and sorry. They did not know it was a magic bike. They did not mean to make the witch angry. They said, "We're sorry, witch. We just wanted to ride on the bike. We thought it was a normal bike. We didn't know it was yours."

The witch looked at them and saw that they were telling the truth. She saw that they were young and curious and did not mean any harm. She softened a little and said, "Well, I suppose you didn't know. But you should always ask before you take something that is not yours. It's not nice to steal. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nodded and said, "We understand. We're sorry, witch. We won't do it again."

The witch smiled and said, "That's good. I forgive you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you won't tell anyone about my bike or me. It's a secret, okay?"

Ben and Mia promised. They said, "We promise, witch. We won't tell anyone. It's a secret."

The witch said, "Good. Then I'll let you go. But remember, be careful and be good. And don't touch things that are not yours. Goodbye, children."

She got on the bike and rang the bell. The bike lifted off the ground and flew away. Ben and Mia watched it disappear in the sky. They were amazed and relieved. They hugged each other and said, "Wow, that was a close one. Let's go home."

They ran back to their parents, who were waiting for them. They did not tell them about the bike or the witch. They kept their promise. They only said, "We had fun in the park. We rode on the swings, the slide and the seesaw."

The end.

Sara and Ben like to play with blocks. They make towers and bridges and houses. Sara has many red blocks. Ben has many blue blocks. They share their blocks and have fun.

One day, Sara wants to make a big red tower. She takes all the red blocks and puts them on top of each other. Ben wants to help, but Sara says no. She says, "These are my red blocks. You can only use blue blocks."

Ben is sad. He says, "That is not fair. We always share our blocks. Why can't I use some red blocks too?"

Sara says, "Because I want to make a big red tower. It is my game. You can play something else."

Ben is angry. He says, "Fine. Then I will quit your game. I will play with my blue blocks by myself. You are not a good friend."

He takes his blue blocks and goes to the other side of the room. He makes a big blue bridge. He does not talk to Sara.

Sara finishes her big red tower. She is proud of it. She looks at Ben. He is not looking at her. He is playing with his blue bridge. She feels lonely. She says, "Ben, I am sorry. I was mean to you. Can we share our blocks again? Can we play together again?"

Ben looks at Sara. He sees her big red tower. He sees her sad face. He says, "OK. I am sorry too. I was mad at you. Your red tower is very nice. Can I help you make it bigger?"

Sara smiles. She says, "Yes, you can. And I can help you make your blue bridge longer. We can use both red and blue blocks. We can make a red and blue city."

They hug and say sorry. They share their blocks and have fun. They are good friends again.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play with their toys. One day, they decided to have a race with their toy cars. They made a row of cars on the floor and said "Ready, set, go!" But Tom cheated and pushed Mia's car away.

"That's not fair!" Mia cried. "You spoiled the race!"

Tom laughed and said "I win, I win!"

Mia felt sorry for Tom and said "I'm sorry, I tied your shoelaces. It was a bad thing to do."

Lon was a cop. He liked to help people and catch bad guys. But he was lonely. He did not have any friends at work or at home. He only had his car and his radio.

One day, he saw a little girl crying on the street. She had lost her mom and did not know where to go. Lon stopped his car and got out. He asked her, "What is your name? Why are you sad?"

The girl said, "My name is Mia. I was with my mom at the store, but she went away and I can't find her. I'm scared."

Lon said, "Don't worry, Mia. I will help you find your mom. Come with me. You can sit in my car and talk to me on the radio. Maybe someone will hear us and tell us where your mom is."

Mia nodded and followed Lon. She got in his car and put on a seat belt. Lon gave her his radio and said, "This is how you use it. You press this button and say, 'Hello, this is Mia. I'm looking for my mom. Can you help me?' Then you let go of the button and listen. Maybe someone will answer you."

Mia tried it. She said, "Hello, this is Mia. I'm looking for my mom. Can you help me?" She let go of the button and waited.

After a few seconds, she heard a voice. It said, "Hello, Mia. This is Sam. I'm a cop too. I know where your mom is. She is at the police station. She is looking for you too. She is very worried. Can you tell me where you are?"

Mia was happy. She said, "I'm with Lon. He is a cop too. He is very nice. He found me on the street and took me in his car. He gave me his radio. We are on Main Street, near the park. Can you come and get us?"

Sam said, "Yes, I can. I'm on my way. Stay with Lon. He will keep you safe. I'll be there soon."

Mia said, "Thank you, Sam. You are very nice too. I can't wait to see my mom."

Lon smiled. He was glad he had helped Mia. He was also glad he had met Sam. He hoped they could be friends. He said, "Mia, you are very brave and smart. I'm happy you are with me. You know what? You can keep my radio. It's a gift from me. You can use it to talk to me and Sam anytime you want. We can include you in our team. How do you like that?"

Mia hugged Lon. She said, "I like that very much. Thank you, Lon. You are the best cop ever. You are not lonely anymore. You have me and Sam. We are your friends."

Lily liked to help her dad deliver newspapers every morning. She would wake up early, put on her coat and hat, and hop on her bike. Her dad would put a big bag of newspapers on his bike and follow her.

They would ride around the neighborhood and stop at each house. Lily would take one newspaper from the bag and run to the door. She would put the newspaper on the porch or in the mailbox. Sometimes she would ring the bell and say "Good morning!" to the people who opened the door.

One day, as they were delivering newspapers, they saw a big dog on the street. The dog was barking and running towards them. Lily was scared and dropped her newspaper. Her dad told her to stay calm and get back on her bike.

"Don't worry, Lily, it's just a friendly dog. He won't hurt us. He just wants to play," her dad said.

But the dog did not look friendly. He looked angry and hungry. He jumped on Lily's bike and tried to bite her leg. Lily screamed and kicked the dog. Her dad threw a newspaper at the dog and shouted "Go away!"

The dog let go of Lily's bike and ran away. Lily and her dad quickly got on their bikes and rode away. They were both shaken and relieved.

"Are you okay, Lily?" her dad asked.

"I'm okay, dad. That was a bad dog. He scared me," Lily said.

"I'm sorry, Lily. That was a very brave thing you did. You are a helpful and strong girl. I'm proud of you," her dad said.

They hugged and continued to deliver the rest of the newspapers. They were glad they had each other.

Lily and Ben are playing pirates in the garden. They have a big box that is their ship, and a flag with a skull on it. They also have some old clothes and scarves to wrap around their heads and arms.

"Ahoy, matey!" Ben says to Lily. "Are you ready to sail the seven seas and find treasure?"

"Yes, captain!" Lily says. "But where is the treasure map?"

Ben looks around and sees a piece of paper on the ground. He picks it up and pretends it is a map. "Here it is!" he says. "It shows us where the treasure is buried. We have to follow the X."

He shows the paper to Lily, who nods. They get into their box and pretend to row with sticks. They make noises like waves and wind. They have fun.

But then, Ben sees a big dog running towards them. It is the neighbor's dog, Spot. Spot likes to play, but he is very clumsy. He does not see the box or the flag. He jumps on them and knocks them over.

"Ah!" Ben and Lily scream. "It's a sea monster!"

Spot licks their faces and wags his tail. He thinks they are playing too. He grabs the flag with his mouth and runs away.

"Hey, come back!" Ben shouts. "That's our flag! That's our skull!"

He and Lily get out of the box and chase after Spot. They try to get their flag back, but Spot is too fast. He runs around the garden, dragging the flag and the skull.

Lily and Ben are sad. They lose their flag and their treasure map. They go back to their box and sit down.

"Maybe we can make another flag," Lily says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But it won't be the same."

They look at each other and sigh. They are not happy pirates anymore.

Lily was a lively girl who liked to run and jump and play. She had a baby brother named Tom who was an infant. He was very small and quiet and slept a lot. Lily loved Tom, but sometimes she did not know how to play with him.

One day, Lily wanted to show Tom her new doll. She ran to his crib and lifted him up. She said, "Look, Tom, this is my doll. She is pretty and soft and has a dress. Do you like her?" But Tom did not say anything. He just made a funny face and started to cry.

Lily was worried. She did not want to make Tom cry. She did not know what to do. She put him back in his crib and ran to find Mom. She said, "Mom, Mom, I made Tom cry. I showed him my doll, but he did not like her. He made a funny face and cried. Why did he do that? Is he sick? Is he mad at me?"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "No, Lily, Tom is not sick or mad at you. He is just an infant. He does not understand what a doll is. He does not know how to talk or play like you. He cries when he is hungry or tired or needs a diaper change. He does not mean to hurt your feelings. He loves you, too."

Lily felt better. She said, "Oh, I see. Tom is an infant. He is different from me. He needs Mom to take care of him. But I can still love him and give him kisses and hugs, right?" Mom said, "Of course, Lily. You are a good sister. You can love him and give him kisses and hugs. And when he grows up, he will learn how to talk and play with you. He will be your best friend."

Lily smiled. She said, "I can't wait for that. I love Tom. He is my baby brother." She ran back to his crib and gave him a kiss and a hug. Tom stopped crying and smiled back at her. He made a happy sound. Lily said, "Look, Mom, he likes me. He is happy." Mom said, "Yes, Lily, he likes you. He is happy. And so am I."

Sam likes to make things with wire. He can bend and twist the wire into shapes and animals. He hopes to show his mom his wire art when she comes home from work.

"I like this one. It is bright like the sky. Do you want to trade?" Ben asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She liked the blue marble too, but she liked the red one more. She shook her head and said, "No, thank you. I want to keep my red marble. It is very pretty."

Ben felt sad. He wanted the red marble too. He thought it was not fair that Lily had it. He decided to take it from her. He waited until Lily was not looking and grabbed the red marble from her hand.

"No, it is mine now. I like it more than you. You have many other marbles. You don't need this one." Ben said.

Just then, the sun started to go down and the night was getting dark. Liza's parents knew it was time to go. They tried to be gentle, but told her she had to go. 

Liza was sad, and said, "I'm sorry." She knew it was time to go, but part of her still wanted to stay. 

Her parents hugged her and said, "It's okay, sweetie. You can come back and play again soon. That's how life works." 

So, Liza hugged her parents, and they all went home together.

Timmy loved the idea of packing. He ran to his room and started putting his toys in a cardboard box. "Look, Mom!" he said. "I'm packing, too!"

His mom smiled and said, "That's cool, Timmy. You're such a big helper." And they continued to pack up their things, knowing that soon they would have a new home to explore together.

"Hello, Carl!" said Timmy. "Do you want to play in the sand with me?" 

"Yes, I do!" said Carl. "But be careful, Timmy. The tide is coming in soon." 

Timmy didn't know what Carl meant by "tide," but he kept playing in the sand. He built a long tunnel that went all the way to the water. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. 

"Timmy, the tide is coming in!" shouted Carl. "We have to leave now!" 

Timmy looked up and saw the water getting closer and closer to his tunnel. He quickly grabbed Carl and ran away from the beach. As they walked away, Timmy looked back and saw that his tunnel had disappeared. 

"The sand is gone!" he said sadly. 

"Yes," said Carl. "But remember, Timmy, all good things must come to an end."

Tom thought it was a good idea. He nodded and smiled. They sneaked out of the door and ran to the fountain. They picked up some ice from the ground and threw it at the water. They laughed and clapped as the water splashed and sparkled.

But they did not see the sign that said, "Do not touch the fountain. It is very cold and slippery." They also did not see their mom and dad looking for them. They were worried and angry.

Suddenly, Lily slipped on the ice and fell into the fountain. She screamed and shivered. Tom tried to help her, but he also slipped and fell. They were both wet and cold and scared.

Their mom and dad heard their screams and ran to the fountain. They pulled them out and wrapped them in warm blankets. They scolded them for being naughty and careless. They said, "You should not joke with the fountain. It is not funny. It is dangerous. You could have hurt yourself or others. You should listen to the signs and stay with us."

Lily and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They apologized to their mom and dad. They said, "We are sorry. We did not mean to be bad. We just wanted to have fun. We will not joke with the fountain again. We will be good and careful."

Their mom and dad hugged them and forgave them. They said, "We love you. We are glad you are safe. But you have to learn from your mistake. Joking is fun, but not when it is harmful or rude. You have to respect the rules and the people around you."

Lily and Tom nodded and learned their lesson. They went back to the restaurant and had a nice dinner. They sang happy birthday to their mom and gave her a big kiss. They were happy and grateful. They did not joke with the fountain anymore.

Lily and Tom were playing with their baby brother, Ben. They liked to make him laugh and smile. They gave him toys and books and sang songs to him. Ben was a lovely baby with big blue eyes and soft brown hair.

One day, Lily and Tom found a feather in the garden. They thought it would be fun to tickle Ben with it. They took turns to gently touch the feather to his nose, his ears and his chin. Ben giggled and cooed. He liked the feather.

But then, something happened. Ben felt a tickle in his nose. He wrinkled his nose and opened his mouth. He sneezed very loudly. "Achoo!" he said.

Lily and Tom were surprised. They had never heard Ben sneeze before. They looked at him and saw that he had a wet nose and tears in his eyes. They felt sorry for him.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Lily asked. "Did the feather make you sneeze?"

Tom gave Ben a tissue and wiped his nose. He hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Ben. We love you. We won't tickle you with the feather anymore."

Ben smiled and snuggled with Tom. He felt better. He said, "Thank you, Lily. Thank you, Tom. You are lovely."

One day, Lily and Tom go to the park with their moms. They bring their cards with them. They find a bench and start to play. They have fun and laugh.

But then, they hear a loud noise. It is a big truck. The truck is noisy and dirty. It comes near the bench. Lily and Tom are scared. They drop their cards. The cards fly in the air.

"Look out!" Lily's mom shouts. "Hurry! Grab your cards!"

Lily and Tom hurry. They try to catch their cards. But some cards fall on the ground. Some cards go under the truck. Some cards are lost.

Lily and Tom are sad. They have no cards to play with. They cry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom says. "I'm sorry, Tom," Lily says.

Their moms hug them. They say, "It's OK. It was an accident. You can share your cards. You can still play together. You are good friends."

Lily and Tom nod. They smile. They share their cards. They play together. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Accidents happen. Friendship is important.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a microscope in the attic. It was a tool that made small things look big. They wanted to see what it could do.

"Let me see first!" Lily said. She grabbed the microscope and put a leaf under it.

"No, me first!" Sam said. He pulled the microscope away from Lily and put a feather under it.

They both wanted to see, but they did not share. They fought over the microscope and made a lot of noise.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She came to the attic and saw them fighting. She was not happy. "Why are you fighting over the microscope? You can both see if you take turns. Fighting is not nice. Sharing is nice."

She took the microscope and showed them how to use it. She told them to yield, which meant to let the other one see. She also told them to say please and thank you. She showed them some unusual things under the microscope, like a hair, a bug, and a coin. They were amazed by what they saw.

"Wow, this is so cool!" Lily said. She yielded the microscope to Sam and said, "Please, can you show me the bug?"

"Sure, here you go!" Sam said. He yielded the microscope to Lily and said, "Thank you, can you show me the coin?"

They both learned to share and to be polite. They had fun with the microscope and saw many new things. They also made Mom happy. They realized that sharing was better than fighting.

Sam and Mia nodded. They understood. They wanted the bridge to be safe too. They asked the man how long it would take to fix the bridge.

Tom and Sam were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Tom found a big red worm and showed it to Sam.

"Look, Sam, I found a red worm! It is so long and wiggly!" Tom said.

"Wow, Tom, that is a cool worm! Can I hold it?" Sam asked.

"Okay, but be careful. Don't hurt it," Tom said. He gave the worm to Sam.

Sam held the worm in his hand. He felt it move and tickle his palm. He smiled and laughed. Then he had an idea. He wanted to see what the worm would do if he pulled it.

"Hey, Tom, watch this!" Sam said. He pulled the worm with both hands.

The worm snapped in half. Sam dropped the pieces on the ground. He saw the worm's guts come out. He felt sick and scared.

"Sam, what did you do? You broke the worm! That is mean and bad!" Tom shouted.

"I'm sorry, Tom, I didn't mean to. I just wanted to play. I regret it now," Sam said. He started to cry.

Tom was angry and sad. He liked the worm. He picked up the pieces and buried them in the dirt. He said a prayer for the worm.

"Goodbye, red worm. I'm sorry Sam hurt you. You were a good worm," Tom said.

He looked at Sam. Sam was still crying. Tom felt sorry for him. He knew Sam was his friend. He decided to forgive him.

"It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. But don't ever do that again. Worms are living things. They feel pain. You have to be gentle and kind to them," Tom said.

"Thank you, Tom. I'm sorry. I will be gentle and kind to worms from now on. You are a good friend," Sam said.

They hugged and made up. They went back to playing in the garden. They hoped to find more worms, but not red ones. They were too sad to see red worms.

The bunny was so excited that she began to jump around. She and the gopher watched as twigs fell everywhere in a circle around them. Then, all of a sudden, the twigs began to move.

The bunny and the gopher gasped. They were so amazed! The twigs moved around in a funny way, spinning and changing colors. It was like a mini, colorful twig show!

The bunny and the gopher watched the twig show until it ended. They both wondered what it was, but neither of them could find out. 

But that didn't matter. They enjoyed the show, and had lots of fun together!

Day by day the boy practiced the piano. He realized that the old man was right. Soon he could play and make music. He was so happy! He thanked the wise old man for his advice and he invited the old man to listen to him play the piano.

"Okay," he said.

"Help! Help!" they cried. They banged on the walls of the box, but no one heard them. They hugged each other and tried to comfort each other. "It's okay, we'll get out soon," Lily said. "Don't worry, we're brave," Ben said.

They remembered that the box was flexible. They pushed and pulled and twisted the box until they made a hole. They crawled out of the hole and saw their mom and dad. They ran to them and hugged them. They were happy and relieved.

"Are you okay, sweeties?" their mom asked. "What happened?"

"We were playing spaceship, but the box fell over and we got stuck," Lily explained.

"That sounds scary. I'm sorry we didn't hear you. We were busy in the kitchen," their dad said.

"It's okay, we got out by ourselves. We were flexible," Ben said.

"That's very smart and brave of you. But next time, be careful with the box. It's not very stable," their mom said.

"We will, mom. We learned our lesson. The box is not a good spaceship," Lily said.

They smiled and kissed their parents. They decided to play something else. They still liked the box, but they used it for something safer. They made it into a fort. They had fun and stayed safe.

The end.

Tom was a young boy who liked to move a lot. He liked to run, jump, climb and play with his toys. But at night, he had to sleep in his crib. His crib was big and cozy, but Tom did not like it. He wanted to sleep in a big bed like his mom and dad.

One night, Tom had an idea. He saw a chair near his crib. He climbed out of his crib and moved the chair to the door. He stood on the chair and reached for the doorknob. He opened the door and walked out of his room. He was very quiet and careful. He did not want to wake up his mom and dad.

He went to their room and saw their big bed. It looked so soft and warm. He moved a pillow and made some space for himself. He crawled into the bed and snuggled with his mom and dad. He felt happy and sleepy. He closed his eyes and smiled.

But soon, he heard a noise. It was his mom. She woke up and saw Tom in the bed. She was surprised and a little angry.

"Tom, what are you doing here?" she asked. "You should be sleeping in your crib. It is not safe for you to move around the house at night. You could get hurt or lost."

Tom opened his eyes and looked at his mom. He felt sad and scared. He did not want to make his mom angry. He did not want to go back to his crib. He wanted to stay with his mom and dad.

"Please, mom, can I sleep with you?" he begged. "I don't like my crib. It is too small and lonely. I like your bed. It is big and cozy. I love you and dad. Please, mom, please."

His mom looked at his face and felt sorry for him. She remembered how she used to feel when she was young and afraid of the dark. She hugged him and kissed him.

"Okay, Tom, you can sleep with us tonight. But only tonight. Tomorrow, you have to go back to your crib. And you have to promise me that you will not move out of your crib again. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I understand. Thank you, mom. I love you."

He cuddled with his mom and dad and fell asleep. He had a good dream. He dreamed that he had a big bed of his own. And he could move as much as he wanted.

"But they are not pets. They are wild. They need to run and climb and play with other squirrels. They need to be free," Mia says. She is right and smart.

"Who cares? They are just squirrels. They are easy to catch and sell. If you don't want to buy one, go away," the man says. He is rude and greedy.

Sam and Mia are sad and mad. They want to help the squirrels, but they don't know how. They look around and see a big tree nearby. They have an idea.

"Hey, mister. Can we see the squirrels closer? Maybe we will buy one," Sam says. He pretends to be interested.

"Sure, kid. But don't touch them. They might bite," the man says. He thinks he can trick them.

He brings his bag closer to Sam and Mia. They pretend to look at the squirrels, but they are really looking for a chance to act. When the man is not paying attention, they grab the bag and run to the tree. They open the bag and let the squirrels out. The squirrels are happy and grateful. They scamper up the tree and thank Sam and Mia with squeaks and chirps.

"Hey, stop! Give me back my squirrels!" the man shouts. He is angry and shocked.

He tries to chase them, but he is too slow and clumsy. He trips and falls on the ground. He hurts his nose and his pride.

Sam and Mia laugh and cheer. They are proud and happy. They have saved the squirrels and taught the man a lesson. They hug each other and the tree. They are heroes and friends.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and made pictures of animals, flowers and people. She was very good at drawing and her mom and dad always praised her.

One day, she wanted to draw a picture of a cow. She found a white crayon and a black crayon and started to draw on a big paper. She made a round body, four legs, a tail, a head and two horns. Then she added some black spots and a smile.

She was very happy with her cow, but she thought it needed something more. She remembered that cows gave milk, and she liked to drink milk. She decided to draw a bucket of milk next to the cow. She looked for a blue crayon, but she could not find one. She saw a blue marker on the table and thought it was the same.

She took the marker and drew a bucket with a handle. Then she filled it with blue. She did not know that the marker was not for paper, but for whiteboards. It was very wet and made the paper soggy. She tried to wipe it with her hand, but it only made it worse.

She started to cry. She had ruined her picture. She wanted to show it to her mom and dad, but now it was ugly. She threw the marker on the floor and ran to her room.

Her mom heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the paper on the table and the marker on the floor. She understood what had happened. She picked up the paper and the marker and followed Lily to her room.

She knocked on the door and said, "Lily, can I come in?"

Lily sniffed and said, "No, go away. I don't want to see you."

Her mom said, "Please, Lily, let me in. I want to talk to you. I want to see your picture."

Lily said, "No, you don't. It's ugly. I messed it up. I used the wrong thing. I'm sorry."

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. It was a mistake. You didn't know. It's not your fault. I'm sure your picture is still beautiful. Can I see it?"

Lily hesitated, but then opened the door. She gave her mom the paper and said, "Here. It's a cow and a bucket of milk. But the milk is blue and the paper is wet."

Her mom looked at the picture and smiled. She said, "Wow, Lily, this is a very attractive picture. I love your cow. It has such a nice smile and such cute spots. And the bucket of milk is very creative. You used a different color and made it look like water. It's very clever."

Lily looked at her mom and said, "Really? You like it?"

Her mom said, "Yes, I do. I think it's wonderful. And you know what? The paper will dry soon and the marker will come off. Then you can hang it on the fridge or on the wall. I'm very proud of you, Lily. You are a great artist."

Lily smiled and hugged her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are the best."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best."

Anna liked to match things. She matched her socks, her toys, her books. She matched everything she could find. One day, she found a camera in her dad's drawer. She had never seen a camera before. She wondered what it could match.

She took the camera and went to the living room. She saw a picture of her family on the wall. She thought the camera could match the picture. She held the camera next to the picture and said, "Look, mom, I matched the camera and the picture!"

Mom looked at Anna and smiled. She said, "That's very clever, Anna, but the camera is not for matching. The camera is for taking pictures. It is a rare camera. It belonged to your grandpa. He gave it to me before he went to heaven. It is very special to me."

Anna looked at the camera and felt sorry. She did not know it was rare and special. She said, "I'm sorry, mom, I did not mean to hurt the camera. Can I take a picture with it?"

Mom hugged Anna and said, "It's okay, Anna, you did not hurt the camera. You can take a picture with it, but be careful. It is not like the phone. It has film inside. You can only take a few pictures. Then you have to wait for them to be printed. Do you want to take a picture of us?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I want to take a picture of us. Then we can match the picture and the camera again!"

Mom laughed and said, "Okay, Anna, let's take a picture. Say cheese!"

Anna and mom smiled and said, "Cheese!" Anna pressed the button and the camera flashed. She was happy. She had taken a picture with the rare camera. She hoped it would be a good match.

Lily was a princess who lived in a big castle. She had many toys and dresses and books, but she was not happy. She was lazy and did not like to do anything. She did not help her parents, the king and the queen, or her friends, the servants and the guards. She only wanted to play and eat and sleep.

One day, a fairy came to visit Lily. She saw how lazy Lily was and decided to teach her a lesson. She said, "Lily, you are a princess, but you do not act like one. You do not provide any help or kindness to anyone. You only think of yourself. That is not good. I will give you a magic wand, but you have to use it wisely. If you use it to help others, it will make you happy. If you use it to be lazy, it will make you sad. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded, but she did not really listen. She took the magic wand and ran to her room. She thought, "This is great! Now I can do whatever I want with this wand. I can make more toys and dresses and books. I can make food and drinks appear. I can make my bed and clean my room. I do not have to do anything by myself."

She waved the wand and said, "Wand, wand, do as I say. Make me happy every day." But the wand did not do what she wanted. Instead, it made her toys and dresses and books disappear. It made her food and drinks taste bad. It made her bed and room messy. It made her feel sad and lonely.

Lily cried and cried. She did not know what to do. She ran to the fairy and said, "Fairy, fairy, please help me. The wand is not working. It is making me unhappy. What can I do?"

The fairy smiled and said, "Lily, you have to learn to use the wand wisely. You have to provide help and kindness to others. You have to think of others, not only yourself. That is what makes a princess happy. Do you want to try again?"

Lily nodded, but she was not sure. She said, "But how can I help others? I do not know how."

The fairy said, "You can start by saying sorry to your parents and your friends. You can ask them what they need and how you can help. You can use the wand to make them happy, not yourself. You can share your toys and dresses and books. You can play and eat and sleep with them. You can be a good princess."

Lily thought about it and decided to try. She said, "Okay, fairy, I will try. Thank you for the wand and the lesson. I hope I can make you proud."

She went to her parents and her friends and said sorry. She asked them what they needed and how she could help. She used the wand to make them happy, not herself. She shared her toys and dresses and books. She played and ate and slept with them. She was a good princess.

She felt happy and warm. She saw the fairy smiling at her. She said, "Fairy, fairy, thank you for the wand and the lesson. You made me happy. You are my friend."

The fairy hugged her and said, "You are welcome, Lily. You made me happy too. You are my friend. And you are a true princess."

Lily and Max were twins who loved to play together. They liked to make up stories and act them out with their toys. One day, they decided to pretend they were explorers in a cold and snowy land. They put on their hats and scarves and grabbed their backpacks.

"Let's go find a cave to hide in," Max said. "Maybe we'll see some bears or penguins."

"Or maybe we'll find a treasure," Lily said. "Or a magic wand."

They walked around the living room, pretending it was a frozen forest. They dodged the sofa, which was a big rock, and the table, which was a frozen lake. They climbed over the cushions, which were snowy hills. They made noises like animals and wind.

They came to the fireplace, which was off. They decided it was a cave entrance. They peeked inside and saw some logs and ashes.

"Look, there's a fire in the cave," Lily said. "Maybe someone lives here."

"Or maybe it's a trap," Max said. "Maybe there's a monster inside."

They were both curious and scared. They wanted to see what was in the cave, but they also wanted to be safe. They looked at each other and nodded. They held hands and walked slowly into the fireplace.

They were surprised by what they saw. There was no fire, no monster, no treasure, no magic wand. There was only a weird thing that looked like a big metal box with wires and buttons. It had a sticker that said "Do not touch".

"What is this?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Max said. "It looks weird."

They touched the box and felt a shock. They screamed and ran out of the fireplace. They fell on the floor and hugged each other.

"Are you okay?" Lily asked.

"I think so," Max said. "That was scary."

They heard their mom coming. She had heard their scream and was worried. She saw them on the floor, dirty and scared.

"What happened?" she asked. "What were you doing in the fireplace?"

"We were playing explorers," Lily said. "We found a weird thing in the cave."

Mom looked at the fireplace and saw the box. She gasped and ran to it. She pulled it out and unplugged it. It was an old heater that dad had forgotten to throw away. It was broken and dangerous.

"Kids, this is not a toy," she said. "This is a heater. It can hurt you. You should never go in the fireplace. It's not safe."

She hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were not hurt.

"We're sorry, mom," Lily and Max said. "We didn't know."

"It's okay, sweeties," mom said. "I love you. But please, don't play in the fireplace again. Okay?"

"Okay, mom," Lily and Max said.

They learned their lesson. They never played in the fireplace again. They found other places to play and other stories to make up. They still loved to be explorers, but they also loved to be safe.

They resist each other, but they are not strong enough. They start to cry and shout.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Lila and Ben fighting over the stamp and the train.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks.

"Lila took my train!" Ben says.

"Ben took my stamp!" Lila says.

Mom sighs and shakes her head. She takes the stamp and the train from Lila and Ben.

Lila and Ben nod and wipe their tears. They agree to share and take turns. Mom gives them back the stamp and the train.

"Thank you, Mom," Lila and Ben say.

Mom smiles and hugs them.

"You're welcome, my loves," Mom says. "Now, play nicely and have fun."

Lily loved to rock on her chair. She rocked back and forth, back and forth, making a squeaky sound. She liked to rock when she was happy, when she was sad, or when she was bored. She rocked so much that her chair became loose and wobbly.

One day, Lily's mom told her to stop rocking. "Lily, you will break your chair if you rock too much. And you will wake your baby brother, who is sleeping in the next room. Please be quiet and still," mom said.

But Lily did not listen. She thought mom was silly and mean. She wanted to rock more and more. She rocked faster and faster, louder and louder, until...CRASH! Her chair broke and she fell on the floor. She hurt her arm and her head. She cried out loud.

Mom heard the noise and ran to Lily. She saw the broken chair and the crying girl. She was angry and worried. She picked up Lily and hugged her. "Lily, why did you not listen to me? I told you to stop rocking. Now you have hurt yourself and your chair. And you have woken your baby brother, who is crying too. How do you feel now?" mom asked.

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She realized she had been naughty and foolish. She had not cared about her mom, her brother, or her chair. She had only cared about rocking. She said, "Mom, I am sorry. I feel bad. I did not listen to you. I rocked too much. I broke my chair. I hurt myself. I woke my brother. I am sorry. Please forgive me."

Mom kissed Lily and said, "I forgive you, Lily. But you have to learn from your mistake. Rocking is fun, but not all the time. You have to be careful and respectful. You have to listen to me and obey me. You have to think about others and not just yourself. Do you understand?" mom said.

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I will be good. I will not rock too much. I will listen to you and obey you. I will think about others and not just myself. I love you, mom. And I love my brother. And I love my chair, even if it is broken."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love your brother. And I love your chair, even if it is broken. You are my brilliant girl. But now, let's go and calm your brother. And then, we will fix your chair. And then, we will rock together, but gently and quietly."

Timmy looked at the thing and said, "I don't like it. It looks dangerous." 

Lily didn't want to believe her friend, but she also didn't want to get hurt. So, she decided to cover the thing with a big leaf and leave it alone.

"Can we help it?" Mia asked Ben.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe we can give it some water and food."

They found a plastic cup and a plastic plate in their toy box. They filled the cup with water from the tap and put some bread on the plate. They brought them to the bird and put them near its beak.

"Here, birdie, drink and eat," Mia said softly. "We want you to feel better."

The bird opened its eyes and looked at them. It made a small noise. It tried to drink some water and eat some bread. Ben and Mia smiled. They hoped the bird would get well soon.

They decided to make a nest for the bird with some plastic grass and leaves. They lay the bird gently on the nest and covered it with a plastic cloth. They stayed with the bird and talked to it. They told it their names and their toys' names. They told it stories and jokes. They made the bird feel loved and safe.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and smell them. Lily saw a big purple flower that was not open yet. She wanted to see it bloom.

"Look, Ben, this flower is not open. When will it bloom?" she asked.

Ben shrugged. He did not know. He saw a shiny rock near the flower. He picked it up and showed it to Lily.

"Look, Lily, this is a mineral. It is hard and sparkly. Do you like it?" he asked.

Lily nodded. She liked the mineral. It was pretty. She touched it with her finger.

"Can I have it, Ben?" she asked.

Ben smiled. He liked to share with Lily. He gave her the mineral.

"Here you go, Lily. You can have it. It is a gift for you," he said.

Lily hugged Ben. She was happy. She thanked him for the gift.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I will keep the mineral in my pocket," she said.

They heard a loud noise. They turned around and saw the purple flower open. It was big and beautiful. It had many petals and a yellow center. They gasped.

"Wow, the flower bloomed! It is so pretty!" they said together.

They ran to the flower and admired it. They smelled it and touched it gently. They laughed and clapped.

They heard another noise. It was their mom calling them for lunch. They looked at each other and smiled.

"Let's go, Lily. Mom has made sandwiches for us. We can come back later and see the flower again," Ben said.

"OK, Ben. Let's go. Maybe we will see more flowers bloom. That would be fun," Lily said.

They held hands and ran to the house. They were hungry and happy. They had a silly and fun morning in the garden.

Sam was a little boy who liked to play with his cars and trucks. He had a red vest that he wore every day, because it was his favorite. He liked to zoom his cars on the floor and make loud noises.

But one day, his mom said, "Sam, it's time for your nap. You need to rest and be patient. You can play with your cars later."

Sam did not want to nap. He wanted to play. He said, "No, mom, no nap. I want to play. Please, mom, please."

His mom was firm. She said, "Sam, you have to nap. It's good for you. You will feel better and have more energy. Come on, let's go to your bed. I will read you a story."

Sam was sad. He did not like to leave his cars. He followed his mom to his bed. He took his red vest with him. He hugged it tight. His mom read him a story about a brave knight and a dragon. Sam liked the story. He felt sleepy.

Soon, he closed his eyes and napped. He dreamed of cars and trucks and knights and dragons. He was happy. His mom smiled and kissed him. She was proud of him. He was a good boy who napped and was patient.

Lily liked to play with her dog, Max. Max was big and brown and very friendly. He liked to run and jump and fetch sticks. Lily and Max had a lot of fun together.

One day, Lily's mom said they were going to have steak for dinner. Lily loved steak. It was juicy and tasty and made her feel strong. She asked her mom if she could give some steak to Max. Her mom said no.

"Steak is for people, not for dogs," her mom said. "Dogs need different food. If you give Max steak, he might get sick."

Lily felt sad. She wanted to share her steak with Max. She thought he would like it too. She looked at Max and saw his big eyes and wagging tail. He looked hungry and hopeful.

"Please, mom, can I give Max a little bit of steak?" Lily begged. "Just a tiny piece. He is my best friend. He always plays with me and makes me happy."

Her mom sighed. She saw how much Lily loved Max. She decided to permit Lily to give Max a little bit of steak. But only a little bit.

"Okay, Lily, you can give Max a little bit of steak. But only a little bit. And only after you finish your own dinner. And you have to promise to brush your teeth afterwards. Deal?"

Lily nodded. She was cheerful. She hugged her mom and said thank you. She ran to Max and told him the good news. Max barked and licked her face. He was cheerful too.

They both waited patiently for dinner. When it was ready, they ate their steak and enjoyed it very much. Lily gave Max a little bit of steak from her plate. Max gobbled it up and wagged his tail. He was very grateful.

Lily and Max were happy. They had steak and they had each other. They were the best friends ever.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, like cars, dolls, blocks and books. But their favorite toy was a big box that they pretended was a spaceship. They would climb inside the box and make noises like zoom, beep and blast.

One day, they found a small box in the kitchen. It had a picture of a fire on it. They were curious and opened the box. Inside, they saw many small sticks with red tips. They did not know what they were, but they thought they looked like rockets.

"Let's take these to our spaceship!" Ben said. He grabbed the box and ran to the living room. Lily followed him. They climbed inside the big box and closed the flap.

"Look, Lily, these are our rockets!" Ben said. He took out one of the small sticks and showed it to Lily. "Maybe they can make our spaceship fly!"

"How do we make them work?" Lily asked.

Ben looked at the small box. He saw a word that he could not read. He tried to guess what it said.

"Maybe it says 'scratch'," he said. "Maybe we have to scratch the red tip on something."

He looked around the big box and saw a rough edge. He rubbed the red tip on the edge. Suddenly, there was a spark and a flame. Ben and Lily were shocked. They did not expect that.

"Wow!" Ben said. "It works!"

But then, the flame grew bigger and hotter. It burned the small stick and the big box. It made smoke and a bad smell. Ben and Lily started to panic.

"Help! Help!" they screamed. "Fire! Fire!"

Their mom heard their screams and ran to the living room. She saw the fire and the smoke. She was scared and angry.

"What are you doing?" she yelled. "Those are matches, not rockets! They are dangerous! You could have burned the house!"

She grabbed a blanket and threw it over the fire. She put out the flames and the smoke. She took Ben and Lily out of the big box. They were coughing and crying.

"I'm sorry, mom," Ben said. "We didn't know. We thought they were rockets. They were weird."

"You should never play with matches," mom said. "They are not toys. They can hurt you and others. You have to be careful and listen to me. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They hugged mom and said they were sorry. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them. She was glad they were not hurt. She threw away the matches and the big box. She gave them some water and a cookie. She told them to play with their other toys and never touch matches again. Ben and Lily agreed. They learned their lesson. They never played with matches again.

But there is a problem. They have only one glue bottle. Anna and Ben both want the glue. They start to pull the bottle. They do not share. They do not listen to the teacher.

"Anna, Ben, stop!" the teacher says. "You have to take turns. You have to be kind. You have to work together."

But Anna and Ben do not stop. They are persistent. They keep pulling the bottle. They make a loud noise. They make a mess.

The teacher is not happy. She takes the bottle away. She puts it on her desk. She tells Anna and Ben to sit in the corner. They have to be quiet. They have to think about what they did.

Anna and Ben are sad. They do not like to sit in the corner. They do not like to be quiet. They do not like to be apart. They look at each other. They feel sorry.

They whisper to each other. They say, "I am sorry. I was not kind. I was not fair. I want to be your friend. I want to play with you. I want to share with you."

They hug each other. They smile at each other. They are friends again.

The teacher sees them. She is happy. She gives them the bottle back. She tells them to finish their task. She tells them to be careful. She tells them to have fun.

Anna and Ben are happy. They go back to their table. They make a picture together. They make a flower and a car. They use the glue. They take turns. They listen to each other. They work together.

They show their picture to the teacher. The teacher likes their picture. She says, "Well done, Anna and Ben! You did a good job. You learned a good lesson. You are good friends."

Ben and Mia like to play in the park. They find many things to do, like swing, slide, and run. One day, they see a big object near the trees. It is brown and hard, and has many shapes on it.

"What is this?" Ben asks.

"I don't know," Mia says. "It looks old and strange."

They touch the object and feel its bumps and holes. They see some letters and pictures on it, but they cannot read them.

"Maybe it is a toy," Ben says. "Let's play with it."

He tries to move the object, but it is too heavy. He pushes and pulls, but it does not budge.

"Maybe it is a house," Mia says. "Let's go inside it."

She tries to find a door or a window, but there is none. She climbs on top of the object, but it is too high. She falls and hurts her knee.

"Ow!" she cries. "This is not a house. This is not a toy. This is a bad object."

Ben runs to help her. He hugs her and says, "Don't cry, Mia. I will call mom. She will make you feel better."

He takes out his phone and presses a button. He hears a voice.

"Hello, this is mom. What's wrong, Ben?"

"Mom, we found a big object in the park. It is old and strange. It hurt Mia. Can you come and get us?"

"Okay, Ben. I'm coming. Stay where you are. Don't touch the object. It might be ancient. It might be important. It might be dangerous."

"Okay, mom. We will wait for you. We love you."

"I love you too, Ben. I love you too, Mia. I'll be there soon."

Ben and Mia were best friends. They liked to play in the park, share their toys and make funny faces. One day, they found a big brown box near the slide. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Mia said.

"OK, but I go first!" Ben said.

"No, I go first!" Mia said.

They both pulled on the box, but it did not yield. They pulled harder and harder, but the box was too strong.

"Stop, stop!" a voice said. "You are hurting the box!"

They looked up and saw a man with a brown hat and a brown coat. He was holding a camera and a microphone. He smiled at them.

"Hello, kids. I'm sorry to scare you, but this is not a real box. It is a prop for a movie. We are filming a scene about a marriage proposal. Do you know what that is?"

Ben and Mia shook their heads. They did not know what a marriage proposal was.

"It is when a man asks a woman to be his wife, and she says yes. Then they hug and kiss and get a ring. Do you want to see?"

Ben and Mia nodded. They were curious.

"OK, then. Come with me. But be quiet and don't touch anything. You can watch from behind that tree."

The man led them to a spot where they could see a man and a woman standing near the box. They were wearing nice clothes and holding hands. The man knelt down and opened the box. There was a shiny ring inside. He said something to the woman, and she smiled and nodded. Then they hugged and kissed and put the ring on her finger. The man with the camera and the microphone said "Cut!" and everyone clapped.

"Wow!" Ben said. "That was pretty!"

"Yes, it was!" Mia said. "Do you think we can do that too?"

Ben thought for a moment. He liked Mia a lot. He said "Maybe, when we are older. But for now, can we just be friends?"

Mia smiled. She liked Ben a lot too. She said "OK, that sounds good. But can we still share our toys and make funny faces?"

Ben nodded. He said "Of course! That's what friends do!"

They hugged and ran back to the slide, happy and giggling. The man with the hat and the coat watched them and smiled. He said to himself "That's what love is!"

Lily and Ben like to play at the park. They run, swing, climb and slide. They have a lot of fun.

One day, they see a big pitch near the park. It is green and flat. Lily and Ben want to play on it. They run to the pitch and see some balls and bats.

They take a ball and a bat and go to the middle of the pitch. Ben holds the bat and Lily throws the ball. Ben swings the bat and hits the ball. The ball flies far away.

"Wow, good hit!" Lily says. "I will get the ball."

She runs after the ball. But the ball is heavy and rolls fast. It goes down a hill and slides into a pond.

"Oh no, the ball is gone!" Lily says. "It is in the water."

Ben runs to Lily and sees the ball in the pond. He is sad.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I hit the ball too hard. How can we get it back?" Ben says.

Lily thinks for a moment. She sees a big stick near the pond. She has an idea.

"Maybe we can use the stick to get the ball. I will try." Lily says.

She picks up the stick and walks to the edge of the pond. She reaches the stick to the ball and tries to pull it out. But the stick is too short and the ball is too far.

"I can't get it. The stick is not long enough." Lily says.

Ben sees another stick near the pond. It is longer and thicker than the first one. He has an idea.

"Maybe we can use this stick to get the ball. I will try." Ben says.

He picks up the stick and walks to the edge of the pond. He joins the stick with Lily's stick and makes a longer stick. He reaches the longer stick to the ball and tries to pull it out. He pulls hard and the ball slides out of the water.

"Yay, we got it!" Ben says.

"Good job, Ben! You are smart." Lily says.

They hug and smile. They are happy. They take the ball and the bat and go back to the pitch. They play some more and have a lot of fun.

One day, it was raining and they could not go out. They were sad and bored. They looked at their toys, but they did not want to play with them. They wanted to play with the ball.

"Mom, can we play with the ball in the house?" Tom asked.

"No, you can't. The ball is too big and loud. You might break something or hurt someone. You have to find something else to do," Mom said.

Tom and Lily did not like Mom's answer. They started to complain.

"It's not fair! We want to play with the ball! We don't like the rain! We don't like the house!" they said.

Mom sighed. She knew they were unhappy, but she had to keep them safe and quiet. She thought of an idea.

"Why don't you play dress up? You can use your old clothes and pretend to be different people. You can make up stories and have fun," she said.

She gave them a big box of clothes and shoes. Tom and Lily looked at the box. They saw some hats, scarves, shirts, pants, skirts, and boots. They decided to try Mom's idea.

They took out some clothes and put them on. Tom wore a green shirt, a blue hat, and a yellow scarf. Lily wore a pink skirt, a purple shirt, and a green boot. They looked at each other and laughed.

"Who are you?" Tom asked.

"I'm a pirate who sails the sea. I have a blue hat because it's my treasure. It can make me invisible and find gold. Do you want to join my crew?" Tom said.

They nodded and smiled. They forgot about the rain and the ball. They played dress up and made up stories. They had fun. Mom was happy. She watched them and smiled. She was glad they stopped complaining and used their imagination.

"Who is that, mom?" Lily asked.

Lily looked closer at the photo. She saw her dad's eyes and nose. They were the same as now. But his hair was different. And he had no beard.

"Yes, I recognize him. He is my dad. But he looks different. Why?" Lily said.

"Well, people change as they grow up, Lily. They get bigger and older. Sometimes they change their hair or clothes. But they are still the same inside. They still love you and remember you." mom said.

Lily nodded. She understood. She turned the page and saw another photo. It was of a big dog with sharp teeth and a mean face. It was barking at the camera.

"Who is that, mom?" Lily asked.

"That's Rex, Lily. He was your dad's dog when he was little. He was very loyal and brave. But he was also very scary. He didn't like strangers or cats. He always protected your dad." mom said.

"Don't worry, Lily. He is not here. He is only in the photo. He can't hurt you or anyone. He is gone now. He was very old and sick. Your dad was very sad when he died. He loved him very much." mom said.
