Tim and Sam are best friends. They like to play with cars and blocks and balls. Sometimes they tell jokes to make each other laugh. They think jokes are funny and fun.

One day, they are playing in the park. They see a big dog with a long tail and a funny hat. The dog is walking with a man who has a beard and glasses. Tim and Sam think the dog and the man look weird.

"Look at that dog," Tim whispers to Sam. "He has a hat on his head. Why does he have a hat?"

"I don't know," Sam whispers back. "Maybe he is cold. Or maybe he is a spy."

"A spy?" Tim says. "What is a spy?"

"A spy is someone who hides and watches other people. Like in the movies," Sam says.

"Oh," Tim says. "Do you think the dog is watching us?"

"Maybe," Sam says. "Or maybe he is watching the birds. Or the flowers. Or the clouds."

Tim and Sam giggle. They think they are very smart and clever. They decide to tell a joke to the dog and the man. They think the joke will make them laugh too.

"Hey, dog," Tim shouts. "Why did the chicken cross the road?"

Sam shouts the answer. "To get to the other side!"

Tim and Sam laugh. They think their joke is very funny. They wait for the dog and the man to laugh too.

But the dog and the man do not laugh. They do not even look at Tim and Sam. They keep walking and talking. They do not hear the joke.

Tim and Sam are confused. They do not understand why the dog and the man do not laugh. They think their joke is the best joke ever.

"Maybe they did not hear us," Tim says.

"Maybe they do not speak our language," Sam says.

"Maybe they do not like jokes," Tim says.

"Maybe they are weird," Sam says.

Tim and Sam shrug. They do not care. They go back to playing with their cars and blocks and balls. They tell more jokes to each other. They laugh and have fun. They are happy.

One day, Tom and Mia went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like monkeys, elephants, and giraffes. They liked to count how many animals they saw in each cage.

When they came to the tiger cage, they saw a big orange and black tiger lying on a rock. He looked sleepy and bored. Tom and Mia wanted to see him move and roar.

"Let's count to ten and see if he wakes up," Tom said to Mia.

"Okay," Mia said. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

They shouted the last number very loud. The tiger opened his eyes and looked at them. He was alert and curious. He got up from the rock and walked to the fence. He opened his mouth and roared.

"Wow!" Tom and Mia said. "He is so big and loud!"

They clapped their hands and laughed. The tiger seemed to like their attention. He roared again and licked his paws.

"Mom, look at the tiger!" Tom and Mia said. "He is awake and he roared for us!"

Mom smiled and took a picture of them with the tiger. She was happy that they had fun at the zoo. She said, "You are very brave and smart to count to ten and make the tiger roar. He is a beautiful animal, but remember to be careful and respectful of him. He is not a pet, he is wild."

Tom and Mia nodded and said, "We know, Mom. We love the tiger, but we don't touch him. We just look and listen and learn."

They waved goodbye to the tiger and went to see more animals. They had a great day at the zoo.

Sam liked to learn new things. He liked to learn about animals, colors, shapes, and numbers. He also liked to learn about stamps. Stamps were small pictures that you could stick on letters or books. Sam's grandpa had many stamps from different places. He was elderly, but he was very smart and kind.

One day, Sam went to visit his grandpa. He saw a big book on the table. It was full of stamps. Sam asked, "Grandpa, can I see your stamps?"

"Of course, Sam. Come here and I'll show you some of them," grandpa said. He opened the book and pointed to a stamp. "This stamp is from China. It has a panda on it. Do you know what a panda is?"

Sam nodded. He had seen a panda at the zoo. It was black and white and fluffy. He liked pandas. He said, "Panda is an animal. It eats bamboo."

"That's right, Sam. You're very smart. And this stamp is from Canada. It has a maple leaf on it. Do you know what a maple leaf is?"

Sam shook his head. He had never seen a maple leaf. He said, "No, grandpa. What is a maple leaf?"

"A maple leaf is a part of a tree. It has a special shape and color. In the fall, it turns red and orange and yellow. It's very pretty. Here, I have a real maple leaf for you. You can keep it as a souvenir," grandpa said. He gave Sam a dried maple leaf. Sam touched it gently. It was thin and crisp. He liked the maple leaf. He said, "Thank you, grandpa. It's very pretty. I like it."

"You're welcome, Sam. I'm glad you like it. And I'm happy you like to learn about stamps. Stamps are like little windows to the world. They can teach you about different places, people, and things. Maybe one day, you can travel and see them for yourself," grandpa said.

Sam smiled. He hugged his grandpa. He said, "I love you, grandpa. And I love your stamps. They are very cool. Maybe one day, I can show you my stamps too."

The end.

Lily loved flowers. She liked to smell them, touch them, and look at their colors. She had a small garden in her backyard, where she planted seeds and watered them every day. She was waiting for them to bloom, to open up and show their pretty petals.

One day, she saw a big red flower in her garden. It was the first one to bloom. She was so happy, she ran to get her mom. "Mom, mom, look! A flower bloomed! It is red and wide and beautiful!" she shouted.

Mom came out and smiled. She hugged Lily and said, "Wow, that is a lovely flower, Lily. You did a great job taking care of your garden. What kind of flower is it?"

Lily thought for a moment. She did not know the name of the flower. She had picked the seeds from a packet with a picture of a flower on it. She said, "I don't know, mom. But I like it. Can I pick it and put it in a vase?"

Mom shook her head. She said, "No, Lily, you can't pick it. It is an emergency flower. It is very special and rare. It only blooms for one day, and then it closes and dies. If you pick it, it will die sooner. You have to let it stay in the garden, and enjoy it while it lasts."

Lily felt sad. She wanted to keep the flower and look at it every day. She said, "But mom, I love it. It is my flower. I planted it. Why does it have to die?"

Mom hugged her again. She said, "I know, Lily, I know. But that is how nature works. Some things are only here for a short time, but they make us happy and grateful. We have to respect them and let them go. Maybe next year, you can plant more seeds and see if another emergency flower blooms. But for now, let's just sit here and admire your beautiful flower, okay?"

Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and smiled. She said, "Okay, mom. Thank you for telling me. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love your flower. It is a very special gift."

Lily said, "I am Lily, a bunny. I like to eat food. What do you like to do?"

Max said, "I am Max, a squirrel. I like to climb trees and collect nuts. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily said, "OK, that sounds fun. Let's play hide and seek."

As she closed her eyes, the weariness slowly melted away. The cuddly toy smiled at her before everything around her started to turn dark. Annie felt calm and peaceful as she drifted off to sleep. 

In the morning, she woke up feeling well rested. She jumped out of bed and ran to the kitchen for another bowl of oat cereal. Then she was off to start her day filled with energy and fun!

Once upon a time there was a shy girl named Lucy. She was always scared of the dark but one night something magical happened.

Lucy was sitting in her room and she noticed a strange powder on the floor. She reached out to touch it and it started to glow with a mysterious light.

The powder started to move and it began to pour itself into a glass jug. Suddenly the powder turned into a shimmering liquid which sparkled and shone.

Lucy was curious and she decided to take a sip. The liquid tasted sweet and Lucy was no longer afraid of the dark.

Lucy was so excited and now she was not so shy anymore. She went on to share the magical powder with all of her friends and they never needed to be scared of the dark ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a family that went to the shore. It was a warm, sunny day and the family wanted to go for a swim in the sea. But when they got to the shore, it was really dirty! There was sand and seaweed, and it was all very filthy.

The family was surprised and decided not to go swimming. So they decided to play some games instead. Dad dropped a heavy ball into the sand, and the kids laughed and chased after it. Then, mom dropped some yummy treats that the kids love. They all laughed and gobbled them up.

But as the day went on, the family got tired and decided to go home. When they got to the shore, it was still very filthy. Mom and dad decided to show the kids a good example and got to work on cleaning up the shore. The kids were given buckets and helped to pick up all the sand and seaweed. Then, they all dropped it into the bucket.

After a while, the shore started to look better! The family cleaned up most of the mess and left the shore much brighter and cleaner than before. Now the family can come back any time they like and enjoy a nice swim in the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Daisy. Daisy's heart was very sad, because she was all alone. Everyone around her was careless, and no one seemed to care about her. She didn't have any friends.

One day, Daisy decided it was time to make a change. She wished for a little friend, who would always be kind and show her attention.

Suddenly, there was a bright light in the sky! It was a magical fairy! She smiled at Daisy and waved her wand. With a happy twinkle in her eye, she whispered: "Your wish is granted!"

The fairy sprinkled some fairy-dust in the air, and a little bunny appeared! Daisy clapped her hands with glee and hugged the bunny tightly.

The bunny stayed with Daisy all day. But as the sun began to set, the bunny started to disappear! Soon the little bunny was gone!

Daisy was very sad, but she knew that the bunny was happy now. With a big smile, she waved goodbye and whispered: "Thank you!" 

From then on, Daisy didn't feel so alone anymore. She had learnt a valuable lesson about the power of love and care.

The chick was sad but then he saw something else. He noticed a tiny path just to the side of the sign. It had small stones scattered across it and he was curious to explore.

The path led to a sharp hill. He looked up and asked his mommy if it was okay to go up the hill. She said yes, so the chick eagerly started climbing. When he reached the top, he was surprised to see a big surprise waiting for him. An apple tree with lots of ripe apples was there and he went to pick one.

It was the sweetest apple the chick had ever tasted! He was so excited that he ran down the hill and back to his mommy to tell her the good news.

Together they shared the big surprise and the chick was so happy. From then on, he remembered to always look for the hidden path because you never know what kind of sharp surprise it may lead to!

Once upon a time, there was a dolphin named Dolly. Dolly was a happy dolphin who loved to swim and play in the ocean. One day, Dolly met a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very curious about the dolphin and asked, "Can you talk?"

Dolly replied, "No, I can't talk like humans, but I can understand you."

Timmy was amazed and asked, "Can you show me how you swim?"

Dolly smiled and said, "Sure, hop on my back!" Timmy climbed onto Dolly's back and they swam together. Suddenly, a big wave came and Dolly got scared. She started to shrink and shrink until she was as small as a fish.

Timmy was sad and said, "Oh no! Poor Dolly, what happened?"

Dolly replied, "I got scared and when I get scared, I shrink. But don't worry, I'll grow back to my normal size soon."

From that day on, Timmy and Dolly became good friends and would often swim together. Dolly never got scared again and Timmy was happy to have a dolphin friend.

After a little while, Lily's mom came to pick her up. She said "Lily, we have to go home now." Lily said "But I don't want to leave! I want to stay and soak my feet." Her mom laughed and said "Don't worry, we can come back tomorrow and soak our feet again." Lily smiled and put her shoes back on. She said goodbye to her friends and went home with her mom.

As Tweetie was flying, she saw a zigzag path and decided to follow it. The path led her to a tree where she saw a family of birds. Tweetie wanted to play with the family of birds, so she asked if they wanted to play with the nut. The family of birds said yes and they all had fun playing with the nut.

After playing for a while, Tweetie realized that she needed to return the nut to Nutty. So, she said goodbye to the family of birds and flew back to Nutty. Nutty was happy to see Tweetie return the nut and thanked her for borrowing it. From that day on, Tweetie and Nutty became good friends and would often play together. The end.

"I'm just taking a walk," replied Lily.

"Well, you better be careful," warned the dragon. "I'm not the friendliest dragon around."

He pointed the gun at Ella and said, "Don't move, kid. This is none of your business. I'm here for the jewels. Your grandma has a lot of them. She used to be a princess, you know."

Ella was scared and angry. She said, "No, you're lying. Grandma is not a princess. She's my grandma. And you're a bad man. You hurt the dragon. He was grandma's friend. He was protecting her. You're a meanie. Go away. Leave us alone."

The man laughed and said, "You're a silly kid. You think this is a fairy tale. Well, it's not. It's real. And I'm the boss. Now, be quiet or I'll shoot you too."

He reached for the necklace again, but he didn't see the dragon's tail. The dragon was not dead. He was only wounded. He had pretended to be dead to trick the man. He had waited for the right moment to strike. He swung his tail and hit the man in the head. The man fell to the floor and dropped the gun and the necklace.

The dragon roared and breathed fire at the man. The man screamed and ran out of the house. He left behind his mask and his car. He never came back.

Ella ran to grandma and hugged her. She said, "Grandma, are you okay? Did he hurt you? I'm sorry I didn't hear you. I was reading a book. It was about a princess and a dragon. Just like you and your friend."

Grandma hugged her back and said, "I'm okay, my dear. He didn't hurt me. Thanks to you and the dragon. You were brave and smart. You saved me. I'm proud of you. And yes, I was a princess once. A long time ago. But now, I'm just your grandma. And I love you more than anything."

The dragon came closer and licked Ella's face. He said, "I love you too, little princess. You're my friend. And I'm sorry I scared you. I was only doing my job. I'm your grandma's guardian. I've been with her since she was a baby. I've watched over her all her life. And I'll always protect her. And you."

Ella smiled and said, "I love you too, dragon. You're my friend too. And you're not scary. You're awesome. And you're the best guardian ever. Thank you for saving us."

They all hugged and kissed and laughed. They were happy and safe. They decided to nap together on the mattress. They dreamed of cookies and stories and games and cartoons. And they lived happily ever after. The end.

Suddenly, Todd heard something coming from the bush - om-p-pah, om-pah! "What is that noise?" asked Todd.

"Oh, that's jazz," said Mom. "It's music for your ears, and it's very fun to listen to. It'll make you want to dance!"

So Todd and Mom listened together. As they listened, Todd couldn't help but move his feet - he springed and spun around, twirling and whirling in the park like a spinning top. It was the most fun that Todd had had all day!

When the jazz ended and Todd stopped to catch his breath, Mom hugged him and squeezed him tight. "That was amazing, honey," she said. "Let's do it again tomorrow!" 

Todd smiled and nodded. He felt very happy. What a wonderful day they had had together in the park - listening to the jazz, feeling the fresh spring air, and playing in the wet puddles.

The wind was so strong that it picked up some of the rubbish in the park. It blew papers and plastic bags up into the air. The wind made the park look untidy.

But then the wind died down. The leaves and rubbish gently fell back down to the park. The trees stopped swaying. Everything returned to looking neat and tidy. The park was peaceful and clean again.

Once upon a time a foolish little bird wanted to go on a journey. He looked around for a way to get started, but found nothing. He thought and thought about what he could do. Finally, he had an idea. He would mail himself!

So he found an envelope and addressed it to himself from the stars. Then he hopped inside and tightened the string around the envelope.

The bird waited and waited. When he heard a knock on the door, he knew the mailman had arrived. When he opened the door, there was the envelope with the bird inside. He opened it up and there was the bird!

The bird thanked the mailman and said, "I'm so glad you made it safely! This is a big welcome!"

The mailman was very impressed and said, "This is the most foolish thing I have ever seen, but it worked and that's all that matters!"

And the bird flew off into the sky, free to explore the world. He was so grateful for the welcome he received from the mailman!

But her mom was smart. She saw the lump under the rug and knew it was Lily. She lifted the rug and saw Lily's face and the ball. She smiled and said, "I found you, Lily. You can't hide from me. Come on, let's go to the store. Maybe we can find a new toy for you."

Lily was surprised. She did not think her mom would see her. She felt a little silly, but also curious. She wondered what kind of toy her mom would buy for her. She grabbed her ball and followed her mom to the car. She hoped it would be a toy that bounced high and made a funny noise, like her ball.

Tom liked to play with his ball. He would kick it, throw it, and catch it. He had a lot of fun with his ball. But one day, he lost his ball. He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. He was very sad.

He asked his mom and dad if they knew where his ball was. They said no, they did not know. They said maybe someone took it, or maybe it rolled away. They said they would buy him a new ball soon. But Tom did not want a new ball. He wanted his old ball.

The next day, Tom went to the park with his mom. He saw some kids playing with a ball. It was his ball! He was sure of it. It had the same color, the same size, and the same mark. He ran to the kids and said, "That is my ball! Give it back!"

The kids looked at him. They said, "No, this is our ball. We found it yesterday. It was lying on the grass. It is ours now. Go away!"

Tom was angry. He tried to grab the ball, but the kids pushed him away. He fell on the ground and hurt his knee. He cried. His mom came and picked him up. She said, "It's okay, Tom. Don't cry. We will find another ball for you. Come on, let's go home."

Tom did not want to go home. He wanted his ball. He felt like he had lost something very important. He did not know that he was about to gain something even better. He did not know that his dad had a surprise for him. He did not know that when he got home, he would see a big box with a ribbon on it. He did not know that inside the box, there was a new bike. A bike that he could ride, and pedal, and steer. A bike that was his, and only his. A bike that would make him happy, and forget about his ball. He did not know that this was not a normal day. It was a special day. A day that he would remember for a long time.

Lily liked to grow mint in her garden. She had a small pot with some dirt and some seeds. She watered them every day and watched them grow. Mint smelled good and made her happy.

One day, Lily saw a light in her garden. It was a fairy! The fairy had wings and a dress and a wand. She flew over to Lily and smiled. "Hello, little girl. I like your mint. Can I have some?" she asked.

Lily was surprised and happy. She liked fairies. She nodded and picked some mint leaves. She gave them to the fairy. The fairy thanked her and ate them. She said they were yummy and fresh.

The fairy and Lily became friends. They played and talked and laughed. The fairy told Lily stories about her home and her magic. Lily told the fairy about her family and her toys. They had fun.

The fairy had to go back to her home when the sun went down. She gave Lily a hug and a kiss. She said she would come back and visit. She waved her wand and made some sparkles. Lily smiled and waved goodbye. She was happy she had a new friend. She went inside and told her mom about the fairy and the mint. Her mom hugged her and said she was proud of her. Lily went to bed and dreamed of fairies and mint.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box of magnets in the garage. Magnets are things that stick to other things.

"Wow, look at these magnets!" Tom says. "They are so cool!"

"Let's prepare a game with them," Sue says. "We can make shapes and patterns on the fridge."

They take some magnets and go to the kitchen. They see a big fridge with a white door. They start to put the magnets on the door. They make a star, a circle, a square, and a heart.

"Look, I made a star!" Tom says. "It has five points."

"I made a circle!" Sue says. "It has no points."

They are having fun with the magnets. But then, they see something strange. One of the magnets is not like the others. It is not regular. It is big and round and shiny. It has a button on it.

"What is this?" Tom asks. He picks up the magnet and presses the button.

Suddenly, the magnet makes a loud noise. It starts to spin and glow. It pulls all the other magnets to it. It makes a big ball of magnets.

"Help!" Tom and Sue shout. They are scared. The magnet is too strong. They can't pull it off.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the kitchen. She sees the big ball of magnets and the kids.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She is surprised and angry.

"We were playing with the magnets," Tom says. "But this one is not regular. It is a super magnet. It took all the others."

Mom takes the super magnet and turns it off. The ball of magnets falls apart. She puts the super magnet back in the box.

"This is not a toy," Mom says. "This is a special magnet for Dad's work. You can't play with it. It is dangerous."

She gives them some regular magnets to play with. She tells them to be careful and not to touch the super magnet again.

Tom and Sue say sorry to Mom. They learn their lesson. They play with the regular magnets and have fun. They make more shapes and patterns on the fridge. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were at the beach with their mom. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Mom told them to stay close and not go into the water.

"Look, Tom, I found a big shell!" Lily said, holding up a shiny pink shell. "It is so pretty!"

"Wow, Lily, that is a nice shell!" Tom said. "Can I see it?"

Lily gave Tom the shell and he looked at it closely. He saw something move inside the shell. He got excited and said, "Lily, there is a crab in the shell! It is alive!"

Lily was scared and said, "A crab? Give it back to me, Tom! I don't want a crab!"

Tom was naughty and said, "No, Lily, I want to keep the crab. It is my friend. I will name him Bob."

He ran away with the shell and the crab, laughing. Lily chased him and said, "Tom, stop! That is my shell! Give it back!"

Mom saw them and said, "Lily, Tom, what are you doing? Come here, now!"

She took the shell from Tom and said, "This is not a toy, Tom. This is a living creature. You have to be gentle and respectful. And you have to share with your sister. Lily, this is your shell, but you have to let the crab go. It belongs to the sea, not to us."

She helped Lily and Tom put the shell and the crab back in the water. They watched as the crab crawled away and hid under a rock.

"Bye, Bob," Tom said, waving.

"Bye, crab," Lily said, smiling.

Mom hugged them and said, "Good job, kids. You did the right thing. Now, let's go and have some ice cream."

One day, his mom gives him a math book. She says he has to do some math before he can play. Ben does not want to do math. He wants to play. He looks at the math book and sees many numbers and signs. He does not know what they mean. He struggles to do math. He feels sad and angry.

He sees his sister, Mia, playing with her doll. Mia is older than Ben. She likes to do math. She says math is fun and easy. She can count and add and take away very fast. She helps mom with math sometimes.

Ben says to Mia, "Math is stupid. I hate math. You are stupid too. You only like math because you are a girl."

Mia feels hurt by Ben's words. She says to Ben, "Math is not stupid. Math is important. You need math to learn many things. Math is not only for girls. Math is for everyone. You are mean to me. You do not like me."

Ben and Mia start to fight. They yell and push and pull. They make a lot of noise. Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Ben and Mia fighting over the math book. She is not happy.

She says to Ben and Mia, "Stop fighting right now. Math is not a reason to fight. Math is harmless. Math is just a way to use numbers and signs. Math can be fun and interesting. You can both do math. You can also help each other with math. You are brother and sister. You should love each other and be kind to each other. Now, say sorry to each other and hug."

Ben and Mia feel ashamed of their fight. They say sorry to each other and hug. They look at the math book again. They see that math is not so hard and boring. They see that math can be fun and easy. They decide to do some math together. They count and add and take away. They learn some new things. They also play with their toys. They are happy. Mom is happy too. She smiles and says, "Good job, Ben and Mia. You are doing great with math. I am proud of you."

Lily was a little girl who liked to play outside. She had a big yard with many flowers and trees. She also had a brown dog named Spot who was her best friend. Spot liked to run and jump and chase balls.

One day, Lily and Spot saw a big bird on the roof of their house. It was black and white and had a long tail. It was a magpie. The magpie was looking for shiny things to take to its nest. It saw something shiny in the chimney and flew down to get it.

Lily and Spot did not like the magpie. They thought it was a bad bird who wanted to steal their things. They ran to the house and barked and shouted at the magpie. The magpie was scared and tried to fly away. But it was too late. The shiny thing in the chimney was a trap. It was a metal cage with a spring door. The magpie went inside the cage and the door snapped shut behind it.

Lily and Spot were happy. They had caught the bad bird. They ran to get Lily's dad, who was inside the house. He came out and saw the magpie in the cage. He was surprised and proud of Lily and Spot. He said they were very clever and brave. He took the cage and the magpie and put them in his truck. He said he would take the magpie to the woods and let it go. He said the magpie would not bother them anymore.

Lily and Spot were glad. They hugged and kissed their dad and thanked him. They went back to their yard and played with their balls. They did not see any more bad birds on their roof. They were happy and safe.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to draw. They had many crayons of different colors. One day, they decided to have a race. Who could draw the best picture in five minutes?

"Ready, set, go!" Lily said, and they both grabbed their crayons and paper. Lily chose a red crayon and started to draw a big heart. Ben chose a blue crayon and started to draw a fast car.

They drew very quickly, trying to make their pictures look nice. They did not look at each other's paper. They wanted to surprise each other.

But then, something bad happened. Lily's red crayon broke in half. She gasped and looked for another red crayon. But there was none. All the other crayons were ordinary colors, like yellow and green and brown. Lily did not like those colors. She wanted a red crayon.

"Ben, can I have your red crayon, please?" Lily asked, looking at Ben's paper. She saw that he had a red crayon, but he was using it to draw the car's wheels.

"No, you can't. It's mine. I need it for my car," Ben said, holding the crayon tightly. He did not want to share it with Lily. He wanted to win the race.

Lily felt sad and angry. She thought Ben was being mean. She did not want to be his friend anymore. She threw down her paper and ran away, crying.

Ben felt sorry and confused. He did not mean to hurt Lily's feelings. He just wanted to finish his car. He looked at his paper and realized that his car was not very good. It was just a blue rectangle with red circles. He looked at Lily's paper and saw that her heart was very pretty. It was big and red and had a smiley face. He wished he had given her his red crayon.

He picked up his paper and ran after Lily. He wanted to say sorry and make up with her. He wanted to be her friend again. He hoped she would forgive him.

Mom takes Ben outside and points to the sky. She shows him a big star that is very bright. She says it is the North Star. She says it can help people find their way. Ben thinks that is cool.

Mom says it is time to go inside. She says they can look at the stars again tomorrow. Ben says he likes the stars. He says he likes to solve shapes in the sky. He says it is easy and fun. Mom hugs him and says she loves him. She says he is her star.

"Anna, look at my car! It can go fast and make beep beep!" Ben says, pushing his car on the floor.

They are having fun, but they are not gentle with their toys. They throw them, drop them, and step on them. Their toys are getting dirty and broken.

"Anna, Ben, it's time to clean up!" Mom says, coming into the living room. "You have to organize your toys and put them away. They are not happy when you are not gentle with them."

"But Mom, we are still playing!" Anna and Ben say, making sad faces.

"I know, but you have to take care of your toys. They are your friends, and they need some rest too. How would you feel if someone was not gentle with you?" Mom says, kneeling down and hugging them.

Anna and Ben think for a moment. They do not like it when someone is not gentle with them. They feel hurt and sad.

"OK, Mom, we will organize our toys and be gentle with them." Anna and Ben say, nodding their heads.

They start to organize their toys by type and color. They put the cars in one box, the dolls in another, the blocks in a third, and the books in a fourth. They are careful not to throw them, drop them, or step on them. They say sorry to their toys and thank them for playing with them.

"Good job, Anna and Ben! You are very smart and kind. I'm proud of you!" Mom says, smiling and clapping her hands.

Anna and Ben smile too. They feel happy and proud. They have organized their toys and been gentle with them. They have learned a new word: organize. They like to organize. It is fun and easy. They hug Mom and their toys and go to bed. They dream of playing with their toys again tomorrow.

Lily loved to draw. She drew flowers and birds and stars and rainbows. She used many colors and made her pictures beautiful. She liked to show her drawings to her mommy and daddy and they always smiled and said, "Wow, Lily, you are very good at drawing!"

One day, Lily found a note on the fridge. It said, "Lily, we have to go to the store. We will be back soon. Love, Mommy and Daddy." Lily felt sad. She wanted to draw with her mommy and daddy. She decided to draw them a picture to make them happy when they came back.

She took a big piece of paper and some crayons and started to draw. She drew her mommy and daddy holding hands and smiling. She drew a big heart around them and wrote, "I love you" in big letters. She was very proud of her picture. She put it on the fridge with a magnet and waited for her mommy and daddy to come back.

But while she was waiting, her big brother Tommy came home. He saw Lily's picture on the fridge and he did not like it. He thought it was silly and childish. He wanted to play a trick on Lily. He took the picture and tore it into pieces. He threw the pieces in the trash and laughed. He thought he was very funny.

Lily heard Tommy laugh and ran to the kitchen. She saw what he had done to her picture and she felt very angry and sad. She started to cry and said, "Tommy, why did you do that? That was my picture for mommy and daddy! It was beautiful and I worked very hard on it! You are very mean and rude!"

Tommy saw Lily cry and he felt sorry. He realized he had made a mistake. He had hurt Lily's feelings and he had ruined her gift. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I was just joking. I didn't mean to make you cry. Please forgive me. I will help you make a new picture for mommy and daddy."

Lily looked at Tommy and she saw that he was sorry. She decided to forgive him. She said, "OK, Tommy, I forgive you. But you have to promise me not to do that again. And you have to be nice to me and my drawings. They are important to me."

Tommy nodded and said, "I promise, Lily. I will be nice to you and your drawings. And I will help you make a new picture for mommy and daddy. Maybe we can draw something together. What do you want to draw?"

Lily smiled and said, "Let's draw a family. A family that loves each other and is happy."

Tommy smiled and said, "OK, let's draw a family. A family like ours."

They used many colors and made their picture beautiful. They put it on the fridge with a magnet and hugged each other. They felt happy and proud of their picture.

When their mommy and daddy came back, they saw the picture and they smiled and said, "Wow, Lily and Tommy, you are very good at drawing! And you are very good at sharing and caring. We are very proud of you. We love you very much."

Lily and Tommy smiled and said, "We love you too, mommy and daddy. And we love each other. We are a family."

Anna and Ben wanted to decorate their place for the party. They had balloons, streamers, stickers and crayons. They asked their mom if they could use them.

"Sure, you can decorate your place, but be careful and don't make a mess," mom said. "And don't go near the stove or the scissors, okay?"

"Okay, mom," Anna and Ben said. They started to decorate their place. They put balloons on the chairs, streamers on the walls, stickers on the windows and crayons on the table. They had fun and made their place look colorful and festive.

But then, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It was the smoke alarm. Mom was cooking something and it burned. She ran to the kitchen and turned off the stove. She opened the window and waved a towel to clear the smoke.

"Are you okay, mom?" Anna and Ben asked. They were alert and worried.

"I'm okay, don't worry. I just forgot to watch the pot. It's nothing serious," mom said. She smiled and hugged them. "You two are very alert and brave. Thank you for coming to check on me."

"Can we still have the party, mom?" Anna and Ben asked.

"Of course, we can still have the party. Your place looks wonderful. You did a great job decorating it," mom said. "Now, let's clean up the kitchen and get ready for the guests. They will be here soon."

Anna and Ben nodded and helped mom. They were happy and excited for the party. They hoped their friends would like their place and have fun.

Dan is a bald man. He has no hair on his head. He likes to wear hats to keep his head warm. One day, he goes to the park with his dog, Rex. Rex is a big, brown dog. He likes to run and play.

At the park, Dan sees a big tree. The tree has many green leaves. The leaves spread wide and make a lot of shade. Dan thinks the tree is nice. He takes off his hat and sits under the tree. He feels the cool breeze on his bald head.

Rex sees a squirrel. The squirrel is small and gray. It has a long, fluffy tail. Rex wants to chase the squirrel. He barks and runs after it. The squirrel is scared. It runs up the tree. Rex jumps and tries to catch it, but he is too slow.

The squirrel reaches the top of the tree. It looks down and sees Rex. It sees Dan too. It sees Dan's bald head. It thinks Dan's head is a big, shiny nut. It wants to eat the nut. It jumps from the tree and lands on Dan's head.

Dan feels something on his head. He looks up and sees the squirrel. He is surprised and scared. He screams and shakes his head. The squirrel is surprised and scared too. It screams and jumps off Dan's head. It runs away.

Rex hears Dan and the squirrel. He runs back to Dan. He sees the squirrel running away. He barks and chases it again. Dan puts on his hat and laughs. He thinks Rex and the squirrel are funny. He is happy. He pets Rex and says, "Good boy, Rex. Good boy."

"Do you know what this is?" Mom asked.

Lila and Ben nodded. They understood.

Mom said yes, but she told him to be careful and not to cut himself. Leo took a peeler and a bowl and sat next to Mira. He tried to peel a potato, but he was not very good at it. "Mama, mama, come here!" they cried.

Mama came to the living room and saw what happened. She was not happy.

"What did you do, Lily and Sam? Why did you break your tower?" she asked.

"We were fighting over the blocks, mama. We wanted to raise the tower higher and higher. But we could not agree on which blocks to use. We were selfish and rude." Lily and Sam said.

"That was not nice, Lily and Sam. You should have worked together and respected each other. You should have used all the blocks, no matter what color they were. You should have been kind and helpful. Then you could have built a beautiful and strong tower." Mama said.

"You are right, mama. We are sorry. We learned our lesson. Can we try again?" Lily and Sam asked.

"Of course you can, my loves. But first, you need to clean up this mess. And then, you need to hug and say sorry to each other. And then, you can play with the blocks again. But this time, remember to share and listen. And have fun!" Mama said.

Lily and Sam nodded and smiled. They hugged and said sorry to each other. They picked up the blocks and put them in a big box. They thanked mama for her advice. They took out the blocks again and started to build a new tower. They used pink and blue blocks, and also yellow and green and purple and orange blocks. They made a thick and tall and colorful tower. They were happy and proud.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play with cars. Tim had a big red car that made loud noises. Sam had a small blue car that was very fast. One day, they decided to trade cars and see how they liked them.

"Can I have your red car, Tim?" Sam asked. "It looks so cool and loud."

"Sure, Sam. You can have it for a while. But I want your blue car. It looks so fast and fun." Tim said. They gave each other their cars and started to play.

Tim liked the blue car at first. It zoomed around the grass and the dirt. But soon, he saw that it was too small for him. His hands were too big to hold it. His fingers got stuck in the wheels. He could not make it go where he wanted. He felt sad and angry.

Sam liked the red car at first. It roared and flashed its lights. But soon, he saw that it was too big for him. His arms were too short to reach it. His ears hurt from the noise. He could not make it stop when he needed. He felt scared and frustrated.

They both wanted their own cars back. They ran to each other and tried to trade again.

"Give me back my blue car, Tim!" Sam shouted. "Your red car is too big and loud for me!"

"Give me back my red car, Sam!" Tim yelled. "Your blue car is too small and fast for me!"

But they were both so angry that they did not listen. They pulled and pushed and fought over the cars. They did not manage to trade them back. They only managed to break them. The cars snapped and cracked and stopped working. They both cried and blamed each other.

They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that trading is not always a good idea. They learned that they should be happy with what they have. They learned that they should be careful with their toys and their friends.

Anna likes math. She likes to count and add and take away. She has a yellow book with math games. She plays with the book every day.

One day, Anna goes to the park with her mom. She sees a boy with a red book. The boy is doing math too. Anna wants to play with him.

"Hi, I am Anna. I like math. Can I see your book?" Anna asks the boy.

"Hi, I am Ben. I like math too. This is my book. It has hard math. Do you know hard math?" Ben asks Anna.

Anna looks at the book. She sees big numbers and signs. She does not know hard math. She feels sad.

"I do not know hard math. I only know easy math. Can we play easy math?" Anna asks Ben.

Ben thinks for a moment. He likes hard math, but he also likes to make friends. He smiles at Anna.

"OK, we can play easy math. You can use my book, and I can use your book. Maybe you can teach me some easy math, and I can teach you some hard math. Do you want to do that?" Ben asks Anna.

Anna feels happy. She nods and smiles back.

"Yes, I want to do that. Thank you, Ben. You are a nice friend. Let's play math!" Anna says.

Anna and Ben sit on the grass and share their books. They play math and have fun. They learn from each other and help each other. They are happy.

One day, a jolly elephant named Ellie went for a walk in the jungle. She saw a little monkey hanging from a tree. The monkey looked sad.

"Hello, monkey. Why are you sad?" Ellie asked.

"I want to learn how to use my tail like you use your trunk. But I don't know how," the monkey said.

Ellie smiled. "I can teach you. My trunk is very useful. I can pick up things, spray water, and make noises with it. Do you want to try?"

The monkey nodded. "Yes, please. That sounds fun."

Ellie showed the monkey how to curl her trunk around a banana and bring it to her mouth. The monkey tried to do the same with his tail, but he dropped the banana.

"That's okay. Try again. You can do it," Ellie encouraged.

The monkey tried again and again, until he finally managed to grab the banana with his tail and eat it. He was very happy.

"Thank you, Ellie. You are a good teacher. And your trunk is amazing," the monkey said.

"You're welcome, monkey. And your tail is also amazing. You can swing from tree to tree with it. Can you show me how?" Ellie asked.

The monkey nodded. "Yes, I can. Come with me. I'll teach you."

The monkey and Ellie became friends. They taught each other how to use their tails and trunks. They had a lot of fun in the jungle. They were both very jolly.

One day, Sara has a funny idea. She finds a bucket and fills it with water. She sneaks behind Ben and pours the water on his head. Ben is wet and surprised. He says, "Hey, Sara, that's not fair!"

Sara giggles and runs away. Ben chases her with the hose. He sprays water at her. Sara screams and dodges. They run around the garden, spraying and pouring water at each other. They are wet and happy.

Mom watches them from the window. She smiles and shakes her head. She thinks, "My kids are so funny. They love to play with water. They are good friends." She goes to the kitchen and makes some lemonade. She calls them, "Sara, Ben, come and have a drink. You must be thirsty."

Sara and Ben stop playing and run to Mom. They hug her and say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. And we love water." They drink the lemonade and dry themselves with towels. They tell Mom about their water game. Mom listens and laughs. She says, "You are very clever and creative. But next time, be careful not to waste too much water. Water is precious."

Sara and Ben nod and say, "OK, Mom. We understand. We will be careful." They go to their room and play with their toys. They are still wet and funny. They are happy.

One day, her mom comes to her room and says, "Sara, we need to remove some things from your room. We have to make space for your new bed. You are a big girl now, and you need a big bed."

Sara does not want to remove anything from her room. She likes all her things. She says, "No, mom, I need my things. They are mine. I do not want a new bed. I like my old bed."

Mom says, "I know, Sara, but you have too many things. You can keep some of them, but not all. How about we remove some of your poems? You can choose which ones you want to keep, and which ones you want to give away. Maybe you can give some to your friends, or to your teacher, or to grandma. They would love your poems."

Sara thinks for a moment. She loves her poems, but she also loves her friends, and her teacher, and her grandma. She says, "Okay, mom, I will remove some of my poems. But only some. I will keep the ones that are very special to me. And I will give the others to the people who will like them."

Mom smiles and hugs Sara. She says, "That's very kind of you, Sara. I'm proud of you. You are a big girl, and a good writer. Now, let's go and choose which poems you want to keep, and which ones you want to remove."

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big stick. They decided to use it as a flag.

"Let's march with our flag!" Lily said. "We can be soldiers!"

"OK!" Ben said. "But where do we march to?"

Lily looked around. She saw a big hill. "Let's march to the hill!" she said. "It will be fun!"

They picked up the stick and started to march. They sang a song as they marched. "We are soldiers, we are brave, we march to the hill, we march to the hill!"

But the stick was not very flexible. It was stiff and hard. As they marched, the stick hit a rock. It broke in two.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Our flag is broken!"

Ben looked sad. He liked the flag. He wanted to march with it.

But Lily had an idea. She smiled. She picked up one piece of the stick. She gave the other piece to Ben.

"Look!" she said. "Now we have two flags! We can march with one in each hand!"

Ben smiled too. He liked the idea. He took the piece of stick from Lily.

"Let's march with our two flags!" he said. "We are still soldiers, we are still brave, we march to the hill, we march to the hill!"

They picked up their two flags and started to march again. They sang their song louder. They were happy. They were flexible. They marched to the hill.

"Yum, these are sweet and juicy!" Lily said.

"Let's take some home and share with our moms!" Max said.

They filled their pockets with blueberries and ran back to the house. But on the way, they saw a big dog. The dog was dirty and hungry. He barked at them and chased them.

"Help, help!" Lily and Max cried.

They ran as fast as they could, but the dog was faster. He caught up with them and jumped on them. He knocked them down and made them drop their blueberries. The blueberries rolled on the ground and got dirty.

"Go away, bad dog!" Lily and Max shouted.

But the dog did not go away. He sniffed the blueberries and licked them. He liked them too. He wagged his tail and licked Lily and Max's faces. He was not a bad dog. He was a friendly dog.

"Maybe he just wanted some blueberries," Lily said.

"Maybe he was lonely and wanted some friends," Max said.

"You two are very kind and brave," their moms said.

"Can we keep him, mom?" Lily and Max asked.

Their moms looked at each other and nodded.

"Sure, but you have to take good care of him," their moms said.

Lily and Max were very happy. They named the dog Berry and hugged him. They had a new friend and a new pet. They had united with the dog and the blueberries. They were a happy family.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their dad. They saw a big pile of lumber near the playground. It was brown and hard and had nails in it.

"Can we play with the lumber, dad?" Ben asked.

"No, you can't. The lumber is bad for you. It can hurt you with the nails or give you splinters. Stay away from it, please," dad said.

Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the swings. They had fun swinging high and low. But then, Ben saw something shiny in the lumber. He wanted to see what it was.

He got off the swing and walked to the lumber. He did not listen to dad. He reached out his hand to touch the shiny thing.

"Lily, look! I found a coin in the lumber!" Ben shouted.

Lily looked and saw Ben near the lumber. She was scared. She knew Ben was doing something bad.

She got off the swing and ran to Ben. She grabbed his arm and pulled him away from the lumber.

"Ben, no! You are not supposed to play with the lumber! Dad said it is bad for you! Come back to the swings!" Lily said.

She pointed to the swings and to dad. She wanted Ben to follow her.

Ben felt a sharp pain in his hand. He looked and saw a nail sticking out of his palm. He had touched the nail when he grabbed the coin. He dropped the coin and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, it hurts!" Ben cried.

Dad heard Ben's cry and ran to him. He saw the nail in his hand and the blood on his fingers. He was angry and worried.

"Ben, what did you do? I told you not to play with the lumber! You could have been seriously hurt! Let me see your hand, I need to take you to the doctor," dad said.

He took the nail out of Ben's hand and wrapped it with a cloth. He picked up Ben and carried him to the car. He also took Lily with him.

Ben was sorry for not listening to dad. He learned his lesson. He never played with the lumber again. He said sorry to dad and Lily. He thanked Lily for trying to help him. He hugged them both.

The end.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with cars and trucks. They had a big box of cars and trucks in Tim's room. One day, they decided to have a race with their cars and trucks.

"Let's see who has the fastest car or truck," said Tim. "We can use the hall as a track."

"OK," said Sam. "But I have the best car. It is red and shiny and has a big engine. It can go very fast."

Tim looked at Sam's car. It was red and shiny and had a big engine. But Tim had a secret. He had a special part for his car. It was a rocket. He had found it in his dad's garage. He had put it on his car with some tape.

"Are you ready?" said Tim. "Let's go to the hall and start the race."

They went to the hall and put their cars and trucks on the floor. They drew a line with a crayon. That was the start line. They drew another line with a crayon. That was the finish line.

"Ready, set, go!" said Tim. They pushed their cars and trucks with their hands. Sam's car zoomed ahead. It was very fast. Tim's car was behind. But then, Tim pressed a button on his car. The rocket part made a loud noise and a big flame. Tim's car flew past Sam's car. It was faster than Sam's car. It was faster than any car or truck. It was faster than the speed of sound.

"Wow!" said Tim. "Look at my car go!"

But Tim's car was too fast. It did not stop at the finish line. It crashed into the wall. The rocket part broke. The car broke. The wall broke. There was a big hole in the wall. There was smoke and dust and pieces of car and rocket and wall everywhere.

"Uh-oh," said Tim. "That was a terrible crash."

Sam looked at the mess. He looked at Tim. He looked at his car. His car was still whole. It was still red and shiny and had a big engine.

"Tim," said Sam. "You cheated. You used a rocket part. That is not fair. And you broke the wall. That is bad. Your mom and dad will be very angry."

Tim felt sorry. He felt sad. He felt scared. He wished he had not used the rocket part. He wished he had not broken the wall. He wished he had not cheated.

"I'm sorry, Sam," said Tim. "You are right. I cheated. I used a rocket part. That was not fair. And I broke the wall. That was bad. My mom and dad will be very angry. Please don't be mad at me. Can we still be friends?"

Sam thought for a moment. He was still mad at Tim. But he was also Tim's best friend. He did not want to lose Tim as a friend.

"OK, Tim," said Sam. "I forgive you. But you have to tell your mom and dad what you did. And you have to help me clean up this mess. And you have to share your cars and trucks with me. And you have to promise not to use a rocket part again. Ever."

Tim nodded. He agreed to do all those things. He was glad that Sam forgave him. He was glad that they were still friends. He learned a lesson. He learned that cheating is wrong. He learned that rockets are dangerous. He learned that speed is not everything. He learned that friendship is more important.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the plants and flowers. They saw some red things on a green plant. They were tomatoes.

"Look, tomatoes!" Ben said. "I want one."

"Me too," Lily said. "Let's take one each."

They picked two tomatoes from the plant. They were juicy and sweet. They smiled and ate them.

But then they saw another tomato. It was bigger and redder than the others. They both wanted it.

"I saw it first," Ben said. "It's mine."

"No, it's mine," Lily said. "You already had one."

They started to pull the tomato. They were selfish. They did not want to share.

"Stop it!" a voice said. It was Mom. She came to the garden. She saw Ben and Lily fighting over the tomato.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked. "Why are you taking tomatoes from the plant?"

"We were hungry," Ben said.

"We like tomatoes," Lily said.

Mom shook her head. She was not happy.

"Tomatoes are not for taking," Mom said. "They are for growing. You have to wait until they are ripe and then ask before you take them. And you have to share with each other. Taking and being selfish is not nice."

Ben and Lily felt sorry. They did not want to make Mom sad. They did not want to be selfish.

"Sorry, Mom," Ben said.

"Sorry, Mom," Lily said.

They gave the tomato to Mom. Mom smiled and hugged them.

"It's okay," Mom said. "I forgive you. But next time, be more careful and kind. And if you want a tomato, I have some in the kitchen. You can have one each, if you say please and thank you."

Ben and Lily nodded. They said please and thank you. They followed Mom to the kitchen. They had another tomato. They shared and were happy.

Tim and Lily liked to play on the farm. They liked to see the cows, the pigs, the chickens and the horses. But they were not allowed to go near the stable. The stable was where the big horses lived. The farmer said the horses were too strong and fast for them. He said they could get hurt if they went inside.

One day, Tim and Lily were bored. They wanted to have some fun. They saw the farmer go away in his truck. They thought he would not be back for a long time. They decided to sneak to the stable. They wanted to see the horses up close.

They found the door of the stable. It was locked with a big padlock. Tim remembered where the farmer kept the key. He ran to the shed and got the key. He came back and unlocked the door. He opened it a little bit and peeked inside. He saw a brown horse with a white spot on its nose. It looked friendly.

"Come on, Lily, let's go in!" Tim said.

"Are you sure, Tim? What if the farmer comes back?" Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily, we'll be quick. And we'll lock the door again when we leave. Come on, it'll be fun!" Tim said.

He pushed the door open and went inside. Lily followed him. They walked slowly to the horse. The horse saw them and neighed. It moved its head and licked Tim's hand. Tim giggled.

"Hi, horse, you're so nice. Can we pet you?" Tim said.

The horse nodded and let them stroke its mane and back. Tim and Lily felt happy. They forgot about the farmer and the time.

They did not see the other horse in the corner. The other horse was black and had a scar on its eye. It did not like strangers. It did not like children. It did not like noise. It heard Tim and Lily and got angry. It snorted and kicked the wall. It broke the rope that tied it to the post. It ran towards Tim and Lily. It was fast and furious.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with green and black balls on it. Sara wanted to pick some and eat them, but Ben was not sure.

"Those are olives," Ben said. "My mom puts them on pizza sometimes. But I don't know if they are good from the tree."

"Let's discuss it," Sara said. "Maybe we can try one and see if we like it."

They climbed the tree and each took an olive. They bit into them and made a face. The olives were bitter and salty and made their mouths dry.

"Yuck!" Sara said. "These are not good at all. Let's spit them out."

They spat out the olives and climbed down the tree. They ran to the water fountain and drank some water. They felt better and decided to play on the swings instead.

"Next time, let's not eat things we don't know," Ben said.

"Yes, that's a good idea," Sara said. "It's safer to eat what our moms give us."

They smiled and swung high in the air. They were happy and forgot about the olives. They did not see the angry man who owned the tree and who did not like children picking his olives. He was coming to the park with a big stick. He was going to teach them a lesson. But that's another story.

Tim and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys and watch TV. They also like to sing songs and make funny noises. One day, they see a big poster on the wall. It has a picture of a man with a guitar and a microphone. The poster says: "Come and see Bob, the famous singer!"

"Wow, look at that!" Tim says. "He is famous. He can sing very well. I want to be like him."

"Me too," Lily says. "He looks happy and cool. Let's go and see him."

They ask their mom if they can go to the concert. Their mom says yes, but they have to be good and stay with her. She buys them tickets and they get ready to go.

At the concert, there are many people. They are loud and excited. Tim and Lily hold their mom's hand and follow her to their seats. They see a big stage with lights and speakers. They wait for Bob to come out.

Soon, the music starts and Bob appears. He has a guitar and a microphone. He smiles and waves to the crowd. He sings his songs and everyone claps and cheers. Tim and Lily like his songs. They sing along and make funny noises.

But then, something happens. Bob stops singing. He coughs and holds his mouth. He looks worried. He says: "I'm sorry, everyone. I have a sore throat. I can't sing anymore. I have to go."

The crowd is quiet and sad. Some people boo and some people say: "Get well soon, Bob!"

Tim and Lily are also sad. They wanted to hear more songs. They wonder what is wrong with Bob's mouth.

They ask their mom: "Mom, why did Bob stop singing? Is he sick? Does his mouth hurt?"

Their mom says: "Yes, he is sick. He has a sore throat. His mouth hurts when he tries to sing. He needs to rest and drink some water. Maybe he will sing again another day."

Tim and Lily feel sorry for Bob. They hope he will get better soon. They say: "Poor Bob. We like his songs. We hope his mouth feels better."

They give him a big hug in their minds. They think he is still famous and cool. They still want to be like him.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They find a big stick. They use the stick to draw in the sand. They make shapes and letters and animals.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a harsh noise. It hurts their ears. They look up and see a big truck. The truck is coming to the park. It is going to make the sand flat.

Lila and Ben are scared. They run away from the truck. They forget the stick. They forget their drawings. They only want to be safe.

They find their mom and dad. They hug them. They tell them about the truck. Mom and dad say they are sorry. They say they are proud of Lila and Ben for being brave.

Lila and Ben feel better. They still miss the stick and the drawings. But they know they can make new ones. They know they have each other. They are still friends.

Lila and Tom are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses with the blocks. Lila is bossy. She tells Tom what to do with the blocks. She says, "Put this block here. No, not there. Here. And this block goes on top. No, not like that. Like this."

Tom is tired of Lila's bossy voice. He wants to play his own way. He says, "Stop telling me what to do. I can build my own tower. You are not the boss of me."

Lila gets angry. She says, "Yes, I am. I am the boss of the blocks. And you are doing it wrong. You are making a mess. Give me that block. Now!"

She tries to grab the block from Tom's hand. But Tom holds on tight. They pull and tug on the block. The block slips from their fingers. It falls to the floor. It makes a loud noise. It hits the other blocks. The other blocks fall down too. They drop to the floor. They make a bigger noise. They scatter on all sides.

Lila and Tom look at the mess. They are scared. They hear footsteps. They see Mom coming. She looks at the mess. She looks at them. She is not happy. She says, "What happened here? Who made this mess? Why did you drop the blocks?"

Lila and Tom are quiet. They do not know what to say. They feel sorry. They look at each other. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We were playing with the blocks. We had a fight. We dropped the blocks. We did not mean to."

Mom sighs. She says, "I see. Well, fighting is not nice. And dropping the blocks is not careful. You need to share the blocks. And you need to pick up the blocks. Can you do that?"

Lila and Tom nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. We can do that. We will share the blocks. And we will pick up the blocks. We will be nice. And we will be careful."

Mom smiles. She says, "That's good. I'm glad you can do that. Now, let's clean up this mess. And then you can play with the blocks again. But this time, no more bossy voices. And no more dropping blocks. OK?"

Lila and Tom say, "OK, Mom. Thank you, Mom." They hug Mom. They hug each other. They start to pick up the blocks. They put them in the box. They say, "Sorry, blocks. We will be gentle with you. We will not drop you again."

The end.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big kangaroo in the field. They wanted to touch it and feed it grass. They ran after the kangaroo, but it was too fast. It hopped away and they lost it.

"Let's search for the kangaroo," Lily said. "Maybe it is hiding behind the trees."

"OK," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. Mom said we should not go too far from the house."

They searched for the kangaroo, but they could not find it. They went deeper and deeper into the woods. They did not see the signs that said "Danger" and "Keep Out". They did not hear the growls and snarls of the wild animals.

Suddenly, they saw a big bear. It was angry and hungry. It saw them and roared. It ran towards them with its sharp teeth and claws.

"Help!" Lily and Ben screamed. "This is terrible! We want to go home!"

But it was too late. The bear caught them and ate them. They never saw their mom and dad again.

The moral of the story is: Do not chase after things that you do not know. Listen to your parents and stay safe.

Ben and Sam were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, Ben saw a new book on Sam's shelf. It had a picture of a big house and a magnifying glass. Ben asked Sam, "What is that book?"

Sam said, "That is my mystery book. It is very fun. It has stories of people who solve problems and find clues. Do you want to read it?"

Ben said, "Yes, please. Can you lend it to me?"

Sam said, "Okay, but you have to be careful. It is my favorite book. And you have to give it back tomorrow."

Ben said, "I will. Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend."

Ben took the book and went home. He read the book and liked it very much. He wanted to read more. He forgot to give it back to Sam the next day. And the next day. And the next day.

Sam was sad and angry. He waited for Ben to bring his book. He asked Ben many times, "Where is my book? When will you give it back?"

Ben said, "I don't know. I lost it. I'm sorry, Sam."

Sam did not believe Ben. He thought Ben was lying. He thought Ben kept his book or gave it to someone else. He said, "You are not sorry. You are not honest. You are not my friend anymore."

Ben felt bad. He wanted to tell Sam the truth. He wanted to say he still had the book and he was sorry. But he was afraid Sam would not forgive him. He was afraid Sam would hate him. He did not know what to do.

He kept the book and lost a friend. He was not happy. He learned a hard lesson. He wished he had been honest and given the book back. He wished he had not hurt Sam. He wished he could have another chance. But it was too late. The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big structure with slides and swings and ladders. They wanted to go on it and have fun.

"Come, Ben, let's go on the structure!" Lily said.

"OK, Lily, let's go!" Ben said.

They ran to the structure and climbed up the ladder. They saw a pretty view of the park and the sky. They smiled and waved to each other.

But then they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you two, get off my structure!" It was Max, a big boy who liked to bully other kids. He was on the other side of the structure, and he looked angry.

"This is my structure, and you can't play on it!" Max said.

Lily and Ben felt scared. They didn't want to fight with Max, but they also didn't want to leave the structure. They liked the structure, and they wanted to share it with other kids.

"Please, Max, can we play on the structure too?" Lily asked.

"No, you can't! This is mine, and you have to go away!" Max said.

He started to walk towards them, and he looked mean.

Lily and Ben didn't know what to do. They looked at each other, and they had an idea.

They slid down the slide, and they ran to the swings. They got on the swings, and they started to swing high and fast.

They laughed and shouted, "Weee, this is fun!"

Max saw them, and he felt angry. He wanted to chase them, but he couldn't. He was stuck on the structure, and he didn't know how to get down.

He yelled, "Hey, come back here! Help me get down!"

But Lily and Ben didn't listen. They kept swinging and having fun.

They learned that the structure was not for one kid, but for all kids. And they learned that sharing was better than fighting.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they find a telephone in the garage. It is old and dusty, but it has buttons and a cord.

"Let's play with the telephone!" Anna says. "We can call someone and joke with them."

"OK!" Ben says. "Who do you want to call?"

Anna thinks for a moment. She remembers that her grandma is healthy and happy. She likes to talk to her grandma.

"Let's call grandma!" Anna says. "She will be surprised to hear us."

Ben nods. He picks up the telephone and presses some buttons. He puts the telephone to his ear.

"Hello?" a voice says.

"Hello, grandma!" Ben says. "This is Ben. I have a joke for you."

"Ben? Is that you?" the voice says. "How did you get this number?"

Ben smiles. He looks at Anna. She smiles too.

"Grandma, why did the chicken cross the road?" Ben says.

The voice laughs. "I don't know, Ben. Why did the chicken cross the road?"

Ben says, "To get to the other side!"

The voice laughs again. "That's a funny joke, Ben. You made me laugh. Thank you for calling me."

Ben says, "You're welcome, grandma. I love you."

"I love you too, Ben. And who is with you?"

Ben says, "This is Anna. She is my friend. She wants to say hello to you."

Ben gives the telephone to Anna. Anna says, "Hello, grandma. I'm Anna. I like your joke too."

The voice says, "Hello, Anna. I'm glad you're Ben's friend. You sound very sweet."

Anna says, "Thank you, grandma. You sound very nice."

The voice says, "Thank you, Anna. You and Ben are very kind. I hope you have fun playing with the telephone."

Anna says, "We will, grandma. Bye-bye."

The voice says, "Bye-bye, Anna. Bye-bye, Ben. Take care."

Anna and Ben hang up the telephone. They hug each other. They are happy. They made grandma laugh. They played with the telephone. They had fun.

Tom goes first. He steps on the scale. The scale says he is 30 pounds. Tom is happy. He thinks he is strong. He tells Sue to go next.

Sue steps on the scale. The scale says she is 28 pounds. Sue is sad. She thinks she is weak. She tells Tom he is mean.

Tom does not understand. He says he is not mean. He says he is just telling the truth. He says Sue is ignorant. Ignorant means you do not know things.

Sue gets angry. She says Tom is ignorant. She says he does not know how to be nice. She says she does not want to be his friend.

Tom and Sue start to fight. They push and pull and yell. They do not have fun. They do not see the big sign on the scale. The sign says the scale is broken. The scale does not tell the truth. The scale is ignorant.

One day, a boy was playing with his ball in the park. He liked to kick the ball very hard and see how far it would go. He did not look where he was kicking, and he did not care if he hit anyone or anything.

Soon, he kicked the ball so hard that it flew over the fence and hit a girl who was riding her bike. The girl fell off her bike and hurt her knee. She cried and cried, and her mom came to help her.

The boy saw what he had done, and he felt bad. He ran to the fence and said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I did not mean to hurt you. Are you okay?"

The girl looked at him and said, "No, I'm not okay. You hurt me with your ball. You should look where you are kicking, and you should care about others. That is not nice."

The boy nodded and said, "You are right, I should. I was being selfish and rude. I will be more careful and kind next time. Can I help you with anything?"

The girl smiled and said, "Thank you for saying sorry and for being kind. You can help me by getting my bike and my helmet. And maybe we can play together later, if you want."

The boy agreed and did as she asked. He learned his lesson and became a better friend. He also learned to look where he was kicking, and to care about others. That is the moral of the story.

When they came back to their snowmen, they saw a big dog. The dog was hungry and angry. It did not like snowmen. It bit and tore them apart. It made a big mess. Anna and Ben were sad and scared. They cried and ran to their house.

Lila was a bird who loved to sing. She sang every morning and every evening, and sometimes in the day too. She sang songs about the sun, the sky, the flowers and the trees. She sang songs that made her happy, and songs that made her sad. She sang songs that were fast, and songs that were slow.

Lila's voice was very pretty, and many other birds liked to listen to her. They came to the big tree where she lived, and sat on the branches near her. They clapped their wings and cheered when she finished a song. They asked her to sing more songs, and to teach them how to sing too. Lila was very popular, and she had many friends.

But not all the birds liked Lila's singing. Some birds were jealous of her, and wanted to be popular too. They said mean things about her, and tried to make her stop singing. They said her voice was too loud, or too soft, or too high, or too low. They said her songs were boring, or silly, or wrong. They said she was selfish, or rude, or proud.

Lila felt sad when she heard these words. She wondered if they were true, and if she should stop singing. She wondered if her friends really liked her, or if they only liked her songs. She wondered if she was doing something bad, or if the other birds were just mean.

One day, a wise owl came to the big tree. He heard Lila's singing, and he liked it very much. He also heard the mean words, and he did not like them at all. He flew to Lila's branch, and spoke to her.

"Lila, you have a wonderful gift. Your singing makes many birds happy, and that is a good thing. Do not listen to the mean birds, they are just unhappy with themselves. They want to make you unhappy too, but you can choose to ignore them. Keep singing, Lila, and be proud of who you are. You have many friends who love you, and I am one of them."

Lila felt happy when she heard these words. She thanked the owl, and gave him a hug. She decided to keep singing, and to enjoy her gift. She sang a song of gratitude, and the owl sang along. The other birds heard them, and joined them too. They sang a song of friendship, and harmony, and joy. Lila was very happy, and she had many friends.

Lily and Tom were playing in their room. They had many toys, but they liked to pretend they were explorers. They used a big box as a boat, and a lamp as a torch.

"Let's go to the island of treasure!" Tom said. He turned on the lamp and shone it around the room. "Look, there's a cave!"

"No, it's mine! I found it!" she said. She put the necklace around her neck and closed the box.

Lily was sad. She wanted Anna to be warm and cozy. She had an idea. She went to her room and found her old belt. It was fat and long. She wrapped it around Anna like a coat. She used the buckle to close it. She said, "There, now Anna has a coat. She is not cold."

She went outside with Anna. She saw her friend Tom. Tom had a truck. He liked to play with his truck. He saw Lily and Anna. He said, "Hi, Lily. What is that on your doll? It looks funny."

Lily said, "It is a coat. Anna is warm and cozy."

Tom said, "It is not a coat. It is a belt. It is fat and long. It does not fit your doll. It looks silly."

Lily was angry. She said, "It is not silly. It is nice. Anna likes it. You are mean."

Tom said, "No, I am not mean. I am honest. You should remove the belt from your doll. It is not a coat. It is a belt."

Lily did not want to remove the belt. She liked the belt. She said, "No, I will not remove it. It is mine. You go away."

Tom said, "Fine. I will go away. But you are silly. And your doll is silly too."

He took his truck and left. Lily was sad. She hugged Anna. She said, "Don't worry, Anna. You are not silly. You are beautiful. And I love you."

Lily pushes the train and says "freeze". Sam stops the train and looks at it. The train is on a bridge over a river. Sam says "The train is going over the water. It is going to the city". Lily says "Yes, you are right. Now it is your turn".

The bear wanted the stone so badly, so he was very patient. He stayed beside the stone, trying to figure out how to move it, even though the sun was setting soon and he would have to go home. Suddenly, he realized that if he moved his feet back and forth in front of the stone, it eventually shifted!

The bear was so happy that he moved the stone. He was also very proud of himself for being patient and not giving up! The bear said to himself, â€œNext time I want something, remember to stay patient, because good things come to those who are patient!â€ And from then on, he always tried to be patient and display good qualities.

Lily and her mom continued walking, and they saw a man sitting on a bench. The man looked sad, so Lily asked her mom, "Why is the man sad?" Her mom said, "Maybe he is feeling unknown and needs someone to talk to." 

Lily went up to the man and said, "Hi, my name is Lily. Do you want to talk to me?" The man smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. I would love to talk to you." They spent some time talking, and the man felt much better. 

The moral of the story is that spending time with someone and being kind can make a big difference in their life.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very lonely because he had no friends to play with. One day, Tweety decided to go to the park to see if he could find a friend. 

At the park, Tweety saw a little girl named Lily. Tweety went up to Lily and said, "Hi, do you want to be my friend?" Lily said, "Yes, I would love to be your friend!" 

Tweety was so happy to have a friend. He said to Lily, "Let me show you something!" Tweety flew up into the sky and then suddenly, a big firework went off. Lily was amazed and said, "Wow, that was so cool!" 

Tweety and Lily played together all day and had so much fun. Tweety was no longer lonely because he had found a friend. The moral of the story is that it's important to make friends and share fun experiences with them.

"Help!" she cried. "The dog is chasing us!"

"Tim, Lily, where are you?" she called.

"Oh, you poor things," their mom said. "That dog must have been very mean. I'm sorry you lost your ball."

"That's okay, mom," Tim said. "We don't need the ball. We have each other."

"Bye, bye, raven!" Tom and Mia said. "You are so big and black and pretty and shiny!"

Tom and Mia went back to play. They did not touch the raven. They learned that some birds do not like to be touched. They were happy to play in the park.

Lily liked to look at the fish in the big glass tank. She saw many colors and shapes. Some fish were big and some were small. Some had long tails and some had spots. Lily wanted to touch the fish, but Mom said no. The glass was hard and cold, and the fish were happy in the water.

One day, Lily saw a new fish in the tank. It was very pretty and shiny. It had a round body and a long thin mouth. It looked like a star. Lily wanted to be friends with the star fish. She waved at it and smiled. The star fish seemed to smile back. It came close to the glass and opened its mouth. Lily thought it wanted to talk to her.

Lily leaned forward and put her mouth on the glass. She tried to say hello to the star fish. But the star fish did not say hello. It bit Lily's lip. Lily felt a sharp pain and cried out loud. She pulled back and saw blood on the glass. The star fish swam away. It did not seem friendly anymore. It seemed mean and hungry.

Mom heard Lily's cry and ran to her. She saw the blood and the bite mark. She hugged Lily and said sorry. She took Lily to the bathroom and cleaned her lip. She put a band-aid on it and kissed it. She told Lily that the star fish was not a good friend. It was a bad fish that liked to hurt people. She said Lily should not touch the glass or the fish again.

Lily felt sad and scared. She did not like the star fish anymore. She did not like the glass tank anymore. She wanted to go home and play with her toys. She wanted to cuddle with her teddy bear. Her teddy bear was soft and warm. Her teddy bear was a good friend. Her teddy bear made her feel comfortable.
