Sam liked to drive his toy car. He had a red car that made vroom sounds when he pushed it. He drove it all over the house, on the floor, on the couch, on the table. He drove it so fast that sometimes it crashed into things and made a mess.

One day, his mom said, "Sam, you need to learn how to drive better. You can't just drive your car anywhere you want. You might break something or hurt someone. I have a surprise for you. I hired a tutor to teach you how to drive."

Sam was curious. He wondered who the tutor was and what he would do. He hoped the tutor was nice and had fun cars to play with. He followed his mom to the door and waited for the tutor to arrive.

Soon, there was a knock on the door. His mom opened it and said, "Hello, Mr. Bear. Thank you for coming. This is Sam, my son. He loves to drive his toy car, but he needs some help with the rules of the road."

Sam looked up and saw a big, brown, fuzzy bear holding a book and a hat. He was wearing a blue shirt and a tie. He smiled and said, "Hello, Sam. I'm Mr. Bear, your tutor. I'm here to teach you how to drive safely and politely. Are you ready to learn?"

Sam was a little scared of the bear, but he also wanted to learn. He nodded and said, "Yes, Mr. Bear. I want to learn how to drive better. Can we play with my car?"

Mr. Bear said, "Of course, we can play with your car. But first, we need to read this book. It has pictures and words that show you how to drive. It tells you what the signs mean, when to stop and go, how to share the road with others, and how to avoid accidents. It's very important to know these things before you drive."

Sam and Mr. Bear sat on the floor and read the book together. Sam learned a lot of new things. He learned what red, yellow, and green lights mean. He learned what a crosswalk, a stop sign, and a yield sign are. He learned how to use his horn, his blinkers, and his mirrors. He learned how to say sorry, thank you, and excuse me to other drivers.

After they finished the book, Mr. Bear said, "Now, let's practice what we learned. Let's take your car and drive around the house. But remember, you have to follow the rules of the road. I'll be your passenger and your coach. I'll tell you what to do and what not to do. Are you ready?"

Sam said, "Yes, Mr. Bear. I'm ready. Let's go!"

Sam and Mr. Bear took the car and drove around the house. Sam followed the rules of the road. He stopped at the red lights, he went at the green lights, he slowed down at the yellow lights. He looked both ways before crossing the street. He used his horn, his blinkers, and his mirrors. He shared the road with others. He said sorry, thank you, and excuse me to other drivers.

Mr. Bear was very proud of Sam. He said, "Sam, you are doing a great job. You are a very good driver. You are safe and polite. You are a smart and kind boy. I'm very happy to be your tutor."

Sam was very happy too. He said, "Thank you, Mr. Bear. You are a very good tutor. You are fun and helpful. You are a nice and friendly bear. I'm very happy to be your student."

They drove around the house for a while, having fun and learning. They didn't crash into anything or hurt anyone. They made a lot of vroom sounds and laughed a lot.

Sam's mom watched them from the window. She smiled and said, "I'm so glad I hired Mr. Bear. He is a wonderful tutor. He taught Sam how to drive better. He made Sam happy and proud. He is a great friend."

Tom and Lily were frogs who lived in a big swamp. They liked to hop on the lily pads and catch flies with their tongues. They were friends since they were tadpoles, and they loved each other very much.

One day, Tom said to Lily, "Lily, you are the best frog in the swamp. You are pretty and smart and kind. I want to be with you always. Will you marry me?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Tom, I will marry you. You are the best frog in the swamp too. You are strong and brave and funny. I want to be with you always too."

They hugged and kissed and decided to ask the wise old turtle to marry them. The wise old turtle lived in a log at the edge of the swamp. He knew many things and helped the other animals when they had problems.

They hopped to the log and found the wise old turtle sunning himself. They said, "Hello, wise old turtle. We are Tom and Lily, and we love each other very much. We want to get married. Will you marry us?"

The wise old turtle looked at them and said, "Hello, Tom and Lily. I am happy for you. You are good frogs and you make each other happy. I will marry you, but first you must do something for me."

They said, "What do we have to do, wise old turtle?"

The wise old turtle said, "You have to promise me that you will always be faithful, respectful, and supportive of each other. You have to promise me that you will always share, care, and dare with each other. You have to promise me that you will always love, laugh, and learn with each other. Can you do that?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other and said, "Yes, wise old turtle, we can do that. We promise."

The wise old turtle said, "Then I will marry you. Repeat after me: I, Tom, take you, Lily, to be my wife. I, Lily, take you, Tom, to be my husband."

They repeated the words and the wise old turtle said, "By the power of the swamp, I now pronounce you frog and frog. You may kiss the bride."

They kissed and the wise old turtle said, "Congratulations, Tom and Lily. You are now married. I wish you a long and happy life together in the swamp."

They thanked the wise old turtle and hopped away, holding hands. They were very happy and they lived happily ever after in the swamp.

One day, her father found out that she had missed her lesson again. He was very angry and said, "Anna, you are a bad princess. You have to learn how to read and write and count. You have to learn how to be a good ruler. If you do not learn, you will not be ready to be a queen. You will punish me and yourself and the people."

Anna felt scared and sad. She did not want to punish her father or herself or the people. She said, "I am sorry, father. I do not mean to be bad. I just do not like learning. It is not fun. Can I not play instead?"

Her father shook his head and said, "No, Anna. Playing is good, but learning is important. You have to do both. You have to balance your time and your duties. As a punishment, you will not play for a week. You will only learn. You will stay in your room and study with your tutor. Maybe then you will understand why learning is valuable."

Anna cried and begged her father to change his mind, but he did not. He sent her to her room and locked the door. Anna felt lonely and miserable. She wished she had listened to her father and learned. She realized that learning was not only boring and hard, but also useful and rewarding. She decided to try harder and make her father proud. She hoped that one day, she would be a good queen.

As Tim went down the hill, he went faster and faster. He saw a big rock in his way but could not stop. The great bicycle hit the rock and broke. Tim was sad, and his shiny bicycle was not shiny anymore.

One day, a girl named Sue found a vase. The vase was big and hard. She wanted to make it look nice. So, she went to find some pretty things to put in it.

Sue saw a tree with pretty flowers. She picked the flowers and ran back to the vase. She put the flowers in the vase, but they fell out. Sue was sad. Then, her friend Tom came by.

"What's wrong, Sue?" asked Tom. Sue said, "I want to put the flowers in the vase, but they keep falling out." Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's tie the flowers together, so they won't fall out!"

Sue and Tom found a string and tied the flowers together. They put the tied flowers in the vase. The flowers stayed in the vase and did not fall out. Sue and Tom were happy. They had made the hard vase look nice with the tied flowers.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a weird cat. The cat loved to stand on a big rock every day. The cat would stand there and watch the people go by.

One day, a man walked by with a newspaper. The weird cat jumped off the rock and ran to the man. The man saw the cat and smiled. He gave the cat the newspaper to play with.

The cat played with the newspaper all day long. The weird cat was very happy. From that day on, the cat and the man became best friends. They would stand together and read the newspaper every day. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a bright sun in the sky. It made everything look happy and shiny. A little cat named Mimi liked to play outside when the sun was bright. Mimi loved to run, jump, and hide.

One day, Mimi saw a big wall near her home. She thought it would be fun to play hide and seek there. Mimi ran to the wall and hid behind it. She waited for her friend, a little dog named Dodo, to find her.

Dodo looked everywhere for Mimi. He searched near the trees, by the flowers, and behind the rocks. Finally, Dodo found Mimi hiding behind the wall. They both laughed and played together under the bright sun all day long.

Once upon a time, a big black bird named Raven lived in a tree. Raven loved to soar high in the sky. He liked to see the whole world when he flew up, up, up.

One day, Raven saw a pale little girl named Lily. She looked sad. Raven wanted to help Lily. So, he flew down and asked her, "Why are you sad, Lily?"

Lily said, "I want to see the world like you, Raven." Raven thought for a moment. Then, he had an idea. He told Lily to hold on to his wings. Together, they soared high in the sky. Lily was happy, and they both had fun flying and seeing the world.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a chubby bunny named Bobo. He had many friends, but he loved to play with his best friend, Toto the turtle. They always had fun together, laughing and playing all day.

One day, while they were playing, Bobo found an arrow on the ground. He thought it was a toy and wanted to play with it. Toto knew it was not a toy, but he didn't want to make Bobo sad. So, Toto had an idea. He told Bobo to close his eyes and count to ten. While Bobo was counting, Toto hid the arrow behind a big tree.

When Bobo opened his eyes, he saw Toto peeking out from behind the tree. Bobo ran to the tree and found the arrow. Toto said, "Bobo, this is not a toy. It can hurt us. We should give it to a grown-up." Bobo understood and they gave the arrow to a grown-up.

The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to our friends when they try to keep us safe. And always remember, not everything we find is a toy.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a well in the park. The well is deep and dark.

"Look, a well!" Sara says. "I wonder what is inside."

"Maybe there is water, or coins, or frogs," Tom says. "Let's go closer and see."

They walk to the well and look inside. They see nothing but black.

"Hello!" Sara shouts into the well. "Is anyone there?"

Her voice echoes in the well. She hears a strange sound. It sounds like a growl.

"Did you hear that?" Tom asks. "It sounds like a monster!"

Sara feels scared. She wants to run away. But Tom holds her hand.

"Don't be afraid," Tom says. "It is not a monster. It is just a noise. I trust you, and you trust me. We are brave, right?"

Sara nods. She trusts Tom. He is her friend. They are brave.

They decide to throw a stone into the well. They want to see if the noise will stop.

They find a small stone and toss it into the well. They hear a splash and a yelp.

They look at each other and smile. They realize it is not a monster. It is a dog.

They hear the dog bark and wag its tail. It sounds happy and friendly.

"Hello, dog!" Sara calls. "Are you stuck in the well?"

The dog barks again. It wants to get out.

Sara and Tom run to get help. They find a man with a rope. They tell him about the dog in the well.

The man follows them to the well. He lowers the rope into the well. The dog grabs the rope with its teeth. The man pulls the dog out.

The dog is wet and dirty, but it is safe. It licks Sara and Tom's faces. It thanks them for saving it.

Sara and Tom hug the dog. They are happy. They have a new friend.

The man says he will take the dog home. He says he will give it a bath and some tasty food.

Sara and Tom say goodbye to the dog. They hope to see it again.

They go back to play in the park. They are proud of themselves. They have done a good thing. They have learned to trust each other and the dog. They have had a fun adventure.

Lily was a caterpillar who lived on a big green leaf. She liked to eat the leaf and watch the other bugs fly and crawl around. But she was miserable because she could not fly like the butterflies and bees. She wished she had wings and could see the world from the sky.

One day, she saw a butterfly land on her leaf. She said, "Hello, butterfly. You are so pretty and free. How do you fly so high?"

The butterfly smiled and said, "Hello, caterpillar. I was once like you, but then I changed. I made a cozy cocoon and slept for a long time. When I woke up, I had wings and could fly. You will change too, one day. You just have to be patient and trust yourself."

Lily was amazed and curious. She said, "Really? How do I make a cocoon? When will I change?"

The butterfly said, "You will know when it is time. You will feel a pull inside you, and you will find a safe place to spin your silk. Then you will sleep and dream, and when you rise, you will be a butterfly too. It is a wonderful feeling, and you will love it."

Lily thanked the butterfly and felt hopeful. She decided to wait and see what would happen. She ate some more leaf and felt a tickle in her belly. She looked around and saw a branch nearby. She crawled to the branch and started to spin her silk. She wrapped herself in a soft cocoon and felt sleepy. She closed her eyes and dreamed of flying.

After many days, she felt a push inside her. She broke the cocoon and saw the sun shining. She felt something new on her back. She had wings! They were colorful and beautiful. She flapped them and felt a breeze. She rose from the branch and flew into the air. She was a butterfly! She was happy and free. She saw the world from the sky and met many friends. She never felt miserable again.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a pink doll that she loved very much. Max had a car that he liked to zoom around. They were having fun, but they also wanted to see what the other had.

"Can I see your doll?" Max asked Lily.

"OK, but be careful. She is very pretty and soft," Lily said, and handed her doll to Max.

Max looked at the doll and felt her hair and dress. He thought she was nice, but he wanted to see what was inside. He pulled at her arm and tried to open her.

"Stop! You will break her!" Lily cried, and grabbed her doll back.

But it was too late. The doll's arm came off, and some white stuff came out. Lily gasped and started to cry. Max felt bad and said he was sorry.

"I didn't mean to break her. I just wanted to see what she had inside. Maybe we can fix her," Max said.

Lily shook her head and hugged her doll. She was very sad and angry. She didn't want to play with Max anymore.

"Go away! You are mean and you broke my doll. She was my wonder. I don't like you," Lily said.

Max felt sad and angry too. He didn't understand why Lily was so mad. He thought dolls were just toys, and toys could be fixed. He didn't want to lose his friend.

"Please don't be mad. I like you and I like your doll. I have an idea. Let's go to Mom and ask her to help us. Maybe she can sew her arm back and make her new again," Max said.

Lily looked at Max and thought for a moment. She still loved her doll, but she also loved Max. He was her friend, and he said he was sorry. Maybe Mom could help them.

"OK, let's go to Mom. But you have to be more gentle with my doll. She is not a car. She is my wonder," Lily said.

Max nodded and smiled. He took Lily's hand and they ran to Mom. They hoped Mom could fix the doll and make them happy again.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pile of leaves in their yard. They wanted to jump in the leaves and have fun.

"Let's go, Tim!" Sam said. "We can make a big mess with the leaves!"

But Tim was troubled. He saw a rake next to the pile of leaves. He thought the rake was scary. He did not want to go near the rake.

"No, Sam, I don't want to go," Tim said. "The rake is scary. It has sharp teeth. It can hurt us."

Sam laughed. He did not think the rake was scary. He thought the rake was useful. He picked up the rake and waved it in the air.

"Look, Tim, the rake is not scary. It is just a tool. It helps us clean the leaves. See, I can rake the leaves like this," Sam said. He raked some leaves and threw them in the air.

Tim watched Sam rake the leaves. He saw that the rake did not hurt Sam. He saw that the leaves were soft and colorful. He felt less troubled. He wanted to join Sam and play.

"OK, Sam, I will go with you," Tim said. "But can I hold the rake too?"

"Sure, Tim, you can hold the rake too," Sam said. "We can take turns. We can rake the leaves and jump in them. We can have fun together."

Tim and Sam ran to the pile of leaves. They raked the leaves and jumped in them. They laughed and shouted. They were not scared of the rake. They were happy.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. The park has a big gate. The gate is green and has a lock.

One day, Sara and Ben go to the park. They see a dog. The dog is brown and has a red collar. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their hands.

"Hello, dog. What is your name?" Sara asks.

The dog barks. He does not say his name.

"Can we play with you, dog?" Ben asks.

The dog nods. He runs to the gate. He wants to go out.

Sara and Ben follow the dog. They try to open the gate. But the gate is locked. They cannot open it.

The dog whines. He scratches the gate. He wants to go out.

Sara and Ben are sad. They want to help the dog.

They look around. They see a man. The man is tall and has a hat. He has a key. The key is shiny and has a tag.

"Excuse me, sir. Can you help us?" Sara asks.

The man looks at them. He sees the dog. He smiles.

"Sure, I can help you. This is my dog. His name is Max. He ran away from home. I have been looking for him. Thank you for finding him." The man says.

He uses the key to open the gate. He calls Max. Max runs to him. He hugs Max.

Sara and Ben are happy. They are glad that Max has a home.

"Can we pet Max, sir?" Ben asks.

"Of course, you can. Max likes you. You are very kind." The man says.

He lets Sara and Ben pet Max. Max wags his tail and licks their faces.

Sara and Ben laugh. They like Max.

"Thank you, sir. Thank you, Max. You are very nice." Sara and Ben say.

They wave goodbye to the man and Max. They go back to the park. They play until it is dark. They have a good day.

Tom and Anna were children who liked to play in the park. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But one day, they stayed too long and the sun went down. The park became dark and they could not see well.

"Tom, I'm scared. It's too dark. Where is mom?" Anna said.

"Don't worry, Anna. I'm here. Mom will come soon. She knows where we are. Remember, she told us to wait by the big tree." Tom said.

They walked to the big tree and sat under it. They hugged each other and tried to be brave. They heard some noises in the dark. They were birds, squirrels and bugs. They did not like the noises.

"Tom, what is that? It sounds big and scary." Anna said.

"I don't know, Anna. Maybe it's a dog. Or a bear. Or a monster." Tom said.

They closed their eyes and wished for mom to come. They heard footsteps and a voice.

"Tom, Anna, where are you? I'm here. I'm sorry I'm late. I got stuck in traffic." Mom said.

They opened their eyes and saw mom. She had a flashlight and a smile. They ran to her and hugged her. They were happy and relieved.

"Mom, we were so scared. It was so dark and there were noises." Anna said.

"I know, sweetie. I'm sorry. You did a good job staying by the tree. I'm proud of you. And you, Tom, you were a good brother. You helped Anna remember what I said." Mom said.

She took their hands and led them to the car. She gave them cookies and milk. She sang them a song. They felt safe and warm. They forgot about the dark and the noises. They remembered mom's love.

But while they were sliding, a big dog came to the bench. The dog smelled the cubes and thought they were food. He tried to bite the cubes, but they were hard and plastic. He got angry and started to destroy the cubes. He tore them apart and threw them around. He made a big mess.

Tom and Mia heard the noise and looked at the bench. They saw the dog destroying their cubes. They were shocked and sad. They ran to the bench and tried to stop the dog. But the dog was deaf. He could not hear them. He kept destroying their cubes.

Tom and Mia cried and shouted. They wanted their cubes back. They loved their cubes. They were angry at the dog. They wished they had watched their cubes.

A lady saw them and came to help. She was the owner of the dog. She apologized and said she did not know her dog was deaf. She said she would buy them new cubes. She said she was sorry.

Tom and Mia stopped crying and thanked the lady. They learned a lesson. They learned to take care of their things. They learned to be careful with their cubes. They learned to forgive the dog. They hugged each other and went home. They still liked to play with cubes.

One day, Sam and Lily go to the park. The park has many trees and flowers. It also has a pond. Lily sees ducks in the pond. She wants to chase them. She barks and runs to the water. Sam calls her name, but Lily does not listen. She jumps into the pond and splashes the ducks.

"Quack, quack, quack!" The ducks are angry. They flap their wings and peck at Lily. Lily is scared. She swims back to the shore. She is wet and cold. She shakes her fur and looks for Sam.

"Bad dog, Lily!" Sam says. He is not happy. He takes Lily to a bench. He dries her with a towel. He tells her not to chase ducks again. Lily feels sorry. She licks Sam's face and wags her tail. She wants to say sorry.

"It's okay, Lily. I still love you." Sam says. He smiles and hugs Lily. He puts a warm blanket around her. He tells her a story. Lily listens and snuggles with Sam. She is happy again. She watches Sam and thinks he is the best owner ever.

One day, their mom said they could have a treat if they were good. She gave them each a cookie and a glass of milk. Mia and Leo were happy and said thank you. They ate their cookies and drank their milk.

"Mine!" Mia shouted. "No, mine!" Leo shouted back. They started to tug and push each other. Mia got angry and pinched Leo's arm. Leo cried out and pinched her back.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "You are supposed to share and be nice to each other. You are not being good at all. No more treats for you today."

Their mom smiled and hugged them too. She said she forgave them, but they had to learn to be modest and not greedy. She said they could have the ball, but they had to take turns and play together. She said they could have another treat tomorrow if they were good.

Mia and Leo agreed and nodded. They thanked their mom and took the ball. They decided to roll it to each other and have fun. They were happy and good again.

Sam and Tom are squirrels. They like to find nuts and hide them for winter. One day, they see a big, shiny nut on the ground. It looks very smooth and tasty.

"Wow, look at that nut!" Sam says. "Let's go and get it!"

"Wait, Sam, it might be a trap!" Tom says. "We should test it first."

"How do we test it?" Sam asks.

Tom thinks for a moment. He sees a stick nearby. He picks it up and throws it at the nut. The stick bounces off the nut and makes a loud clang.

"See, Sam, that nut is not a real nut. It is a metal nut. It is hard and cold and yucky. Someone put it there to trick us. We should leave it alone."

But Sam does not listen to Tom. He is too curious and hungry. He runs to the nut and tries to bite it. His teeth hurt and he makes a loud squeak. The nut opens up and a big net falls on Sam. He is trapped and scared.

"Help, Tom, help!" Sam cries.

Tom runs to Sam and tries to free him. But the net is too strong and tight. He cannot lift it or bite it. He hears footsteps and sees a man coming. The man has a big bag and a smile. He picks up the net with Sam inside and puts it in his bag. He walks away with his prize.

"Bye, bye, little squirrel. You will make a nice pet for my son," the man says.

Tom watches the man go. He feels very sad and sorry. He wishes he could save Sam. He wishes Sam had listened to him. He learns a hard lesson. He goes back to his tree and cries.

Lulu couldn't believe her eyes - the brush was so sparkly and shiny, just like she'd always wanted. She was so excited to start brushing her hair, but she didn't know how.

So her mum explained, "Honey, you need to use the brush like this." She showed Lulu how to brush her hair.

But when Lulu touched the brush, she said, "Mum, this brush is fake, it doesn't feel right!"

Mum laughed and said, "Don't worry, sweetheart - this is a special brush and it has been made to look like it is made of plastic, but it is actually made of the softest material. That's why it doesn't feel like the other brushes," she said. 

Lulu said in surprise, "That's amazing! I love my new brush!" And she hugged her mum.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly farm. One day, a little girl named Kate decided to go to the farm. As she arrived, she saw a beautiful place. There were animals, flowers and tall trees.

"Wow!" said Kate.

Suddenly, an old farmer appeared. She had a big smile on her face.

"Hello! Welcome to my farm," said the farmer.

Kate was so excited. She ran around and petted all the animals. She also picked some flowers.

The farmer watched with a kindly smile. She was very happy to see Kate.

"You're so friendly," said the farmer. 

Kate smiled and thanked the farmer. Then she said goodbye and ran back home. She always thought of her friendly farm and the gentle old farmer.

Once upon a time there was a silly rabbit. He wanted something very badly and was feeling quite anxious. He was looking at the big round clock and noticed it was nearly noon. This made him very excited as he had an idea. He hopped over to the store and waited patiently for the door to open.

When it was noon the rabbit quickly hopped inside. He saw the thing he wanted and he smiled. The rabbit could not buy the thing he wanted, so he decided to steal it. He took the thing and raced out of the store.

The rabbit was very pleased with himself and ran home as fast as he could. He was so excited he showed the thing he had stolen to all his friends. Everyone was impressed and congratulated him on the steal.

The rabbit was very happy and kept the thing he had stolen forever. He was never anxious again.

When Pickles opened the journal, he saw lots of beautiful pictures and ideas. Suddenly, a friendly squirrel came hopping over and asked Pickles if he wanted to keep the journal. Pickles quickly said yes and thanked the friendly squirrel.

The friendly squirrel then gave Pickles some wise advice. He said, "Be sure to protect your journal. Carry it with you wherever you go and never let it out of your sight!" 

Pickles thanked the friendly squirrel again and said he'd be sure to protect his journal. He then hopped away with the journal tucked safely under his arm.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Tory. She wanted to go up high in an elevator. But when she stepped inside, it began to tremble. Tory was afraid, so she slowly pushed the buttons. Finally, the elevator's doors opened and Tory stepped out. 

The next day Tory wanted to go up high in the elevator again, but the same thing happened. This time the trembling was slower, but Tory was still scared. 

So Tory decided to ask her mom for help. Together they went to the front desk and asked if anything was wrong with the elevator. The clerk said that the elevator had been having some trouble, but it should be fixed soon. 

Tory stayed brave, and together with her mom she stepped inside the elevator. This time it didn't tremble and they went up high without any trouble. Tory was so happy she could go up high in an elevator again.

Little Frankie picked up the envelope and started to open it. But then, his mom caught up with him and stopped him from opening it.

"This is someone else's envelope," said Mom. "It would be thoughtful for us to give it to the park ranger so he can try to find out who it belongs to."

Little Frankie and his family walked over to the park ranger, who was delighted to find such a thoughtful surprise. He thanked them for their support and offered each of them a gumball in return.

Little Frankie was excited! As they walked away, he thought it would be even more fun if they one day got to open the envelope and see what was inside.

Anna and Ben nodded and took turns stirring the pot with a big spoon. They watched the berries change color and smell good. They were excited to taste the jam.

"Anna, Ben, where are you?" the cow toy mooed.

"Help, help, I'm stuck in the wheat!" the tractor toy vroomed.

But no one heard them. They were too small and too far away. They wished they had followed Anna and Ben to the kitchen. They wished they had not played in the wheat field. They wished they could grow big again. But it was too late. They were shrinking!

"That's a pity," the man said. "But maybe I can help you. Do you see this hook on my rod? I can use it to catch your hoop. Do you want me to try?"

"Yes, please, sir, that would be very nice of you," Ben said.

The nice lady took Lily to the ticket booth and asked if they could help her find her mommy and daddy. But they couldn't. Lily was so sad. She wanted to go home. She didn't want to be at the circus anymore. The nice lady tried to make her feel better, but Lily just wanted her mommy and daddy. 

In the end, the police came and found Lily's mommy and daddy. They were so happy to see her again. But Lily was still sad. She didn't want to go to the circus anymore. She just wanted to go home.

He tried to go for a bike ride, but he just couldn't go on. He was too sad. Suddenly, Joe spotted a bird flying in the sky. It made him smile. 

The bird was so happy and free. Joe wanted the same feeling. He spoke to the bird, "Hi bird! What is your name?"

The bird stopped and answered, "My name is Frisky. What is yours?"

Joe smiled and said, "My name is Joe. You're so lucky to be free! I wish I could be free like you."

Frisky lifted off the ground and said, "Everything starts with a single step. You can be free too! Take off your helmet and fly!"

Joe looked at Frisky and decided to take off his helmet. He lifted off the ground slowly and felt the wind whipping around him. He felt so free and happy. He had been so miserable before, but now he understood the feeling of freedom. Joe and Frisky flew around in the sky for hours and Joe was finally happy.

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Josh and Dan, who were always fighting and competing with each other. One day, their mom decided to take them to the park so they could play together. When they got there, they saw a big tall hill that they wanted to explore.

So Josh was the one who got the boot. The brothers tried to zip it open, but it wouldn't budge. No matter how hard they tried to open it, the boot wouldn't budge.

After a while, a wise old man appeared and said: "If you work together, you can open it up. You see, the boot is thick, so it needs two hands to open it." 

Josh and Dan raced to the other side of the tree, each grabbing one end of the boot. With their combined strength, they were able to zip up the boot. Inside they found a shiny gold coin. 

The brothers were so proud they had worked together that they hugged each other and ran back home. From that day on they never fought again.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Janey. She was only three and wanted to be successful. But she didn't know how to be successful. So, she asked her Mommy.

"Mommy," Janey asked, "how do I be successful?"

Mommy smiled and said, "You must work hard and never give up. That's how to be successful."

Janey thought hard and then demanded, "I want to be successful now."

Mommy sighed and said, "It's not that easy, Janey. Success takes lots of hard work and determination, even when things get tough."

Janey scowled. She didn't like the idea of having to work hard, but she was determined to get what she wanted. So, she asked, "Can I have some help?"

Mommy smiled again and said, "Yes, my smart girl. Let's get to work. We'll start by cleaning your room, it's looking filty."

Janey squealed with delight and quickly grabbed the cleaning supplies. After scrubbing, sweeping, and wiping, Janey's room was sparkling clean. She beamed with pride and said, "Look Mommy, I'm successful!"

Mommy laughed and said, "That's just the beginning, my dear. Now let's see what else you can do."

They watch the boat race. They cheer for their boat. The ducks watch too. They quack. Tom and Sam are happy. They are friends. They like to play with boats.

Lily did not want to play with Spot. She hissed and scratched at him, then ran away to hide under the bed. Spot was sad and confused. He did not understand why Lily did not like him. He followed her and tried to coax her out, but Lily only growled and spat at him.

Lily began to weep. She wept softly at first, then louder and louder. She wept until her eyes were red and her fur was wet. She wept until her owner heard her and came to see what was wrong. He lifted the bed and saw Lily curled up in a ball, shaking and sobbing.

"Oh, Lily, what's the matter?" he asked, gently stroking her head. "Why are you so unhappy?"

He carried her to the living room, where Spot was waiting. Spot wagged his tail and licked Lily's nose. He said, "Hi, cat! I'm sorry if I scared you. I didn't mean to. I just wanted to play with you. You're very pretty and soft and fluffy. Can we be friends?"

Spot nodded and barked. He said, "Yes, cat. I can do that. I'm happy to share with you. You're my new friend. And I love you."

Lily and Spot smiled at each other. They cuddled up on the couch, next to their owner. They felt happy and safe and loved. They had learned to accept and appreciate each other. They had become a family.
